## Researcher Response 55

**On an arbitrary ordinary 3-computad, a raw obstruction in degree six or above supported on at most two 3-rule uses requires a genuine 3-scalar.** In ordinary planar evaluation both 2-faces of that use have zero gates on an empty spatial path. There must also be a joint chart where the other use is a point marker in the same face and has a zero-gate side. In particular all ten individual ordinary surfaces reflect in these degrees at weight at most two if neither use is such a scalar. This improves the two-use case of [Response 54](#researcher-response-54), whose split-injectivity criterion can fail even for a proper death and a proper birth.

### Recovering the joint chart path

The additional case is a death consuming a nonempty closed diagram \(P\) with zero-gate output, and a birth with zero-gate input creating a nonempty closed diagram \(Q\). Both have empty spatial paths. There can be stationary wires, other gates, or nested components in the containing diagram. Name gates and uses by occurrence as in [Response 52](#researcher-response-52). First allow the two outside ends to vary. The refinement from a simultaneous chart to the **birth-first** serial coefficient is fully faithful as a map of groupoids.

Indeed take an arrow between the refinements of any two simultaneous charts. At their canonical serial representatives the seam paths are identities. The arrow is given by a path \(u\) in the chart with the birth marker and the gates of \(P\), and a path \(v\) in the chart with the death marker and the gates of \(Q\). Expanding the birth in \(u\) to \(Q\) and the death in \(v\) to \(P\) gives the same positioned braid between the fully expanded readings. This is precisely the seam compatibility since the ordinary diagram space is a 1-type. Restrict the common braid to the spectator gates and one specified gate of each of \(P,Q\). This gives a candidate joint path \(w\), including for arrows between different joint readings.

There is a positioned realization of this restriction. In \(u\), retain the birth marker and all spectator gates. Erase the internal wires of \(P\), retain its chosen gate as a point at its ambient object and erase its other gates. At the initial reading \(P\) occupies its own insertion disk with no exterior ports. Under each exchange its wire incidences persist, and spectator wires and gates remain outside the bounded faces of its connected components. Equivalently, project each horizontal slice onto the spectator wires in their order. The projected offset of a retained row counts exactly the retained wires to its left. An exchange of two retained rows still satisfies the same left-right disjointness inequality after projection. An exchange involving an erased row leaves the projected reading fixed. The new point occupies the gap of its floating component, at the ambient object after its internal wires are erased. At the two grouped endpoints this construction puts it at precisely the original death marker. Thus the projected switches give a path of joint charts with the required two endpoints. It is unnecessary for the separate components of \(P\) to remain together along \(u\).

To recover \(u\) from \(w\), keep every strand of \(P\) and just the chosen strand of \(Q\) in the common expanded braid. On the \(u\) side this recovers \(u\). On the \(v\) side it duplicates the death strand of \(w\) by the whole ordered packet \(P\), since deleting the extra \(Q\)-strands commutes with cabling the disjoint death strand. The other restriction recovers \(v\) by duplicating the birth strand by \(Q\). These are equalities of paths in the positioned groupoids by planar braid faithfulness. The same double restriction recovers any joint preimage, proving uniqueness. The argument allows compound ports with internal bounded faces and disconnected ports. Choosing names first also covers repeated generator colours. [Positioned braid faithfulness](../answered/semistrict-surface-conservativity-2026-11-24.md#researcher-response-79)

### Consequences at fixed ends

A fully faithful map of groupoids identifies its domain up to equivalence with a union of components of its codomain. This property persists under homotopy pullback, so one can prescribe both outside 2-ends, including their paths. With two named uses the schedule space is the homotopy pushout of the two serial coefficients along the joint coefficient. On the birth-first side the joint coefficient identifies exactly with its image components. The pushout is consequently equivalent to the death-first coefficient together with the disjoint birth-first components outside this image. Each is a 1-type. This argument does not assume that the map on the death-first side is injective, or that every birth-first chart admits a joint refinement. If the gate incidence forces a single order, its single serial coefficient already is a 1-type.

There is a degree-five conclusion on every component meeting the joint chart or containing a death-first history. Each such component is contractible at fixed ends. A loop at the death-first vertex is determined by its two site braids. Expansion of the first site to the prescribed initial diagram detects its entire braid by retaining one gate of \(P\). Expansion of the last site to the final diagram does so by retaining one gate of \(Q\). The end conditions force both braids to be trivial, independently of the seam path. The unmatched birth-first components have only the 1-type conclusion from this argument.

To deduce the weight bound, apply Response 54 whenever its criterion holds. In every remaining two-use chart there is an order with empty output on the first marker and empty input on the second. If neither marker is a genuine 3-scalar, their opposite ports are both nonempty, exactly the case just proved. The named coverings detect the higher difference spheres as in Response 54. The conclusion concerns existence of raw fillers, so it gives reflection for each of the ten individual surfaces in those degrees. Two genuine free 3-scalars in a common face do give the raw two-point configuration sphere of Response 54. Whether an individual surface fills a particular obstructed raw boundary is a further question.

## Researcher Response 58

**One free 3-scalar beside an arbitrarily long gate-dependent chain of point sites has at most one potential 2-cell relation in its probe fibre. Even when both ends are empty, a nontrivial attaching word which is not a proper power suffices. A full twist at a seam can change the answer while fixing all the incidence names and written ports.

### Sweeping the probe through the chain

Forget the distinguished scalar use. The fixed-end coefficient of the remaining chain is a 1-type by Response 52. Over a chosen point of this base the schedules for the probe are its serial placements in the gaps of the chain and its ties with a single site. They form a subdivided interval, since no two chain sites can tie. At a gap the fibre coefficient is the space of positions of a probe point in the corresponding planar diagram. At a tie it is the space of such positions with the other site marked. Its two maps are the point-position maps under input and output insertion. Indeed in the gap the unmarked interface path factors at the extra probe-only batch. After forgetting its point the space of intermediate objects and path factorizations of this fixed path is contractible. At an outer gap use the prescribed end path in the same way. This identifies the forgetful fibres at all vertices and ties, compatibly with refinement and transport along the given seams. Taking their homotopy colimit computes the fibre, as homotopy colimits of spaces over a groupoid are fibrewise. The long exact homotopy sequence now identifies every based homotopy group in degrees at least two of the total space with that of the corresponding fibre component. This last step allows loops in the forgotten chain. [Single-site point-position maps](#researcher-response-56)

Sweep from the initial gap to the final one. At each gap take one punctured plane per face bearing the probe's object. At a site, all joint faces except its containing face map equivalently to their corresponding outside faces on both sides. In the containing face the maps fix the other hole meridians and send the site meridian to the product about the outermost children of the inserted port. Bounded faces internal to an input port finish at that gap; those internal to an output port start there. A seam transports the faces and their based meridian frames by its actual path. In particular distinct continuing faces never merge.

If the output port is nonempty and the site face admits the probe, the map from that joint face to the new exterior face is inclusion of a free factor up to homotopy. One may use the product of the new child meridians in place of the first new meridian in a free basis, retaining the other new meridians and all the spectators. Thus the next step wedges on one circle for each new exterior child beyond the first, irrespective of the map to the accumulated old space. On the other continuing faces it does nothing up to equivalence; newly available bounded faces enter as separate graphs. This also proves the graph conclusion when the site's object excludes the probe. Each nonfinal output is nonempty by gate dependence, so until a possible empty final output all accumulated components are graphs. If the first input is nonempty the reverse sweep has nonempty ports in its sweep direction throughout, proving the same conclusion even for an empty final output.

At a final empty output the map from the joint exterior face to the last gap fills just its site puncture. Its mapping cylinder relative to the joint face therefore attaches one disk along the site meridian, up to homotopy. When this face admits the probe, let \(W\) be the image of the *input* packet's peripheral word in the accumulated free group. The resulting component is a rose with a single disk attached along \(W\). Other components remain graphs. If \(W=1\), this gives a wedge with a 2-sphere and hence raw degree-six obstructions. For a nontrivial cyclically reduced word that is not a proper power, Lyndon asphericity gives the vanishing of every higher homotopy group. The word test is exact for this presentation complex. If a nontrivial proper power occurs, the maximal root has finite order greater than one in the one-relator group, which precludes a finite-dimensional aspherical complex (restrict the cellular resolution to that finite cyclic subgroup). A simply connected 2-complex with zero second homotopy is contractible by cellular homology and Hurewicz, so failure of asphericity here already gives second homotopy. This criterion does not require a realizability assertion about proper powers. [Louder and Wilton, §5.2, on Lyndon asphericity](https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/10131842/1/Louder_Negative%20immersions%20for%20one-relator%20groups_AAM.pdf) · [Karrass, Magnus and Solitar on the order of a relator root](https://doi.org/10.1002/cpa.3160130107)

### The word at a written seam

In the positive access comb of Response 56, let \((a_1,\ldots,a_m)\) be the input child meridians expressed in the accumulated group. A nonempty output of size \(n\) introduces \(n-1\) new free generators and determines its first meridian by \(b_n\cdots b_1=a_m\cdots a_1\). Spectators keep their words. A positive adjacent seam crossing changes the ordered pair \((x,y)\) to \((x^{-1}yx,x)\); the negative crossing uses the inverse change. This is pullback of a loop at the *next* reading along the seam. It follows by conjugating the probe's two actual meridians with the adjacent half twist and preserves the reversed peripheral product. At the split the new branch meridians are \(b^{-1},b\), and the stationary meridian is \(a\). With straight seams the final word is empty and the exterior fibre is a two-circle rose wedged with a sphere. A full twist of the separate point about the stationary lens at the second seam gives \(b^{-1}a^{-1}ba\). The exterior fibre then has the torus presentation and is aspherical. All four resulting diagrams admit the middle cut. At the history selecting the first source occurrence and then the second, the pushout diagram is isomorphic over the input to the literal occurrence diagram of the raw two-step witness.

For an unbounded example use the two rules \(p:B_L\to B_R;B_R\) and \(q:B_R;B_R\to B_L\). Both declaration source maps cover every vertex of their diagrams. From this source the quotient search has three states: the initial one, the one with the expansion, and the one with both changes. In each state the three edges form the same line. The left two-edge gate, right two-edge gate when present, and middle unary gate all cross its middle cut. More explicitly each entrance for an available rule must place its full three-edge path on that line, fixing the placement of every gate. After the first expansion both ports of the expansion and contraction are present; identifying equal labelled attachments leaves at most one copy of each rule. This accounts for all five transitions, including repeats. It proves reflection for **every written parallel target** from this source. Weight two on each left birth or death, one on each right birth or death, and one on each middle birth or death is positive and conserved. Thus the individual old queries from this source are decidable in the four effective settings. The argument uses only the unary gate at its actual middle position, although the input loop permits that gate on any of the three edges.

In the expansion/contraction example it exhausts the state graph and verifies that exactly two of its states admit a parallel raw lift of the target \(M;(B_R;B_R)\). ### Puncturing the one-probe comparison

Choose a point of the unmarked chain base. Draw the original and fully flattened histories of [Response 61](#researcher-response-61) in the same rectangle, with the same changing disks, gate positions and seam motions. At regular times the flat obstacles are the gate points; the planar obstacles additionally include the wires. At a site the disk replaces its contents in both pictures. This realizes the raw comparison on each occupied component as an orientation-preserving open inclusion \(C\hookrightarrow V\) of the one-probe 3-manifolds, where \(V\) is its flat component. The comparison on configurations uses that same inclusion in every coordinate. At a gap it forgets the wires and at a tie it uses the common outside of the disk, exactly as on the positioned charts. For point-site chains, [Response 59](#researcher-response-59) gives this one-probe inclusion a homotopy left inverse at the fixed history. We need a separate argument to pass to configurations: a homotopy left inverse on points need not preserve distinctness.

Let \(C\hookrightarrow V\) be an orientation-preserving open inclusion of connected open 3-manifolds with a homotopy left inverse. For any finite \(Q\subset C\), the inclusion \(C-Q\to V-Q\) is injective on all positive homotopy groups. Removing points leaves fundamental groups unchanged by general position. In the universal covers the induced map identifies distinct lifts of a given puncture with distinct lifts in the target, by fundamental-group injectivity. Locally around each such puncture it is an oriented homeomorphism onto a neighborhood. Here are the details for higher homotopy.

A simply connected open orientable 3-manifold \(X\) has the homotopy type of a wedge of 2-spheres. Its homology above degree two vanishes. Its second homology is free abelian: by ordinary Poincaré duality this is \(H_c^1(X;\mathbb Z)\). Exhaust by connected compact submanifolds with finite boundary and fill the relatively compact complementary components. The exact sequence of each pair, using \(H^1(X)=0\), computes the direct limit as the locally constant integer functions on the finite sets of complementary components modulo constants. As the exhaustion increases every old unbounded component has a descendant. Pullback along these refinements splits, with free cokernel (choose one descendant per old component). The union is therefore free. Represent a basis by based spheres using Hurewicz; the map from their CW wedge is a homology equivalence between simply connected spaces of CW type, hence an equivalence. This reasoning applies also after puncturing a universal cover at a closed locally finite set of points, which preserves simple connectivity by general position.

For the punctured cover, excision gives the short exact sequence on second homology with kernel freely generated by the small meridian spheres at **all individual puncture lifts** and quotient \(H_2(X)\). This uses \(H_3(X)=0\) and ordinary finite chains. In the source-to-target comparison the map on these kernels has a left inverse by the distinct-lift and orientation observations. The map on quotients has a left inverse from the lift of the unpunctured homotopy retraction (choose compatible basepoints). Since the quotient groups are free, splitting both short exact sequences gives a block triangular map with split-injective diagonal blocks. Subtract its off-diagonal block using those left inverses to get a left inverse on the whole \(H_2\). For the two wedges of 2-spheres this homomorphism can be realized by a based map, by Hurewicz on each summand; its composite is homotopic to the identity on the source wedge. This proves the punctured-cover comparison, including its effect on torsion in higher homotopy.

Forget the last of \(m\) ordered points. The configuration fibration has fibre the manifold minus the other \(m-1\) positions and has a section: place the extra point sufficiently far out a fixed proper ray, continuously beyond a proper exhaustion bound for the existing points. One may choose the exhaustion increasing along a terminal part of the ray or a continuous majorant for its last exit times. The homotopy sequence therefore makes the fibre groups injective; a change from the section basepoint to the desired basepoint only transports the sequence. Compare the fibrations for \(C\) and \(V\). Induction on \(m\), using the punctured-cover result on the fibre and injectivity on the base, proves injectivity on \(\pi_j\) for every \(j\ge1\). The sections need not commute with the inclusion. For several occupied planar components, forget all names except those in one component at a time. This detects each factor even when the different components map to the very same \(V\). [Fadell and Neuwirth, *Configuration spaces*](https://www.mscand.dk/article/download/10517/8538)

The two unmarked chain bases are still 1-types and their map is injective on fundamental groups by Response 52. The same exact-sequence argument as in Response 59 now gives positive-degree injectivity on the **total** based history spaces. A flat raw filler therefore gives a raw filler at the original boundary in degree five or above. The scalar-rule theorem of Response 48 supplies the flat filling from any filling for the two published surfaces or the four binary surfaces omitting interchange. This proves the six unrestricted probe-count assertions. Nothing in the proof applies a pointwise retraction to a tuple that might acquire a collision.

### How many probes a difference sphere needs

For a connected open orientable 3-manifold \(C\) as above, all coordinate projections onto at most \(k\) of the original named points jointly detect \(\pi_k\operatorname{Conf}_m(C)\) for \(k\ge1\). In degree one, paths and homotopies of paths in the product can avoid the pair diagonals by general position in codimension three. For \(k\ge2\), induct using the same forgetful fibration. If projection to the base vanishes the class lies in the injected fibre group. In its universal cover choose the sphere basis for the unpunctured manifold and move its representatives off the discrete puncture set by general position. With one small sphere per lift of a puncture, these form a wedge basis of the punctured cover by the excision calculation. Forgetting punctures pinches exactly their meridian spheres. The old representatives persist even when the unpunctured manifold itself carries nonzero second homotopy.

Take a finite subwedge supporting this class. In Hilton's decomposition in degree \(k\) only basic products of length at most \(k-1\) can contribute, since a product of length \(d\) has sphere dimension \(d+1\). Keep the puncture names of one nonzero summand, together with the moving point. At most \(k\) original names suffice; old ambient spheres cost no puncture names. The retained wedge still detects the summand, by pinching to its letters, and the projected configuration fibration injects the resulting fibre class. This proves the bound, including classes with zero total linking. Applied to the fibre in Response 61 it holds for arbitrary spatial ports. For \(k=1\) on total spaces one also retains the unmarked chain projection; for \(k\ge2\) its base has vanishing higher homotopy. [Hilton, Theorem A](https://ncatlab.org/nlab/files/Hilton55.pdf)

For an individual surface flatten the old query first. Lift a putative flat surface witness and its boundary with the scalar wire and event names fixed at the common source, as in Responses 44, 48 and 52. In degree five this forces the two paths to have the same transported names at their common end; above it the named coverings preserve higher homotopy. Keep the whole chain and any selected probe names, specializing other probe uses to the identity at their empty ports with the point-only fits. This is a surface substitution on the named scalar-rule presentation. Reflection at the resulting tests with at most \(k=n-4\) probes, including the unmarked test, forces the full flat difference class to vanish by the preceding projection bound. Total-space injectivity then gives the original raw filler. Conversely the bounded scalar-rule tests are themselves members of the class. **Reproduce.** Run `python3 tools/semistrict_surface_collision_sheets.py --agda-dir DIR` and `agda --safe --no-libraries -i src -i DIR DIR/CollisionSheets.agda`. It separates the resulting puncture lifts in an explicit finite permutation cover. For two different compound ports it recovers 106 signed coefficients from 318 summands each, in covers of 79 and 105 sheets. A difference of two collision meridians with access paths differing by a commutator has zero ordinary total linking but yields coefficients \(+1,-1\) on sheets 0 and 10 of an 11-sheet cover. ### The trace at a gap

On the supporting edge path mark positions by cumulative weight. An actual gap at a horizontal slice thus has an integer coordinate \(j\), between zero and the full width inclusive. Every gate has a well-defined support interval in these coordinates and its two ends are the same on both sides of the gate. Say that a gate or site crosses \(j\) when \(j\) is strictly interior to its interval. In a 2-diagram read just the crossing gates in drawing-height order. An exchange of disjoint positioned rows preserves this list since two disjoint blocks cannot both cross \(j\).

In the plane with coordinates drawing height and history time construct a progressive diagram \(K_j\). Its strands are the occurrences on these lists transported through the history. A chain use crossing \(j\) gives a vertex whose incoming and outgoing lists are exactly the crossing gates in its input and output ports, including the empty list at either end. A use outside the cut leaves the list unchanged. The affected sublist is consecutive: the whole port is inserted at the single row of the site. A crossing vertex is present even when both sublists are empty. The diagram may have several floating components and they can enclose each other. At time zero or one a strand meeting the boundary is anchored. For a probe at a written slice use its actual wire gap to compute \(j\), then locate it in the face of \(K_j\) at that time by counting the crossing rows below it.

Every accessible face \(F\) of \(K_j\) gives exactly one probe component, with the homotopy geometry of \(F\times\mathbb R\), naturally also for configurations of distinct probes. Here is a way to see the width and accessibility assertions simultaneously. Draw an edge of weight \(d\) as a thick band of \(d\) parallel lanes, filling the internal gaps of that band. Between successive lane blocks keep a narrow open interval for each actual wire gap. At a gate use a transverse bar joining the incident lanes, covering all gaps strictly inside its interval; the lateral gaps continue. Rectangular collars of a gate with its incident strips are regular neighborhoods of its planar star, with the same boundary ports. Replacing the star by this drawing gives the same open-face configuration spaces and the same inclusions outside the change disks, as in [Response 61](#researcher-response-61). Use the common band positions on both sides of a change. In its time collar the bars of its crossing input rows end at the site and those of its output rows begin there. Equivalently use a small disk about this vertex in the height-time diagram, straightening the incident strands to its rim. At an exchange the order of crossing rows does not change; their heights move by an isotopy. In the narrow interval for coordinate \(j\), the barriers are precisely the strands and vertices of \(K_j\), times the transverse interval. An intrawire gap in an undivided band is filled. Its availability can change only across a bar or a change straddling \(j\), so it is constant on each open face of \(K_j\). This proves the product description on accessible faces; it avoids counting gaps internal to a weight-two edge as probe positions. Different accessible faces have separate position components. The planar face is a disk with one hole per directly enclosed floating component, so a single probe there has zero higher homotopy.

The complexity statement concerns recognition by this sufficient condition for reflection; it does not classify conservativity itself.

### Two certificates for reflection at a written query

Write \(D_e\) for the literal occurrence diagram, with its universal term and map to the given computad \(X\). Fix an old 4-type with faces \(s,t\). Start at \(D_s\) and repeatedly attach \(D_g\) along **any** match of \(D_{s g}\) for a 4-generator \(g\), as in Response 62. Here every finite sequence is admitted, without a count bound or any intermediate quotient. Keep the distinguished lift of \(s\). Call a stage terminal if it carries a lift of the written \(t\) literally parallel to that lift. The test asks whether every terminal stage has a nondecreasing two-colouring on vertices with every generator of degree two through four crossing from left to right. A positive answer proves reflection: a surface witness has such a terminal development at its lifted old boundary, so the cut theorem gives a raw filler there, which folds. [Cut reflection](#researcher-response-49) · [Construction from the source of a witness](#researcher-response-62)

A certificate is a computad \(Y\to X\) with a lift of \(s\) such that every generator-preserving map \(D_{s g}\to Y\) over \(X\) extends over \(D_g\). It suffices to give its skeleton through degree three and require that every matching written source has a parallel matching written target. Adjoin copies of the corresponding 4-generators at those pairs. There are two ways to finish the certificate:

1. Give a cut on \(Y\), requiring crossing object poles for each matched 4-source as well. This certifies reflection for **every parallel old target** from \(s\).
2. Require that no lift of \(t\) in \(Y\) is literally parallel to the marked lift. This certifies emptiness in both theories at that query.

These two alternatives, allowing infinite \(Y\), are jointly **equivalent** to the test. Every finite development maps to a certificate extending its seed, by successive pushouts. For the converse, form a countable chain of finite developments by fairly extending all matches: enumerate those at each finite stage and dovetail the resulting requests, transporting each match to the current stage. Its colimit \(C\) has the extension property. A match into the colimit involves finitely many generators and finitely many literal type equalities, hence factors at some common stage; any eventual equalities of names hold at a finite stage. The same argument lifts a terminal match back to a finite stage, including the parallelism equations at the distinguished lift. If no terminal match appears, \(C\) gives the second alternative. Otherwise all sufficiently late stages are terminal. If the test holds, each has a cut. Pullback of a cut along the maps of stages is a cut, including when vertices become identified. Compatible cuts on the whole chain exist by the finitely branching tree lemma, applied to finite compatible strings of choices, of which there are arbitrarily long ones. They give a cut on \(C\) and the first alternative. A negative answer has a finite witness, enumerable by enumerating raw matches, pushouts and terminal lifts and testing the finite graph. This characterizes the test also when different occurrences of one generator have the same lifted source and different lifted targets.

The following translation gives a finite certificate whenever the condition below holds. It also specifies how to check the condition directly on the occurrence diagrams. In a computad model one can use its generator names as tokens, and store for each generator its entire canonical tuple of tokens. We describe a family of finite raw computads. On one object use loops for letters, with nonempty words given fixed raw bracketings. The graph of the forward rule diagram consists exactly of the path for \(u\) and a fresh path for \(v\) between its ends. The death has the identical gate and is glued along it. No interior vertex of \(v\) is glued to \(u\). All higher generators have the two exterior poles. Thus a forward attachment adds the alternate path at any match of \(u\); a reverse attachment adds no edge or vertex and identifies none of the old ones. In particular pairing these 4-rules does **not** reverse the word rewrite. The reverse source already contains the whole pair of paths.

Start at \(s=1_{1_w}\). Before a special attachment, colour every path by putting stationary tape edges on the appropriate side of its state and making every state edge cross. This starts on \(w\). In one direction, a word step adds the required alternate subpath and preserves the rest of the route. For the converse the graph stays acyclic, each fresh path being inserted parallel to a nonempty old path, and every vertex stays on a route between the initial exterior poles. Every occurrence of an edge of the newest alternate path in a full route traverses that entire fresh path, as its interior vertices were fresh. Replacing that segment by the matched \(u\) gives a route in the preceding graph. Induction shows that the word of every exterior route is reachable by forward rewrites. A matched \(Hk\) extends to such a route, which proves the converse. The reverse special rule cannot be the first special attachment because its source uses the fresh special birth and death.

Take a fixed universal Turing machine, encode a configuration by its tape word with endmarkers and a single state at the scanned letter, and simulate its local steps by nonempty word rules. A right move replaces the state and scanned letter with the written letter and new state before the next scanned letter; a left move also matches the immediately preceding letter. Include the endmarker cases inserting a blank when necessary. Use a fresh halting rule replacing the halt state by \(Hk\). These rules preserve the one-state condition and make the distinguished pair reachable exactly on halting inputs. With \(t=s\) every development is terminal already. The preceding equivalence and finite enumeration of bad developments prove \(\Pi^0_1\)-completeness of this occurrence cut test even with the finite computad fixed and only the input word varied. The query \(s\to s\) itself always has its raw identity. This distinguishes precisely the complexity proved here from the complexity question about conservativity in Q2. [Configuration-word simulation, §23.5](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~ear/cs341/automatabook/AutomataTheoryBook.pdf)

There is a small explicit instance where the positive result needs an infinite-vertex certificate. Use the five word rules
\[
 S\rightsquigarrow aSb,\qquad S\rightsquigarrow T,\qquad
 aTb\rightsquigarrow T,\qquad aTr\rightsquigarrow Hk,\qquad lTb\rightsquigarrow Hk.
\]
Use the special rule above and the initial word \(lSr\). The reachable words are \(la^i S b^i r\) and \(la^i T b^i r\), \(i\ge0\). Thus every query from \(1_{1_{lSr}}\) to a parallel old target reflects by the cut argument. Suppose one cut certificate extending all matched sources had finitely many vertices. Between its fixed exterior poles it must have a path for \(la^i S b^i r\) for every \(i\), by iterating the expansion at the state edge. Choose \(i\) greater than the number of vertices. Along its \(a\)-segment two vertices coincide, so skipping the intervening loop gives a path for \(la^j S b^i r\) with \(j<i\). Extension at \(S\) supplies a \(T\)-edge there. Apply \(aTb\rightsquigarrow T\) exactly \(j\) times. The resulting path contains \(lTb\), which supplies \(Hk\) and forces the incompatible cut. This rules out even a certificate having infinitely many parallel generators on finitely many vertices. For target \(s\) the target-exclusion alternative is impossible too. The infinite certificate is supplied by the chain construction; every particular witness uses a finite cut diagram.

**Validation.** The checker evaluates the relation conjunctions and independently enumerates maps of raw computads. It checks both extension directions in the guarded example, a boundary equality identifying the two endpoints of a lifted edge, and target exclusion at a scalar seed admitting no cut. Six literal round trips grow from four vertices to ten. For each of the five word rules it unfolds the actual 4-declaration and checks its two labelled paths, including the absence of extra edges or vertices; five nested pushes yield exactly six balanced exterior words. Agda checks the guarded round trip, its literal fold from the occurrence diagram, and the expansion followed by its reverse in the balanced-word presentation. The general decision and hardness proofs are above. Run `python3 tools/semistrict_surface_guarded_occurrences.py --agda-dir DIR` and `agda --safe --no-libraries -i src -i DIR DIR/GuardedOccurrences.agda`. ## Researcher Response 66

**Gate dependence in Response 64 can be dropped.** On finite ordinary 3-computads with positive conserved wire weights and strictly positive 2-gate widths, degree-wise reflection for each individual surface is equivalent to its conjunction on two subclasses: the same weighted presentations without scalar 3-generators, and the single no-2-generator test computad of [Response 23](#researcher-response-23). In particular one may use the previously established raw asphericity tests on the unmarked component alone, without testing whether a probe forms a simultaneous triple with two of its sites.

### Forgetting probes over a changing schedule

Under the weight hypotheses every change on an empty spatial path is a free scalar occurrence in planar evaluation. Its attaching terms are point-only fits: an ordinary 2-gate cannot act on a path of zero weight. There is a literal substitution retaining the lower computad and the non-scalar rules, sending the scalar declarations to point-only comparisons. In realization it forgets their marked uses. Denote the resulting space of fixed-end unmarked histories by \(B\), which need not be a 1-type. Use individual occurrence names at the chosen boundary. Since all the ordinary gates and non-scalar markers have positive input, each component of an unmarked lower chart is contractible: its planar components are input-anchored and the positioned pure braid group has no floating factor. The unmarked coefficient at any ordered partition is thus homotopy discrete, including its paths between successive expanded batches. Its points can be represented by marked batch drawings with the prescribed seam and end paths.

Here is the homotopy fibre of the forgetful map over any such point. Use the space \(M\) of Response 61 with **one disjoint changing disk for each site of a tied batch**. Two simultaneous sites can use the same wires at different drawing heights; disjointness concerns their small disks in the planar drawing. The fibre is the ordered configuration space of the named probes in the components of \(M\) having their object labels. In particular the identification is compatible with splitting the batch, with the actual seam transports, and with forgetting probe names.

For details, project the ordered partitions of all names to those of the non-scalar names. First take the homotopy left Kan extension of the marked coefficient diagram along this projection. At an unmarked schedule \(u\), one can use just the marked schedules projecting *exactly* to \(u\). Indeed in the comma category a marked schedule projecting to a coarser one has a contractible poset of further refinements projecting exactly to \(u\). Within each old tier place its ordered subtiers of unmarked sites at prescribed distinct times and let all its probe times vary in the intervening open time interval. The weak-order cells, allowing any ties, have exactly this refinement poset, and their order complex is contractible by the convex time region. A tier with only probes has its original tier as a minimum among refinements. Take the product over tiers. This proves finality for the Kan extension before imposing any geometric coefficient restrictions. [The corresponding shuffle calculation](#researcher-response-50)

Over a chosen unmarked drawing the exact-fibre calculation is now the one in Response 61 with several disks at a critical time. Subdividing an unmarked path in a regular gap at probe batches has contractible space of choices. At a critical time tied probes avoid all the disjoint disks, with planar points distinct within their equal-time blocks. Order the times and subdivide the allowed position cells as in that response. The resulting homotopy colimit is the configuration space in this particular \(M\).

It remains to check that these objectwise fibres are still the fibres after forming the unmarked homotopy colimit. For a refinement choose a collar about each split tier, disjoint from the other time collars. In its planar drawing take disjoint slightly larger neighborhoods of the site disks. On the annuli between them, the external wire arcs are constant in time, using radial collars. Move the change times to the prescribed suborder by a time shift supported in these neighborhoods. Explicitly in each smaller disk use an increasing piecewise linear reparametrization of the collar time, fixed at its ends; interpolate it to the identity across the annulus. At each fixed planar position the interpolation is still strictly increasing. Scaling the shifts from zero to their chosen sizes gives an ambient isotopy. This identifies the complements and the ordered configurations throughout the refinement.

To see that this checks the Kan transition itself, include the shift parameter as a base edge. At its initial endpoint the unmarked tier is tied; elsewhere take its ordered subtiers with separations proportional to the parameter. Subdivide by the probe time orders relative to these times, allowing equality with each other and with the subtiers. At the initial endpoint the faces are the exact marked lifts of the tied schedule. At positive parameter they are the exact lifts of the refined schedule. Specializing a positive face to parameter zero coalesces the subtiers and permits precisely the corresponding marked coarsenings: inside a coalescing tier any prescribed refined probe times can be realized by scaling their offsets too. Subdividing the position coordinates compatibly with the port drawings and their disks now gives the same flag diagram over this edge as in the Kan construction. Its generization maps relax collisions or insert the appropriate ports. This is the mapping-cylinder comparison for the two exact subdiagrams, including the refinements inside each end. On the configuration-space side the isotopy trivializes the family over the edge, so these transitions on fibres are equivalences. A different reading or seam representative transports configurations by the corresponding planar motion. Consequently all squares over unmarked refinements are homotopy cartesian. The homotopy-colimit fibre lemma identifies the computed fibres with the actual homotopy fibres over \(B\). This is a local assertion and allows monodromy around an unmarked loop. ## Researcher Response 68

**There is a finite one-object computad and a written 4-type empty in every theory in Q1, including the ordinary join, that has an inhabitant under every interpretation in a model with finitely many 1-cells.** More generally, for the family below, raw and surface inhabitation are both exactly acceptance by a word-rewriting system. A countermodel finite through its nonidentity cells exists **if and only if** a regular language containing the input is closed under forward rewriting and avoids acceptance. The same criterion characterizes countermodels with finitely many 1-cells and unrestricted higher cells. This concerns actual inhabitants at the given boundary. It holds for every admissible \(E\) under both rules, as well as the Gray and ordinary theories. For ordinary CaTT and its strict-sound surfaces there is such a family in every output degree at least four.

### A word step acts on a specified old boundary

Use tape letters and disjoint state letters, all loops at one object. A configuration \(l q r\) has one state.  W_w=P(q),\qquad K_w=P(1_q),\qquad A_w=P(Z_q),\qquad E_w=P(1_{1_q}).
\]

### A strict countermodel from a language invariant

Let \(J\) be any forward-closed set of configurations avoiding \(H\). Choose a monoid \(M\) of tape grades, generated by the image of the tape alphabet, such that membership of \(lqr\) in \(J\) depends only on \(([l],q,[r])\). The free tape monoid always works. For regular \(J\) use the transition monoid of the tape letters in an automaton recognizing \(J\); reading the state letter between the two tape transitions determines membership. Write \(J(m,q,n)\) for this predicate on grades.

Construct a one-object strict 4-category by describing its hom as a strict monoidal 3-category. Its objects (global 1-cells) come in three parts:

- Zero state letters gives the discrete 3-category on \(M\).
- One state letter gives objects \((m,q,n)\). Between each ordered pair put one local arrow. Its local 2-endomorphisms are the subsets of \(M\times M\); both compositions of these 2-cells take union, with the empty set as identity. Between two parallel such cells put one local 3-cell exactly for inclusion in the forward direction.
- Two or more state letters gives a terminal 3-category.

There are no higher cells between the three parts. The monoidal product on objects adds the numbers of states truncated at two, multiplies two zero-state grades, and acts on a one-state triple by multiplying its exterior grades. On the subset \(D\) at a one-state arrow the simultaneous left and right actions of \(a,b\in M\) are
\[
                       (a\cdot D\cdot b)(c,d)
                         \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad D(ca,bd).
\]
Products reaching the terminal part are unique. Associativity of multiplication gives the two commuting exterior actions in their indicated orders. Inverse image preserves union, the empty set and inclusion. Within the one-state part, union is associative, commutative and unital and the top homs are thin. These facts verify strict functoriality, units and interchange at every cut. Use only identities above global degree four. If \(M\) is finite there are finitely many nonidentity cells in total.

Send the tape and state generators to their grades and state triples, with \(q\) going to \((1,q,1)\). The local arrows for \(c,d\) are forced. The birth and death are parallel local 2-cells with the required local-arrow faces, and can each take the empty set. Assign \(Z_q\) the set of \((c,d)\) for which \(J(c,q,d)\) holds. The mark on a configuration now tests membership in \(J\) at every further exterior pair, while its empty reading has value the empty set. The advance generator is well typed by forward closure at all those pairs. Every pair of grades has tape representatives, so this is precisely the ordinary closure under placement of a word rule. The closing generator compares empty sets, and the accepting mark is empty at all exterior grades. This interprets the computad. If \(w\in J\), the interpreted mark contains \((1,1)\), excluding a 4-cell to the empty reading. Every surface under consideration is sound in ordinary strict categories, including insertion and the join. In particular taking \(J\) to be the set of configurations with **no** route to acceptance proves that both the raw and the surface answer to \(Q(w)\) are exactly reachability of \(H\).

Conversely, interpret the raw computad in *any* model of one of these theories and let \(J\) be the set of words at which the interpreted query has empty fibre. The conditional raw judgement proves forward closure, and the accepting generator excludes \(H\) from \(J\). If the model has finitely many 1-cells, \(J\) is regular. A finite automaton can accumulate the interpretation of each tape segment by the chosen left fold, retaining the left value and state while it reads the right segment. At the end these three finite data specify both interpreted faces since their constructors were fixed above. The finite table of their fibre emptiness gives the accepting table of an automaton; there is no computability assumption on the higher cells of the model. This proves both converses in the finite-countermodel criterion. In fact finiteness of the set of tape-term values at the chosen object suffices.

### One old query and the recognition complexity

Take the word rules
\[

### A cut for each marked occurrence

Choose marked generating edges of an ordinary computad $X$, with a label $c$ on each. Call the other edges passive. For each label choose two sets $L_c,R_c$ of passive edges. Require that both strict edge words of each declaration $g$ of degree at least two have the form $a e b$, with $e$ marked, $a$ a path in $L_c$, and $b$ a path in $R_c$. The mark must have the same label $c$ on both faces. Its edge, its object poles and the two passive paths can all change. The attaching terms themselves may be weak composites.

Between successive marks of labels $c,d$ on a path, read the passive word $h$. Call the path **protected** when each such gap satisfies
\[
              R_c\cap L_d=\varnothing
              \quad\text{or}\quad h\notin R_c^*L_d^* .
\]
In particular every one-mark path is protected. Every path is protected if all right alphabets are disjoint from all left alphabets. More generally the all-path hypothesis is decidable on the finite graph: for each pair of marked edges with intersecting alphabets test for a connecting passive path in $R_c^* L_d^*$. This is reachability in two copies of the graph, with a transition from the first to the second at each vertex. Include the empty connecting path and allow the two occurrences to use the same generating edge.

Grade paths by a category with the vertices of $X$ as objects. Use the passive arrows and formal arrows $c_{x,y}:x\to y$ for every label and ordered vertex pair. Impose $l c_{x,y}=c_{x',y}$ for $l:x'\to x$ in $L_c$, and $c_{x,y}r=c_{x,y'}$ for $r:y\to y'$ in $R_c$. A marked edge maps to the formal arrow with its label and poles. All generating 2-relations respect this grading. Orient the two relations towards absorption of a passive letter. Forgetting vertex tags gives a terminating confluent word reduction: disjoint moves commute, either order in $l c r$ gives $c$, and either absorption of the middle letter in $c p d$ gives $cd$. Thus the ordered labels and each remaining passive word are invariants of the grade. The residual word in a gap is empty exactly when $h\in R_c^*L_d^*$. At a protected grade the overlap $c p d$ with $p\in R_c\cap L_d$ cannot occur in any representative, even one reached by expanding letters. The other overlaps commute with their vertex tags. Termination and local confluence on this class give a unique **typed** normal form. Every factor of a protected grade is protected, since adjoining words at the ends leaves all gaps internal to that factor unaffected.

Take the factorization interval $X_w$ of Response 32 at a protected grade $w$. Its endpoints are the frames $(1,w)$ and $(w,1)$. The piece for $c_{x,y}$ is as follows.

- Its left vertices are $L_c$-paths $a:x\to z$. Its right vertices are $R_c$-paths $b:t\to y$. These are disjoint copies, even for $x=y$. The two empty paths are the entry and exit.
- A left edge appends a passive letter and a right edge consumes the first passive letter. A marked generating edge $e:z\to t$ of label $c$ gives an edge from $a$ to $b$ for each such pair. A higher declaration $g$ of label $c$ with object poles $z,t$ occurs with those same indices. Its boundaries are its written boundaries placed at that frame. In particular a crossing edge in a pole $A e B$ uses the indices $aA,Bb$.

Here is the verification at *all* interval frames. Expand the factors of a factorization into words and put a cut between them. At a gap with nonempty residue there is a unique maximal absorbable right run before the residue and left run after it. At a gap with empty residue the split $R_c^* L_d^*$ is unique by disjointness. The outermost runs have just one possible absorbing mark. Inside a left run the part already read is a passive suffix of the **prefix** factor, and the unread part is absorbed by the mark in the suffix factor. Inside a right run the unread part survives as the passive prefix of the **suffix** factor. In a residual word the frame retains its two literal fragments. These are exactly the vertex addresses above: the number of marks read locates the occurrence, and the typed normal forms of both factors retain its indicated path, including its endpoints. At the split of two runs both are absorbed on their respective sides, giving the common joint. Conversely each address specifies both factors by writing the completed portion of the normal form, the retained path and the remaining portion, using the marked arrows with the prescribed poles. The formal arrows for all vertex pairs ensure this also indexes vertices whose passive path has no actual crossing continuation. Placing one generator at a frame now gives exactly the listed edges and higher declarations. The recursive placement of its attaching terms remains in this piece, by the same calculation applied at its own single-mark grade. This proves the interval description. The overlap exclusion matters: if $p:0\to1$ belongs to both alphabets, absorbing $p$ on opposite sides in $c_{0,0} p d_{1,1}$ gives two different seam vertices in irreducible typed words.

### Raw homs and the surface calculation

Let $B_c(x,y)$ be the ordinary computad with an object $[a,e,b]$ for each crossing edge of the piece and a generator $[a,g,b]$ of degree $\dim(g)-1$ for each higher copy. Project its actual attaching type by the indexed cut of round-1 Response 14. The two passive graphs here are trees: the path from the entry to a left vertex and the path from a right vertex to the exit are unique. Thus the indexing paths in that cut are exactly $a,b$. For instance a crossing column preceded by the stationary path $A$ and followed by $B$ sends its crossing labels to the indices $aA,Bb$. This prescription applies recursively to the actual heads in its faces. The raw entry-to-exit hom maps by a weak equivalence to the free ordinary realization of $B_c(x,y)$. [Indexed cut and fixed-hom equivalence](../answered/semistrict-surface-conservativity-2026-11-24.md#researcher-response-14)

For clarity, the raw hom across the whole interval maps by a weak equivalence to the **cartesian product** of these free ordinary realizations. To verify the product step in the ordinary enriched realization, glue two successive parts $D,E$ at the sink $z$ of $D$ and source $z$ of $E$. These are cellular pushouts along an object. There are no backwards homs across it. A mixed hom from $u$ to $v$ is the free composite of $D(u,z)$ and $E(z,v)$ over the joint endohom. Indeed composites entering the second part have a single passage through the joint. The mixed hom carries the left and right actions by the two parts, and its defining composition balances the two actions at $z$. In the enriched pushout the universal such bimodule is given by their relative tensor: maps out are balanced pairings, since all actions before or after the passage compose within one part. The derived balancing uses the two-sided bar with terms $D(u,z)\times \mathrm{End}(z)^k\times E(z,v)$. The endohom is equivalent to the unit: any path at the joint in its own part is confined to that vertex, where only the free point acts. Thus this bar is equivalent to the constant product. Pure homs within either part acquire no new passages back into that part. Iteration gives the assertion, with a terminal factor for each passive edge. To identify the actual projections, clamp all pieces other than the selected one to its nearest endpoint. This can be done by a raw substitution, choosing fillers recursively for the resulting parallel faces on a point. It is the identity on the selected piece. In the balanced pairing this evaluates the other factors in the terminal hom and composes by units. Composing the clamp with the indexed cut therefore realizes the corresponding product projection. This last identification lets us use the product equivalence on prescribed raw faces. [Ordinary enriched path products](../answered/semistrict-surface-conservativity-2026-11-24.md#researcher-response-12) · [Raw realization of hom attachments](../answered/semistrict-surface-conservativity-2026-11-24.md#researcher-response-6)

For an old query inhabited on a surface, first place the derivation at its canonical frame by Response 32. Clamp and project to each marked occurrence. For insertion the projected equations are insertion equations. For the full binary surface the indexed cut also uses unary disc removal; its addition preserves old inhabitation in each dimension. For their join $J$ the projected derivation is itself a $J$-derivation. In detail the substitution on a labelled spine is the same for both sets of rules. Stationary labels evaluate to paths. The binary generator calculation uses the lower word and disc equations, and the insertion calculation uses lower insertion, including disc and endo removal. In a mixed derivation the arguments and boundary equalities of a last rule have already been projected by induction; its generic calculation takes place in this same lower algebra. Ordinary strict evaluation checks the bound arity condition there.

One ingredient of the root insertion calculation merits checking for mixed typings: disc trivialization still holds over $J$. Induct on output degree and then on the structure of the term on a disc. Normalize its maximal arguments by this induction to the variables or identity towers specified by their strict disc values. The faces fix the other entries up to conversion. Prune an identity at a maximal position whenever its head is not itself the identity being computed. Each pruning reduces the number of positions and retains the surviving labels up to conversion; newly exposed faces are already classified by the lower-degree induction. The identity head itself acts by identity on its classified argument. With only variable maximal arguments left, a labelling by disc variables is a subdisc inclusion: a branch would require two consecutive composable disc variables at its branching level. On that subdisc the generic head faces have smaller degree and trivialize by induction. Thus disc removal in the degree of its top variable, or endo removal above that degree, computes the indicated strict value. This argument uses pruning and congruence in $J$ on the actual generic type, without assuming a mixed term has a pure insertion typing. It supplies the disc calculation of round-1 Response 12 for the last-rule induction. If each projected old query has a raw filler, their tuple gives existence at the projected faces, and local essential surjectivity of the raw hom equivalence at the specified iterated boundary gives a raw filler upstairs. Refold it into $X$. The graph-only case contributes a discrete path hom. Degree-zero and degree-one existence just asks for a vertex or a path. [Two-sided placement](#researcher-response-32) · [Rule projection](../answered/semistrict-surface-conservativity-2026-11-24.md#researcher-response-12) · [Disc removal for binary surfaces](../answered/semistrict-surface-conservativity-2026-11-24.md#researcher-response-15)

Conversely, a failure on a $B_c(x,y)$ gives a failure one degree higher in $X$. Use the single protected grade $c_{x,y}$. As in the necessity direction of the indexed cut, represent a homotopy inverse of the raw projection by an ordinary map from the free cofibrant lower computad into the fibrant entry-to-exit hom. Suspend the failed surface derivation and substitute its raw generator images there. Each word generator and each insertion generator suspends to the same rule in the hom, so this also works in the join. A raw filler at the resulting old boundary would give existence at the lower boundary by reflection along that weak equivalence. Folding to $X$ preserves this obstruction because any proposed raw filler there lifts back at the canonical frame. An empty indexed computad contributes no failure. Consequently, when all paths are protected, for insertion, for the full binary surface, and for $J$, the first global failure is exactly one more than the least first failure among the $B_c(x,y)$, taking $1+\infty=\infty$. The single-grade direction needs no hypothesis on any other grade. [Suspension and necessity at an indexed hom](../answered/semistrict-surface-conservativity-2026-11-24.md#researcher-response-14)

### Dimensions, recognition and persistence

In a 3-computad the indexed computads have dimension at most two. The separate ordinary surfaces reflect in every such computad by the dimension-two theorem, using finite dependency-closed subcomputads for a finite derivation. The full binary result gives all its subsurfaces; strict units follow from insertion. For $J$, Response 1 gives the exact criterion on each indexed computad: no positive positioned 2-history from the empty path at an object back to that same empty path. For an infinite indexed computad, a positive history still has a finite spelling, and the count-and-permutation obstruction to a raw filler interprets *all* its 2-generators. Conversely every finite dependency-closed subcomputad of a bubble-free one is bubble-free and the lower reflection proof applies there. A positive history gives the lower failure at degree four and no lower failure is possible below four. The shift proves the degree-five claim. Enumerating indexed generators by the lengths of their passive paths and dovetailing over finite positioned histories semidecides failure. Hardness already holds on bipointed suspensions of finite ordinary 2-computads: mark every edge with the same label and take both alphabets empty. The indexed computad at the suspension poles is the original one. [Individual surfaces in dimension two](../answered/semistrict-surface-conservativity-2026-11-24.md#researcher-response-10) · [Joined criterion and hardness](#researcher-response-1)

A bad indexed history in the 3-skeleton also precludes all-dimensional reflection for $J$ in **every finite higher extension**, even one that violates the marking condition. Choose its object $[a,e,b]$ and an actual bracketed raw path $p$ for $a e b$. The cut of $1_p$ is a raw identity on that object (or a structural representative of the empty path). Fit the ends of the positive planar history to this literal lower 1-cell by raw path comparisons. The resulting lower 2-cell has positive generating 2-count. Local essential surjectivity for the raw hom equivalence at $1_p,1_p$ produces a raw 3-cell between those literal identities whose projection is equivalent to the lower 2-cell. Strict evaluation in the free strict 2-category preserves this count across equivalence: every 3-cell there is an identity. The raw 3-cell must use a generating 3-declaration, since the cut of any expression in the 2-skeleton uses only the 1-skeleton of the indexed computad in its strict value. Folding preserves the occurrence. This gives exactly the positive raw bubble to which Response 4 applies in the extended context. [Persistence under finite higher extension](#researcher-response-4)

For Q3(b,c), in arbitrary finite rank assume each generating 3-cell has at least one generating 2-event in its ordinary strict 2-source. Then each local 2-generator has a nonempty input word: every such event crosses the mark and projects to one indexed generating edge. The dual hypothesis on all targets works as well; the orientation can be chosen separately in each indexed computad. Response 36 now gives the individual lower results through degree five, and the cut gives reflection at every protected query through degree six. The unrestricted questions still include contexts where a higher rule changes several marked occurrences at once, as well as the directed kernels of Q1(a). [One-sided dimension-five theorem](#researcher-response-36)

For a one-object example take passive loops $l,r$, a marked loop $f$ with wings $\{l\},\{r\}$, and rules $\alpha:lf\to fr$, $\beta:fr\to lf$. Put $t=\alpha;\beta$ and add a 3-cell $t\to t;t$. Every indexed 2-rule consumes a nonempty word, so all indexed computads are bubble-free and the join reflects. On $(lf)^n$ the same generating rules can act in all $n$ blocks. Adjoining $1_{lf}\to t$ and $t\to1_{lf}$ gives a positive bubble at the indexed object $[l,f,1]$ and the first joined failure moves to degree five.

**Validation.** Run `python3 tools/semistrict_surface_marked_blocks.py --agda-dir DIR` with an existing directory, then `agda --safe --no-libraries -i src -i DIR DIR/MarkedBlocks.agda`. Across words through length six the checker compares the frame and the independently read block address in both directions at 66,073 positions on 4,392 protected grades. A two-object test checks unique typed normal forms on 2,511 paths and realizes the two seam choices in the overlapping example. Positioned rule moves give exactly the cube edges for one through seven copies of $lf$. Agda checks the projected bubble at its specified identity faces, the projected positive-input rule, and actual raw spatial composites of the bubble on up to three consecutive interval pieces. ## Researcher Response 72

**All ten ordinary surfaces reflect in every degree for mixtures of nonempty closed point-site rules and the following rules on spatial wires.** At each wired site require the condition below on **each** written 2-port, with at least one spatial wire at the rim of its disk. The two ports may have different internal graphs. This includes repeated many-to-many changes between branched diagrams on the same wires; no private gate colours or separation of the different rules' supports is required. Every old boundary in degree five and above on such a 3-computad fills raw. Adding arbitrary independent free 3-scalars preserves all-degree reflection for the two published surfaces and the four binary surfaces omitting interchange. For any of the four containing interchange, in degree \(n\ge5\) the class with probes reduces to scalar rules with both ports nonempty together with at most \(n-4\) occurrences of free probes.

For a wired port, all its spatial boundary wires must meet one connected component of its gates and wires, called its core; in particular no wire passes unchanged through the disk. The other components, if any, must be in **bounded internal faces** of this core, allowing further nesting. Require two terminal gates \(a,b\) on the core. Every boundary input ends at \(a\), every boundary output starts at \(b\), and every core gate is on a directed path from \(a\) to \(b\). Paths of length zero are allowed, as are \(a=b\) and an empty list of inputs or outputs. Use the nonempty closed-port condition of [Response 70](#researcher-response-70) at point sites. These are finite tests on positioned diagrams; they also apply to a supported computation using just such ports. The conclusion through \(h+1\) with further arbitrary declarations first in degree \(h\ge4\) holds for the probe-free global condition.

### Simultaneous contraction on the spatial wires

Use the named cubical complex and full-incidence-path cover of Response 70. The cover kills the cut and cube groups for the same reason as before: flattening reads the positioned gate braid, each site expands to a nonempty list of gates, and every named gate is on a full path of 3-event incidences. The extra issue is the corner link: recognizing the same gates after flattening is insufficient evidence that they can be contracted on the actual wires.

At a cut, transport all specified edge germs to one ordinary drawing. A wired port exposes its particular core gates and everything inside the port's bounded internal faces. From just after its first gate until its last, the running core wires are a nonempty interval if one includes its enclosed contents between the extreme core wires. To see why an exterior row cannot lie strictly inside this span, take a point between two such wires in a horizontal slice. Through each wire choose a directed path from the first to the last gate. The path up one and back down the other has winding number of absolute value one about that point, by crossing the horizontal ray at that slice. Thus it is separated from the rim by the core. Wires or gates in the intervening regions belong to the port, including components wholly enclosed there. No exterior wire can enter or leave a core gate mid-block. The same argument applies in any other reading of the given corner, since incidence and the face addresses of its floating components transport with the drawing.

Consequently one can gather the port at its first row using legal planar switches: bring each later port row leftwards in the temporal reading past the intervening exterior rows, in port order. The exterior rows operate on the left or right of the running block, with the offset changed by the ordinary switch rule. This works across forks and joins, even when several interior rows can exchange with each other. The grouped block contracts to its site with the specified rim wires. For several pairwise square-compatible directions, their gate sets are disjoint. Grouping and contracting one wired block leaves each of the other wired cores and its enclosed contents intact. In particular it cannot put an exterior gate in one of their internal faces. Closed point ports are whole sibling subtrees, with their contents; pairwise compatibility precludes a second port inside any selected subtree. One may contract all wired blocks, then group the point ports in their respective remaining parent faces. The simultaneous chart component is unique: the ordered rim attachments and ports fix the replacement vertices on the anchored or floating core, and the spectator face addresses and the collapsed point markers determine the remaining planar component. This constructs the common downstairs cube; directions inducing different transports to it still have to pass the lifted test.

For a wired block choose its first core gate as braid representative. In the product description of a named planar loop by its sibling braids, contraction preserves the motion of the core to which the marker belongs. Its outer face sectors and the corresponding sibling lists are unaltered: in the disk the connected core meets all the rim legs, so each outside sector persists, and the extra complementary faces are internal. The factors for motions confined inside the contracted block are forgotten. More explicitly, in the flattened gate braid retain every spectator strand and one strand of the wired core. An exterior sibling motion acts on this representative exactly as on the corresponding marker, by unframed cabling of its containing component. Sibling motions in surviving faces give the same positioned factors after contraction. Every internal factor loses all its moving strands. These are all generators of the named planar loop group by the sibling braid calculation. Hence restriction gives an actual loop class of the collapsed chart; expanding the marker again gives its retraction on the corner group. On ambient braids this endomorphism cables the representative by the port size and erases the rest of that port. This reasoning covers an anchored block (whose core itself contributes no floating motion) and a block lying on a floating spectator lens. [Named positioned loop groups](../answered/semistrict-surface-conservativity-2026-11-24.md#researcher-response-164)

The endomorphisms commute for disjoint ports and their product retracts to the simultaneously inserted chart. The coset argument of Response 70 therefore makes the lifted links flag. Its CAT(0) interval argument gives homotopy-discrete fixed-end arrow spaces, proving the probe-free assertions at the written boundaries.

### Comparing a probe during a change of its enclosing wire diagram

For the probe argument alone the two terminal gates are **unnecessary**. Suppose at every nonpoint site that each port has a connected gate core meeting all its boundary wires, with any further components only in bounded internal faces of the core and no through wire. Here the argument concerns the probe fibre over one chosen unmarked history, so it does not require simultaneous contraction of several wired blocks.

In the site disk a connected core meeting all rim legs has exactly one complementary sector at each open rim interval, prior to any identifications outside the disk. Distinct intervals are separated by paths in the core joining boundary points; equivalently, first take an embedded spanning tree containing all the boundary legs, then add its remaining edges. No enclosed decoration changes the outer sectors. Replacing the marker star by this port thus preserves the equivalence relation on the continuing faces outside the disk. Every other port face is internal and starts or ends on that side. For a given face through regular cuts the life interval calculation of Response 59 still applies.

To give the one-probe inclusion into the flat spacetime a left inverse on a selected component, keep one gate **incident to the selected face** on each directly enclosed child core. If its life has an internal endpoint also keep a gate incident to the face on its outer boundary and compactify the target plane to a sphere as in Response 59. Such a face is bounded away from the exterior of the drawing: at the internal endpoint it lies inside the changing disk and the continuing sector bijections preserve contact with the fixed exterior. Its outer boundary belongs to one connected wire-and-gate core, which can be anchored. Begin with any such choices at the first available cut and transport them across seams.

At a wired change, representatives outside the disk persist. If a chosen boundary gate in the disk changes while the face continues, retain the marker at the tie, then choose a gate on the new core incident to that same rim sector. For a surviving sector the only core inside the disk available to carry such a representative is the core meeting the rim. Its enclosed decorations are invisible from that sector. A continuing child cannot be born in such a sector, since all the other port components are in internal faces. These restrictions intertwine the punctured-plane or punctured-sphere comparisons with port expansion up to isotopy inside the disk. At point sites use the old rule: a site in the face substitutes the list of representatives of its outermost children; replacement of the whole enclosing component ends the life of a face inside it.

At an internal endpoint all of the selected children and the outer boundary representative lie in the **one** changed port; this is why adjacency to the moving face was required of the outer representative. The flat site meridian around the entire list is null in the punctured sphere by the peripheral relation, and all spectator meridians map trivially. This extends the projection constantly over the unavailable side. On available gaps and ties the composite from the chosen original face is an equivalence, since one puncture lies in each complementary hole and the added outer puncture, when used, lies outside its outer boundary. Taking the interval homotopy colimit supplies the one-probe left inverse. Compatible choices of homotopies of the edge maps suffice on this subdivided interval.

The comparison of spacetime complements is the orientation-preserving open inclusion obtained by erasing wires and keeping gate points and the same critical disks. [Response 63](#researcher-response-63) lifts the injection to configurations of any number of probes, testing one component and at most \(n-4\) names at a time. Erase the probes to test the original base class, then apply these flat tests to a fibre preimage as in that response. This proves the stated joint detection. For the two-terminal subclass the unmarked groups already vanish. Its flattenings have nonempty input and output on every structural use, and the six-surface scalar-rule theorem applies. ### The angle contribution at a rim sector

A progressive planar graph has a cyclic order and a linear list of inputs and outputs at each gate. Give the angle between consecutive darts label zero when one is incoming and one outgoing. At a source or sink label the angle around the outside of its ordered list \(+1\); all other same-direction angles have label \(-1\). Count angle *occurrences*, including both visits to a bridge. An upward plane embedding of a connected graph has angle sum \(-2\) on each internal face walk and \(+2\) on its outer walk. Conversely a plane graph with these face sums, the stated vertex counts, and the compatible edge directions admits an upward drawing with those lists. One can use the characterization for undirected plane maps with a consistent splitting: the angle data recovers the splitting starting from an exterior source, up to simultaneous reversal. The given directions are such a splitting. In particular one need not assume separately that a quotient graph obtained by the contractions is acyclic. One can subdivide edges to apply the criterion with no parallel edges; the new one-in/one-out vertices contribute zero on each side. A self-loop may likewise be subdivided into a cycle of length three before applying the criterion. [Didimo and Pizzonia, Lemma 1 and Theorem 1](https://jgaa.info/index.php/jgaa/article/download/paper68/2902/2709)

Temporarily set the floating components of a port aside. Draw the remaining connected core between two fans with bottom and top poles, one ray for each actual boundary wire in order. Each open rim interval of the port meets one local exterior sector of the core and distinct intervals meet distinct sectors: a spanning tree reaching all rim legs already separates them in the disk. Extra core edges bound internal faces. In both framed drawings the sector gives an internal face, and the contributions at its fan poles agree dart for dart. Thus the contribution from the core along the sector walk equals that of the marker angle there. This also covers a source, a sink and a single rim leg, where a face walk may turn back along the same edge. The two side edges separate the framed unbounded face from the port. At a port with rims only at one end the single sector extending around the other end meets both side edges and is counted only once.

In an ambient component several such sectors may be in the same face. Their contributions then add, with multiplicity. Replacing any number of disjoint connected cores by their stars therefore preserves the angle sums on **every surviving face**. Each internal core face disappears with that core. The combinatorial embedding has a disk for this replacement: thicken the core with its named rim legs and fill its bounded internal faces, cutting the legs at short transverse arcs. For a genuine germ there is no spectator inside those filled faces. The resulting disks for disjoint cores can be chosen disjoint unless one lies inside a filled face of another. A pair admitting a joint square excludes that possibility. This step uses connectivity inside the disk before adding its boundary.
