## Researcher Response 107

**The number of generators needed by the probe-complement groups of an ordinary history has a bound computed directly from its written ports.** In Response 103's universal presentation at empty written 2-ends it is at most the smaller of the two counts of oppositely directed two-wire exceptions. This bound is sharp at every integer, on a single temporary lens. If either direction is absent, designated independent free probes add no degree-five surface test; in higher degrees they add at most the pure tests of Response 80. If either direction occurs just once, an integer winding decides every named one-probe fibre loop. These assertions concern the additional probe test at a fixed supporting history; the unmarked query can still have its own obstruction.

### A generator count for arbitrary ports

Count connected components of the spatial wire-and-gate graph of a port \(D\) before attaching its rim to any surrounding graph. Include each untouched through-wire as a component. Put \(d(D)=\max(0,\#\pi_0 D-1)\). Choose a serial reading of the structural history, with actual signed seams, and a regular gap \(j\). Let \(h_j\) count all floating connected components at this cut, including nested ones. For the spacetime regions \(C\) of the one-probe complement there is a bound on the **sum** of the minimal generator numbers:
\[
  \sum_C \operatorname{rank}_{\rm gen}\pi_1(C)
   \ \le\ h_j+\sum_{i<j}d(\mathrm{input}_i)+\sum_{i\ge j}d(\mathrm{output}_i).
\]
Events and regular gaps use zero-based indices. Any gap of any legitimate serial refinement gives a bound. In particular a scan for the best gap in a given movie takes only the port costs, the cut counts and prefix sums.

The cut alone is a disjoint union of planar surfaces, whose fundamental groups have one generator for each directly enclosed floating component. Their total rank is \(h_j\). Grow the spacetime away from this cut, first along one time direction, then along the other. At a site attach its tie-to-new-cut mapping cylinder along the existing side by the other tie map. Outside the site disk the tie and new cut agree. By van Kampen for groupoids, it suffices to add to the tie enough paths to generate the groupoid on the new local side, allowing a basepoint in each new component. Joining two previously disconnected components by one such path costs no loop generator; adding it within a connected component costs at most one. Relations can only lower the count. Thus the argument does not assume injectivity into the already constructed complement. Ordinary seams induce equivalences. [Cut, tie and seam model](#researcher-response-69) · [Finite groupoid presentation](#researcher-response-84)

For a port with \(N>0\) incident rim legs, the marker star has \(N\) exterior sectors. Suppose \(c\) components of the port meet its rim. Exactly \(1+N-c\) local faces meet the rim: take one tree on the rim legs within each such component. A tree with \(k\) legs cuts its containing disk region into \(k\) rim regions. Adding further edges creates bounded internal faces; it does not change the rim partition. Equivalently this follows by adjoining the rim circle and using the planar Euler formula. Inside each exterior face join the former sectors by a tree of paths. This uses a total of \(c-1\) paths. Take a basepoint in every new internal face, and add the meridians of the floating children of **all** faces, interior and exterior. Each floating component contributes once. These paths generate the local groupoids relative to the individual rim sectors, since each face is a planar disk with those holes. They remain sufficient when several local sectors have the same ambient address. The total cost is exactly \(d(D)\).

At a point site the tie is locally an annulus. For a nonempty closed port let \(e\) be its number of outermost floating components. The tie meridian reads the ordered product of their meridians, up to compatible choices of stems. With this product one needs only \(e-1\) of their generators. The remaining generators are one per direct child in the internal faces, so the same cost \(d(D)\) works. For a blank point port the new disk kills the meridian and costs zero. This proves the formula in both time directions. It also explains why a blank two-wire side costs one although it has no gates.

A bound of zero makes all the regions simply connected. Response 80 then reduces each individual surface with free probes to the unmarked history and its pure point tests, or just the unmarked query for all ten in degree five and the six indicated surfaces in higher degrees. With a bound of one, at most one region can have a nontrivial group, and that group is infinite cyclic. Indeed its first integral homology is torsion-free by Alexander duality for the tame complement in the three-sphere: the relevant cohomology group is in degree one. A cyclic group equals its abelianization. Hence for a signed loop in the finite spine, compute its pairing with a primitive generator of integral first cohomology (zero if the group vanishes). This signed integer, up to change of orientation, detects raw nullity exactly, including words with nonzero even winding. For several named probes the degree-five fibre group is the product of the single-coordinate groups by general position away from pair diagonals in three dimensions. The occurrence-named section includes these groups in the actual raw total. [Spine presentation](#researcher-response-84) · [Section at transient components](#researcher-response-79)

### Sharpness in the fixed ordinary presentation

Every port in the universal presentation has cost zero except the bare two-wire side of the exceptional pair. The two extreme gaps at empty ends give the minimum-of-direction-counts bound. To attain \(r\), open a floating interval, expand its start by the leaf rule, and expand its unary gate to a split followed by a merge. Within this lens use the two-wire creation and immediate consumption \(r\) times, then close the lens and the interval. The lens spacetime has disk slices throughout each regular and tie face. Each connector separates its middle wire gap into two faces for one interval of time; the two branches rejoin after the connector disappears. Between successive connectors the lens again has one face. Its graph of spaces with disk coefficients therefore retracts to a graph of rank \(r\). One may carry a separate outer floating interval through a signed exchange without altering this component. The lower and upper bound now agree, and the lens group is the free group of rank \(r\), even though the written outer ends are empty.

This also exhibits actual degree-five raw differences in the universal presentation with no added probe generator. In the lens use a further disjoint floating interval born and consumed there with no internal updates. Over the fixed parent its marked planar position is a single particle: select the start gate, or its point marker at a cap. Each cut/tie sibling braid is read by this representative and the two expansions select one or zero points as prescribed. Contract its free-ended trajectory to its birth as in Responses 91 and 106, in the open complement of this parent. This identifies the named total component with the corresponding free-probe component over the parent; the parent itself may have two-wire events. The section of Response 79 therefore still includes the whole free group. A nullhomotopy in the folded presentation would lift from the chosen event names. In particular **one use of each two-wire direction suffices for a nonzero named raw degree-five difference** at empty ends, and its winding is invisible after replacing the parent by any finite selection of spacetime event points, whose complement is simply connected. **For each of the four named kernels, the two raw rules agree on degree-five inhabitation in all finite contexts if and only if they agree on one fixed globular 3-computad with four declarations.** For the tree test of Response 105 it suffices to use trees of dimension at most three. This holds both for agreement of raw inhabitation and for preservation of the specified strict value at all common old types on arbitrary finite computads. There is also a local version for Q1(a). Fix a finite globular 3-skeleton \(B\), and allow arbitrary full-rule raw attaching terms in higher dimensions. If the two raw rules agree at every common old fifth-degree type on \(B\) itself, they agree through five on every such extension, and every full-support interchange-free binary surface is conservative through five on every extension. In particular this conservativity holds whenever no two generating 2-cells of \(B\) can occur on successive spatial intervals. The last condition permits arbitrary 4- and 5-declarations outside those intervals.

In the first version the hypothesis is equivalent to agreement of the two raw rules on old fifth-degree inhabitation on \(B\). The converse will follow by taking the extension to be \(B\). For the identity-value version we use the hypothesis **on the positions**, before folding. ### Separating the generating 4-cells

On a pasting tree \(P\) consider a strict 4-expression. Expand structural products by their Godement formula and distribute fixed actions over chronological composition. A placed generating 4-cell is recorded by its name and its fixed left and right lower pads at each cut. Use the structural normal records, with the lower cuts nearest the name, multiplying pads by the lower actions when a new exterior is distributed. The pad fields take values in the strict skeleton through degree three. Separate the chronological word at every such placed generating 4-cell, retaining the intervening paths of native operations, including empty paths with their objects.

If two strict expressions are equal, they have identical separator records in the same order and the corresponding intervening paths are equal as strict 4-values. To check this, use the support-free presentation of the four pasting tables. Each proper rank-four nonstructural equation has top letters formed from lower inputs. This covers the prism subdivisions and varying whiskers, triple crossing, binary join factorization, restricted inner subdivisions and the enabled unrestricted subdivisions. None has a formal input 4-globe as a top letter on either side. Unit specializations of these heads also have only lower inputs. A substitution in their operands still uses data through degree three. A fixed action on such a path distributes to a path with the same property, and a chronological context changes a contiguous interval within one gap. For an empty interval the identity records its actual object. Structural distribution, units and associativity preserve the records by their construction. A change of lower spelling in a pad preserves its lower value. The guarded completion has the presented low-rank tables on trees by (K58). This verifies the assertion along the entire equality derivation, even if a native join occurs midway in a derivation between two realizable paths. ### Returning to the old type

Translate a variable-rule raw 5-derivation at a common old type in \(X\). Through rank four use the exact translation of Response 105, which commutes literally with substitution. For a 5-head translate its two generic 4-faces and its tuple. If the full test succeeds, apply the resulting full head to the translated tuple. Otherwise the original head is a variable-only coherence. Its two translated raw 4-faces are equal in the strict table on the bound tree. Their evaluations at the translated tuple have equal normalized arrows by the separation just proved. Inverse transport gives the required full-rule witness at the literal substituted faces, of identity value in the specified-value version. This last step takes place in \(X\). A 5-variable uses its declaration, and any 5-label in a tuple is treated at the literal type determined by the translated prefix. Such a label's own value is never read in computing a 4-face. Thus mere inhabitation also transfers when some 5-witnesses have unspecified value. Since the full rule embeds in the variable rule and Response 102 reflects variable-rule interchange-free surface inhabitants in \(X\), reflection for the full surface follows. In the specified-value version the entire transfer preserves the value.

If the test on trees of dimension at most three holds globally, apply this result with \(X=P\), \(B=P_{\le3}\), for every tree \(P\). Response 105 then translates rank five on **arbitrary** finite computads, including those with nonglobular lower attachments. Conversely, agreement on all computads entails the test on the low trees themselves. This proves the claimed equivalence in both versions.

 T_3=(x:\star,\ e:x\to x,\ a:e\Rightarrow e,\ f:a\to_3 a).
\]

This last formulation keeps the distinction between equality on positions and equality of the evaluated labels.

The fixed context also gives an explicit separation for the additional admissible profile of Response 85. ## Researcher Response 109

**For every \(n\ge1\), one computable translation sends each old degree-\(n\) inhabitation query on a finite globular set to a single old query on a fixed globular context \(U_n\) with \(n+2\) declarations.** It preserves and reflects raw inhabitation and, independently, inhabitation with each binary surface of Response 5. It works for every admissible \(E\) and both coherence rules. In particular the all-dimensional pasting-context problem in Q3(a) is equivalent to conservativity in degree \(n\) on \(U_n\) for every \(n\). The reduction also preserves individual negative answers. It requires no oracle for the equations or reachability of \(E\) on promised well-formed input types.

For \(n\ge2\) take one object and one generator in each positive degree through \(n-2\), each an endomorphism of the preceding generator. Add two distinct parallel \((n-1)\)-generators \(l,r\), both endomorphisms of the last lower generator, and one \(n\)-generator \(z:l\to r\). For \(n=1\) take two vertices \(l,r\) and the edge \(z:l\to r\). In the free **ordinary strict** category on \(U_n\) there is at most one \(n\)-cell at any prescribed parallel faces. In fact an ordinary \(n\)-cell over globular generators gives a common lower positional paste together with a chronological string of generating \(n\)-changes at each \((n-1)\)-slot. The only nonempty string in \(U_n\) is the single change \(z\). Its ends distinguish it from either empty string. At an iterated identity on a paste below degree \(n-1\) there is no top slot to change. [Positional description and the finite tree reduction](#a-finite-search-for-fixed-faces-on-globular-generators)

Let the input be the old type \(u\to v\) on a finite globular set \(Z\). Compare the ordinary positional shapes of its faces. They must match with the same labels below their top slots. For \(n=1\) use one vertex slot. At each corresponding slot with distinct \((n-1)\)-labels \(b,c\), test whether the directed graph of generating \(n\)-cells in \(Z\) contains a path from \(b\) to \(c\). If either the positional test or a path test fails, output the old type \(r\to l\) on \(U_n\). Ordinary strict soundness excludes a filler on both sides for every indicated language. Otherwise form one tree \(K\) from the common shape. At a slot with equal labels retain the single stationary position; at a slot with distinct labels insert exactly one \(n\)-globe between its two versions. These operations respect the lower incidences since all versions of a slot are parallel. Lift the original raw faces to their respective signed sections using the original labels there. The two lifts have the same literal lower boundary by the uniqueness part of positional lifting. Write them as \(\widetilde u,\widetilde v\) in \(K\). The sections suffice for this operation even when \(Z\) has no single generator implementing one of the required changes.

There is a globular labelling \(k:K\to U_n\). Use the unique lower labels, label every changed slot by \(z\) and every stationary top slot by \(l\). The different top strings are at distinct positions over the common lower skeleton, so these choices agree on their intersections. Output \(k\widetilde u\to k\widetilde v\), using ordinary relabelling of raw syntax. All these operations on a given writing are effective. In particular its ordinary pasting value and the raw lifts at its sections are computed by splitting the ordinary paste along the supplied head application and recursing on the tuple. Every admitted head has full ordinary positional support in both rule forms. This computation uses the given derivation and reads no new directed-kernel head tests. [Raw and surface positional lifting](#lifting-syntax-at-the-positions-of-an-ordinary-strict-cell)

**Preservation.** Take any witness on \(Z\) in the indicated language and lift it to the tree \(P\) of positions of its ordinary value. Its signed faces are the lifted old faces, literally for raw syntax and as surface classes for surface syntax. Make a raw substitution sending variables of \(P\) to terms over \(K\). Fix the common lower positions. At a slot with equal original end labels send *all* intermediate versions to its stationary position and all changes to identities. At a slot with different end labels its string is nonempty. Send the first change to the retained top globe and all later changes to identities on its target. The old initial version goes to the new initial version and all later versions go to the new final version. The substitution is typed at each declaration since the versions have common lower faces. On either signed section it is exactly the identification of corresponding positions used to lift the old writing there. Internal versions need not have their original labels after contraction. Substituting and then labelling by \(k\) therefore gives a witness at the output type. In the surface case syntactic substitution respects the generating equations at these signed faces. In particular a nonempty return to an equal label cannot force the use of a top change in the output.

**Reflection.** A witness on \(U_n\) at the output type has a forced ordinary value. At each changed slot it uses \(z\) exactly once, at each stationary slot it uses no top generator, and all positions below are fixed by the two faces. Hence this value is the image of the total of \(K\) elevated to rank \(n\). Lift the witness along \(k\) at that total. Its signed faces agree with the prescribed \(\widetilde u,\widetilde v\) by positional uniqueness, using the surface pullback for the surface assertion. Now substitute from \(K\) into \(Z\). Give each changed slot the chronologically composed raw string along any path found by the finite graph test, and give each other position its original label. A nonempty path is composed along cut \(n-1\), so its two outside faces are precisely the original endpoint variables. The tuple is typed and its restriction to each signed section is the original globular labelling. The resulting witness has type \(u\to v\). This proves reflection with the same output query for the raw language and its surface. It also explains why there is no disjunction over different simple paths.

A failure on \(U_n\) is a failure on a finite globular set. Conversely any failure on such a set translates to \(U_n\). By Response 5 a failure on a globular set is detected on a pasting tree, and the existence of a failure on a tree is a special case of the globular-set question. These implications give the stated equivalence for Q3(a). For fixed \(n,E\) and rule the same translation identifies the decision problem on promised old types over arbitrary finite globular sets with that on \(U_n\), under many-one reductions. For \(n=5\), the four-declaration test in the preceding response concerns agreement of the two rules themselves and uses the additional degree-four separation argument.

The checker constructs the contraction, expansion and labelling substitutions for 324 rows in degrees one through six. It checks their types, both signed restrictions and recovery of every changed position from its two colours. The contraction makes that slot stationary and replaces a path in another slot by a shorter path with the same end labels. The checker compares the resulting substitutions on every variable of each signed section. ## Researcher Response 110

**Every scalar plat probe test of Responses 69 and 77 has a realization at empty written ends on the universal ordinary presentation that preserves and reflects the answer for each individual surface.** A plat on \(2b\) strands uses exactly \(b\) two-wire exceptions in each direction, also when the probe itself is realized by a returning interval. Two of each direction suffice for a degree-five nonfilling with zero abelian winding even when the structural probe region has first homology of rank one. By Response 107, two of each are necessary for *any* one-probe degree-five difference invisible to integral abelianization on this presentation at empty ends.

### An interval pair with a readable representative in each strand

Use \(b_0:\varnothing\to f\) and \(d_0:f\to\varnothing\) for the birth and death **2-gates**, and encode a point 2-generator by their closed interval. The following program implements a birth of two intervals. Create one interval by the point-site exception. Expand its start to \(b_0;h\); expand \(h\) to \(h;h\) by the reverse vertical rule. Expand the lower unary gate into a new birth on the **left** of the old wire followed by a merge. Expand the upper unary gate to a split followed by a new death on the **right**. The merge and split are now adjacent at their full two-wire ports. Consume them with the two-wire exception. This leaves two separate intervals. In temporal order their four gates are old birth, new birth, new death, old death. Exchange the two middle gates by the permitted signed switch. The resulting order is the first complete interval (old birth, new death), then the second (new birth, old death). All other steps of this program have zero port cost in both directions. The reversed program uses the separately declared opposite rules.

Mark the original interval's birth and death at its creation, transferring the mark on the start to the replacement start when it grows a unary gate. Immediately after the final switch there is **one mark in each outgoing interval**, at the birth of the first and the death of the second. That switch crosses only unmarked gates. During any signed braid of entire intervals, restriction of the two-gate packet cables to these marks gives the original braid. At a closing pair the mark on either incoming interval might be on the opposite gate from the one required by the reversed program. To move a mark from the birth to the death, expand the birth to birth–unary, retaining the unary, then contract unary–death to the new marked death. To move it back use the two opposite rules. Both are raw endomorphisms of the same interval, and throughout each transfer the flat reading is one continuing mark. Perform the necessary transfers inside the closing pair's port before reversing its program. Each cap has literal boundary fits: the empty end is the seed's written empty drawing, and the positioned switch and graph and stacking fits at the two-interval end give the chosen stack of the two equal interval writings. [Universal port declarations](#researcher-response-103) · [Placement and boundary fits for closed copies](#researcher-response-92)

For the forward implication take the scalar plat with its occurrences named and substitute these programs for its pair births and deaths, the interval for each point gate, and the point-site interval creation followed by consumption for its free probe. The closing programs may differ at different named occurrences. Substituting a surface witness and folding the names therefore gives a witness at the encoded old faces. This applies to a specified old probe loop or a higher difference sphere, keeping the two given faces throughout.

For the converse first flatten a proposed wired witness and lift from the names of its structural events and gate segments as in Response 52. Map a marked gate to the original point 2-scalar and all other gates to the empty fit. Map an interval program's initial seed of a pair birth or terminal seed of a pair death to the original pair rule. Inside the separate probe copy, retain the opening event as the free 3-scalar and erase both its 2-gates. Every other structural event reads either zero marks on both ports, or one on each. Map it to the corresponding identity with its boundary fits. For the closing programs the transfers ensure exactly the prescribed two marks reach the consuming seed. Thus this is an occurrence substitution at the *actual* flat ports; the two-wire exception itself always has empty marked lists. It is available on a surface filler.

The composite on the original probe family reads the original pair events and the original signed strand braid. More explicitly, each point placement is read inside its own small substitution box. On a regular strand the read point is its chosen gate; a mark transfer just changes this position inside the packet. At a cap the two points come from the single pair event, with no mutual crossing before the ordered packet end. The comparison to the standard pair germ is relative to its two port positions: restrict the packet paths to the selected slots, then contract their constant-braid paths in the aspherical ordered planar configuration component. Along a moving cap use the same homotopy in its insertion disk. Disjoint insertions and subdivisions preserve the selected addresses. The probe position similarly contracts to its old point inside its own box. This gives the original raw comparison class at the fitted old faces, including for a family representing a higher sphere. Transport by these raw fits and homotopies gives the reverse surface implication. In particular the six surfaces of Response 48 have exactly the raw answers on this wired family. The four binary surfaces containing interchange have exactly the corresponding scalar **surface** tests. [Wire and event lifting](#researcher-response-52) · [Scalar link tests](#researcher-response-69) · [Higher word tests](#researcher-response-77)

### Probe group and a sharp threshold

One can also compute the whole wired fixed-history probe complement without using the decoding. In each opening cap the regular diagrams between the seed and the disconnection are single plane trees. The three newly introduced branches have no bounded faces. The marker trees for the internal expansions are connected too. Their exterior meridians map isomorphically along these internal steps. The seed on its empty side kills the single tree meridian. At the disconnection the exterior meridian of the connected marker maps to the product of the two outgoing interval meridians. This last map can be read on a curve surrounding the cap disk: its two children are the two outgoing intervals. There are no internal faces of either tree or of the two intervals. The two paths to the selected gates fix the same ordered meridians as the preceding marked reading. An end transfer also preserves the single meridian.

Equivalently, work relative to the disk boundary in each cap. The exterior faces in the cap are disks with zero, one or two holes, hence are 1-types. The preceding meridian maps identify the cut-and-tie diagram, after contracting the intermediate equivalences, with the ordinary two-point cap diagram (the tie circle maps to the empty disk and to the peripheral of the two-hole disk). These identifications are relative to the exterior collar, where nothing changes, so adjacent caps and all spectators may be glued back. Between the caps the two-gate interval packets induce exactly the ordinary signed braid on their complementary holes. The resulting one-probe spacetime has the homotopy type of the complement in three-space of the given plat closure. The separate probe interval can be shortened to its selected birth in this open complement, and the named section includes the resulting fibre in the raw total. [Cap complement](#the-two-particle-birth-and-death-computad) · [Section and interval probe](#researcher-response-107)

For two pairs take the commutator of the first meridians of the two opening pairs. The middle words \(\sigma_2^2\) and \(\sigma_2^3\) give the Hopf and trefoil examples respectively. The first commutator is trivial; the second acts nontrivially on three sheets although its integral abelianization vanishes. The trefoil region has first homology \(\mathbb Z\). Its group therefore needs at least two generators, and the two-wire count supplies the matching upper bound. The difference is raw at the actual wired empty ends. The translated sphere over infinity and its iterated brackets give the same word test in every degree from six on, with the same structural cap counts. No assertion about the four unresolved scalar interchange fillers is needed for the equivalence.

**Reproduce.** Run `python3 -B tools/semistrict_surface_wired_plats.py --agda-dir DIR` and `agda --safe --no-libraries -i src -i DIR DIR/WiredPlatCaps.agda`. The compiler recovers the exact cap arities and signed braid by restricting the actual seam words on all 259 four-strand braids of length at most three. On seven signed plats it separately builds the full wired complement spine, simplifies its relators and counts homomorphisms to the symmetric group on three letters. The Hopf and trefoil counts are 18 and 12, respectively, agreeing with the compact plat presentations. Agda checks both directed structural cap programs and transfer along an interval. Pass `{"pairs":2,"braid":[2,2,2],"word":[1,2,-1,-2]}` in a JSON file for the nonfilling certificate; use two braid letters for the filling derivation. Add `"sphere_degree":3` for the degree-seven tensor coefficient and its finite permutation model. The `--movie` and `--selection` options emit the full wired history and its occurrence certificate. ## Researcher Response 111

**A single knot type suffices to test the stationary-puncture obstruction, in every degree from five on.** If one of the four binary interchange surfaces fails a mixed scalar test of Responses 44–45, it fails at empty written ends on an explicitly constructed plat of the trefoil, for the same surface and in the same degree. The number of bridges may grow. Even a probe commutator that becomes trivial on deleting *any* one of arbitrarily many stationary punctures survives in the trefoil complement. The construction uses raw whiskering and cap programs on a proposed surface witness. In degree five it gives one integral matrix representation that detects all words of the embedded punctured disk, with a finite permutation certificate for every nonzero word.

### Where to place the punctured disk

For \(h\ge1\) punctures use \(h+1\) opening pairs. Denote their ordered meridians at the first gap by
\[
             a,a^{-1}, b_0,b_0^{-1},\ldots,b_{h-1},b_{h-1}^{-1}.
\]
In the closing braid first move the last strand left into the fourth slot, crossing negatively so that its meridian is unchanged. Apply three positive crossings in the second slot and close adjacent pairs. The extra death pairs each connect the second end of a \(b_i\)-bridge to the first of the next. Their peripheral relations identify \(b_i=b_{i+1}\): the two crossed meridians in each such pair have the same conjugator from the move of the last strand. On writing their common value as \(b\), the first two death relations are precisely those of the standard four-strand trefoil. Geometrically the enlarged part is one boundary-parallel arc in the bridge box of the second opening pair. To see this, undo the slide of its last endpoint: the internal adjacent pairs then cap on the plane of the opening arcs and the two outside ends go to the original two bridge endpoints. These successive small extrema straighten in that box. The three crossings with the first bridge remain the original trefoil diagram. This also describes the operation as repeated local bridge perturbation.

Before this closing braid insert a braid \(P\), a time interval with the probe query, and \(P^{-1}\). For the unmarked structural history they cancel as signed braids. To construct \(P\), move each \(b_i,b_i^{-1}\) pair as a packet next to the single strand \(a\), wind the packet positively around it \(5i\) times, and return it to its slot. Moving the packet left by negative crossings keeps its members unchanged and conjugates each bypassed strand by its trivial total peripheral. A positive full winding conjugates both members by \(a^{-1}(-)a\) and leaves \(a\) unchanged. Undoing the approach has the same trivial effect on the spectators. Finally move the first member of each pair left by negative crossings, placing those \(h\) members in their initial relative order at the beginning of the reading. Moving a strand left this way retains its meridian. Thus in the gap after \(P\) a disk about the first \(h\) slots has its standard free meridians read, in the complete knot group, as
\[
                     x_i=a^{-5i}ba^{5i},\qquad 0\le i<h .
\]
Here meridians and stems use the signed Artin convention of Response 69. Spectators stay outside the disk. For \(h=0\) use an empty disk beside the ordinary four-strand trefoil. [Signed cap and braid presentation](#the-two-particle-birth-and-death-computad)

These elements freely generate. In the projective action send \(a\) to \(z\mapsto z+1\) and \(b\) to \(z\mapsto z/(1+z)\). The trefoil relation in the indicated signs is \(a b^{-1} a=b^{-1}a b^{-1}\), which the determinant-one matrices satisfy. Every nonzero power \(b^k\) sends the exterior of \([-2,2]\), including infinity, to its interior: the image is \(1/(k+1/z)\). The corresponding intervals for \(x_i\) have centres \(-5i\) and are disjoint. Starting at infinity and grouping a reduced word into maximal powers, successive powers land inside their own intervals. Hence the word moves infinity. This proves injectivity on the entire free group, beyond abelian winding or bounded subfamilies. For a computed nonscalar matrix \(M\), take a prime not dividing \(\gcd(M_{12},M_{21},M_{11}-M_{22})\). Its action on the projective line over that finite field moves one of \(0,1,\infty\). Every closing relation fixes every sheet. For example the two-puncture commutator gives matrix rows \((151,625),(115,476)\) and takes zero to infinity modulo two.

### Why the same inclusion detects the higher tests

Let \(V\) be the open punctured disk times the available middle time interval, \(C\) the probe complement in three-space, and \(Y=S^3\setminus K\) for the same trefoil, with the point at infinity restored. One can take these complements with open collars. A punctured disk is aspherical, and the nonsplit knot exterior in the three-sphere is aspherical by the compact-core calculation of Response 82. Filling in infinity preserves the fundamental group. The explicit calculation therefore gives a \(\pi_1\)-injective open inclusion \(V\to Y\) of aspherical 3-manifolds, factoring through \(C\).

For every number of distinct named probes, the coordinate inclusion \(\operatorname{Conf}_m(V)\to\operatorname{Conf}_m(Y)\) injects on every positive homotopy group. In the forget-last-point fibre, lift to the universal covers before puncturing at the other fixed points. Distinct lifts of the named punctures in the source remain distinct in the target by group injectivity. The punctured covers are simply connected; excision gives free second homology on the small meridian spheres and no other reduced homology. The wedges of these spheres are weak equivalences, and the map sends each source summand to its corresponding distinct target summand. It splits up to homotopy on the covers. In degree one, puncturing leaves the original injective group map. The configuration forgetful fibrations have sections by placing a particle far out a proper ray beyond a compact exhaustion of the existing configuration. Their exact sequences and induction now give the asserted injectivity, also for torsion classes. Factorization gives injection into the actual three-space configuration of \(C\). This step retains the additional sphere over infinity in the actual complement while using the aspherical target to detect the incoming classes. To apply this to a surface query, use its stationary-puncture factor in Response 44. A fixed underlying planar path can be placed in an end collar and fitted back by its inverse; this is transport by raw cells and gives the same fixed-end configuration difference. Named probes suffice because a proposed surface witness agrees on their transport. At the chosen middle disk, pad the stationary gate row with the other strands of the trefoil by a fixed 2-whisker. Precompose by the opening pairs and the signed prefix; postcompose by the signed suffix and the closing pairs, using planar fits at the written 2-ends. These fixed actions on the old higher cells are defined on their proposed surface filler too. On the raw difference they include the probe configuration in its actual middle box, holding the rest of the structural movie fixed. The preceding injection and the occurrence-named section into the raw total preserve every nonzero difference; folding names still detects raw nullity. This proves the failure transfer. One may first use the bound of \(n-4\) probe occurrences in degree \(n\), and then apply Response 110 to obtain a wired realization. Whether an individual interchange surface fills a nonzero image class remains a surface question. The argument uses the stabilized histories at their actual written faces. **For Q3(a) in each degree $n\ge2$, pasting-context conservativity is equivalent to conservativity in that degree on the single globular set $T_{n-1}$ with one generator in each degree from zero to $n-1$.** Each positive-degree generator is a loop on the preceding generator. ### Moving the labels while keeping the written operation

Put $h=n-1$. We use this consequence of the slot-raising argument. Let $s,t$ assign labels to the same finite globular $h$-skeleton, agree below degree $h$, and provide for each $h$-slot an old raw $(h+1)$-cell from its $s$-label to its $t$-label at the common written type. Then every old raw $h$-term $w$ on that skeleton admits a forward raw comparison $sw\to tw$. To check the direction, perform induction on $w$. In a head at a top slot, raise the slot on the bound tree to a globe between the two versions, leaving the other slots fixed. The strict spelling of the head's value places the top generator, with fixed whiskers and a chronological prefix and suffix, at its unique ordinary top occurrence. Put the raised globe at that occurrence. The resulting strict comparison between the two generic head applications covers the raised ordinary tree. In degree $h\ge2$ the original full operation arity bearing an $h$-slot has just one active outer column by the sum of hom-tree heights. A variable-rule coherence case cannot use an $h$-slot at this rank either. The raised tree still has one active column, so a full operation head realizes the comparison at the literal generic faces. For $h=1$ one raises one edge of the composable line and its new column is the only active one. Substitute the induction comparisons and change the top arguments one at a time. All lower arguments stay fixed literally. Heads using exclusively lower arguments admit the identity. This proof uses each supplied arrow in its given direction. [Slot raising for arbitrary coherence heads](#researcher-response-41)

Given the old query $u\to v$ on $Z$, perform the ordinary shape, lower-label and directed slotwise path tests of Response 109. If a test fails, ordinary strict soundness excludes both sorts of inhabitant. Use the fixed impossible type $1_p\to a$ on the tester, where $a$ is its top generator and $p$ its common pole. The tester has only identity ordinary $n$-cells, and these two $h$-values differ. Otherwise let $K$ be the common unlabelled positional tree of the two $h$-pastes. Each slot is **stationary** in $K$: retain one copy, even if the two labels there in $Z$ differ. The two labellings $s,t:K\to Z$ agree below rank $h$. Lift $u,v$ at these positions to old writings $u_0,v_0$ on $K$ with $su_0=u$, $tv_0=v$. The written lower faces coincide by positional uniqueness on their common lower sections. Both $u_0,v_0$ have ordinary value the total of $K$ elevated to rank $h$. Let $k:K\to T_h$ be its unique globular labelling. Output $ku_0\to kv_0$. [Ordinary feasibility and effective signed lifts](#researcher-response-109)

**Preservation.** Lift any given raw or surface witness on $Z$ to the positional tree of its ordinary $n$-paste. Over each $h$-slot of $K$ this tree contains a string of $n$-changes, possibly empty or returning to its original label. Send all versions to the one slot of $K$, all changes to identities, and the common lower positions to themselves. This is a typed raw substitution. Its signed restrictions recover $u_0$ and $v_0$ by uniqueness, modulo the same surface in the surface case. Applying $k$ gives the desired tester witness.

**Reflection.** A tester witness has forced ordinary value: the identity on the common folded $h$-paste. Lift at that value to $K$. Positional uniqueness fixes the two signed faces to $u_0,v_0$ (or their surface classes). Evaluate using the *target* labelling $t$, obtaining $tu_0\to v$. At every changed slot use a raw chronological composite of the directed path found in the feasibility test, and at a stationary slot use the identity. The slot-raising lemma applied to the *source writing* $u_0$ gives a raw comparison $u=su_0\to tu_0$. Compose. Both interfaces have exactly the specified writings, with conversion available in the surface case. This proves reflection, including when the two $h$-pastes originally differed in their top labels. The reduction is effective on given old derivations and uses no reachability oracle in the selected directed kernel. By Response 5 a failure on a globular set lifts to a tree; trees are themselves finite globular sets. This proves the asserted equivalence for the class of trees. Degree one reduces directly to directed reachability of objects in the generating graph. [Positional lifting for both languages](#lifting-syntax-at-the-positions-of-an-ordinary-strict-cell)

For the fixed-context statement use $B=Z_{\le h}$. Any feasible query on $Z$ has the same answer, in either language, as $tu_0\to v$ on $B$. This follows by the same preservation (land on $K$ and label by $t$) and reflection (lift the witness on $B$ at its forced ordinary identity, or use it directly on $Z$ and prepend the slot action). This carries a failure on $Z$ to $B$. Conversely an old failure on $B$ has identical ordinary $h$-values at its two faces, since it has a surface witness there. If a raw witness appeared on $Z$, contract all its top strings onto $K$ as in preservation and label by the two faces' *common* $B$-labelling. This gives the missing raw witness on $B$. Both directions use truncation above the tested rank. In particular adjoining arbitrarily many globular $n$-generators changes individual answers but cannot change whether all old degree-$n$ queries reflect.

There is a related statement with nonglobular lower attaching terms. Let an arbitrary finite computad truncated at $n$ have all its $n$-generators running between $h$-variables at the same literal attaching type. Suppose every weak component of the resulting graph of $h$-variables is strongly connected. Keep one variable per component, with that attaching type over the unchanged lower context, forming $B'$. Collapse the other versions to their representative and the top changes to identities. This collapse has a raw section selecting the representatives. For any $h$-term $w$, directed paths of variables followed by the slot action compare $w$ with its collapsed and sectioned writing in *both* directions. The slot action proof works here too: it inducts on the term's bound heads and holds the entire lower assignment literally fixed. A raw or surface witness after collapse therefore lifts by the section and composition with the two endpoint comparisons; a witness before collapse descends by raw substitution. Thus each old query has exactly its collapsed answer in both languages. The strongly connected hypothesis supplies the backwards endpoint path in this last argument; the globular theorem above handles general directed top graphs by using positional lifting instead.

**Validation.** The top-string checker now also constructs a rank-five replay. On the stationary three-slot tree it takes the two distinct bracketings of the temporal product of the 4-slots. It folds their comparison to $T_4$. Over a cyclic graph with three versions it raises one occurrence at a time in the left bracketing, composes the three resulting directed 5-heads, and appends the comparison evaluated at the final labels. The check compares the result with the original type at its two different writings and labellings. ## Researcher Response 115

**On a fixed ordinary 3-computad, a free-probe fibre failure in any old degree from five through eleven forces failures in every higher degree for the same individual surface.** For a starting degree \(n=k+4\) with \(2\le k\le7\), keep at most \(k\) original probes and park one more occurrence of their free scalar. That one history supports failures in every later degree. This covers torsion failures as well as the infinite-order cases of Response 112. More generally the same conclusion holds in any starting degree when the last-point fibre class has nonzero stabilized loop adjoint. There is a nonzero order-two difference in old degree twelve for which both this invariant and the first Whitehead product with a fresh meridian vanish.

### A coefficient that survives each additional bracket

Reduce a hypothetical fibre failure to a minimal set of named probe coordinates, choose the last moving point, and park a new probe as in Response 112. Projection forgetting the last moving point is zero by minimality. The proper-ray section therefore gives a nonzero last-point fibre class. The coordinate bound and the section into the structural history use the actual old faces. In sphere degree \(k\ge2\) pass to the universal cover of that moving-point fibre, of homotopy type \(W=\bigvee S^2\) by Response 82. Let \(\alpha\in\pi_k W\) be the old class. Parking gives a surface-null lift \(\alpha'\); on covers forgetting the new punctures pinches their sphere summands. This statement uses the splitting obtained by puncturing the compact core and lifting its new sphere. Only finitely many letters of a wedge occur for any given class. [Probe bound and section](#researcher-response-79) · [Cover of a punctured core](#researcher-response-82) · [Parking on a surface witness](#researcher-response-112)

Take the adjoint \(S^{k-1}\to\Omega W\) and stabilize it. Use the augmentation ideal of the ring spectrum \(\Sigma^\infty_+\Omega W\), so that the constant map reads as zero. Its word summands are copies of the sphere spectrum shifted by word length, one degree-one letter per meridian. Multiplication concatenates words. For a proof, write \(W=\Sigma Z\) with \(Z\) a wedge of circles. The reduced James monoid on \(Z\) models its loop space. In the suspension spectrum take the length-one inclusion minus its unit value on the basepoint; this gives a map of reduced generators from \(\Sigma^\infty Z\). Extend multiplicatively from the free tensor ring spectrum. On the successive length-\(j\) filtration quotients this is the identity of \(\Sigma^\infty Z^{\wedge j}\): terms using a unit correction have shorter length. Induction on the cofibration filtration and passage to its union give the equivalence. This proof also makes pinching letters act by deletion of all words using them. [James, *Reduced Product Spaces*](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/jamesred.pdf)

The stabilized loop adjoint of a Whitehead product is the graded commutator in this ring. Indeed the loop adjoint is the Samelson commutator. On the product of the two representing spheres, expand their unit-corrected images and their inverses; terms using either reduced input twice vanish by the reduced diagonal of that sphere. On the top smash the surviving terms are the two products with the graded interchange sign. Thus this calculation retains stable stem coefficients, including ones invisible in integral loop homology.

Suppose the stabilized adjoint of \(\alpha\) has a nonzero coefficient \(c\) at the old, nonempty word \(u\). The coefficient in the parked lift is still \(c\). For any new meridian \(z\), the stabilized adjoint of \(\operatorname{ad}_z^r(\alpha')\) has coefficient \(c\) at \(z^r u\), up to the sphere orientation convention. At each commutator only left multiplication can contribute to this word, since its last letter is old. Arbitrary new-letter coefficients in the parked lift do not affect it. Consequently the iterated product survives in the raw fibre and total in *every* sphere degree \(k+r\). In the surface it vanishes by naturality, since \(\alpha'\) vanishes in the comparison hom space. This is a conditional statement about the same assumed surface filler, and an unconditional detection statement about the resulting raw classes.

### Why all classes through sphere dimension seven are covered

Take a nonzero Hilton component \(\beta\in\pi_k S^d\), \(2\le d\le k\), of \(\alpha\). The Hilton–Milnor product splitting provides a based map of loop spaces as **spaces** onto this factor. It sends the adjoint class to the adjoint of \(\beta\); it need not preserve multiplication for this detection step. Nonzero stable adjoint on the factor therefore implies nonzero stable adjoint on the original wedge. Suspending an adjoint once and applying evaluation recovers \(\beta\), so nonzero ordinary stabilization of \(\beta\) always suffices. Other based maps on loop spaces followed by stable evaluation are available too. [Hilton components used for probe coordinates](#researcher-response-45)

Here are the integral checks for \(k\le7\).

* For \(d=2\), \(k=2\) is detected by degree. For \(k\ge3\) use the complex Hopf fibration. Multiplying the bottom circle in \(\Omega S^2\) with the image of \(\Omega S^3\) gives a space equivalence \(S^1\times\Omega S^3\to\Omega S^2\): the connecting map is degree one on that circle and the higher homotopy groups agree by the fibration. The inverse followed by projection reads the Hopf lift in \(\pi_k S^3\).
* For \(d=3\), the first three groups, in dimensions three through five, are detected by stabilization (degree, \(\eta\), and \(\eta^2\)). In dimension six the order-twelve generator stabilizes to twice a generator of the order-twenty-four third stem, up to choosing generators. In dimension seven the nonzero class is \(\nu'\eta_6\). Apply the second James–Hopf map \(\Omega S^3\to\Omega S^5\). Its reading on \(\nu'\) is \(\eta_5\); since \(\eta_6\) is a suspension its reading on the composite is \(\eta_5\eta_6\), stably nonzero. Here the degree-seven generator uses the 2-primary \(\nu'\).
* For \(d=4\), dimensions through six lie in the stable range. In dimension seven write the two coordinates in \(\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/12\) on the Hopf map and the suspended order-twelve generator. The second James–Hopf map followed by stable evaluation reads the integer Hopf invariant. On its kernel ordinary stabilization embeds the order-twelve summand as the even subgroup of \(\mathbb Z/24\). For \(d\ge5\) all the remaining cases lie in the Freudenthal stable range.

These calculations use Toda's sphere groups, compositions and generalized Hopf invariants. They test the stable **adjoint** of the whole class: a nonzero factor reading precludes cancellation of all its stable word coefficients in the original wedge. Combining with Response 112 for degree five gives the stated range. In particular, reflection on all probe tests in any *one* degree at least twelve with up to eight probes on the relevant structural histories rules out every fibre failure through degree eleven. [Toda, *Composition Methods in Homotopy Groups of Spheres*, Chapters II and V](https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctt1bgzb5t) · [Integral low sphere groups and generators, Section 2](https://londmathsoc.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1112/tlm3.70010)

### First limit of this operation

In dimension eight take \(\gamma=\nu'\eta_6:S^7\to S^3\) and \(E\gamma:S^8\to S^4\). The latter is the nonzero generator \((E\nu')\eta_7\) of one of the two order-two summands of \(\pi_8 S^4\). Its adjoint factors as \(\gamma\) followed by the bottom \(S^3\to\Omega S^4\). Since the fourth stable stem is zero, its stabilized adjoint vanishes. Moreover \(E^2\gamma=0\): it is \((\pm2\nu_5)\eta_8\), zero because \(\eta_8\) is a suspended order-two class. Take a basic length-three Whitehead inclusion \(B:S^4\to S^2\vee S^2\). Hilton projection detects \(B\circ E\gamma\ne0\). This occurs at empty ends on three copies of a pure free 3-scalar: the moving-point fibre in three-space with two fixed points is the indicated wedge and injects into the total. After parking, the image is \(B'\circ E\gamma\) for the image of the same basic product under the placement map. For any fresh meridian \(z\) its bracket is \([z,B']\circ E^2\gamma=0\) by naturality of the universal Whitehead product under suspended precomposition. Thus dimension eight is a genuine sharp limit on *uniform detection by this operation*. The raw degree-twelve class and its vanishing bracket do not decide its surface image. [Strickland's explicit two-primary generators and Hopf map at \((8,4)\)](https://strickland1.org/toda/)

**Reproduce.** Run `python3 -B tools/semistrict_surface_stable_probe.py`. The solver uses the cited sphere data as inputs. It compares the combined stable readings on 1,040 factor coordinates, including cancellation between the two degree-seven generators over \(S^4\), and verifies the exceptional invisible order-two coordinate in dimension eight. Its independent word calculation evaluates 56 signed iterated commutators with integer, order-two and order-twenty-four coefficients and extra parked-letter terms. Pass `{"target_sphere":3,"source_sphere":6,"coordinates":[6]}` in a JSON file to see an order-two element detected as 12 modulo 24, or `{"target_sphere":4,"source_sphere":8,"coordinates":[0,1]}` for the sharp limit. ## Researcher Response 116

**In Q1(a) the top variable-to-variable declarations can be eliminated in every output degree, even over arbitrary nonglobular lower attachments.** Let $n=h+1\ge2$ and truncate a finite context $X$ at $n$. No connectedness or acyclicity hypothesis on the top graph is needed. An individual query translates to a computable finite disjunction of old queries on $B$, with the same disjunction for raw and surface syntax.

### The finite disjunction

Write $[a]$ for the chosen representative in the component of $a$, and $a\leadsto b$ for directed reachability, including the empty path. For an old query $u\to v$ keep all lower data literally. Replace the $h$-occurrences in $v$ by their representatives, obtaining $v_B$. For **each occurrence** of $a$ in $u$, independently choose a representative $c$ with $a\leadsto c$. Let $u_c$ denote the resulting source. Output $u_c\to v_B$ for all these choices, discarding any whose multisets of top names differ. Replacements are well typed because every edge of the graph preserves the whole written attaching type. An empty list of choices means the original query has no inhabitant. Occurrences in an $h$-term are read recursively in the order of its top arguments. The same old variable occurring twice may require two different choices.

If a retained query has a witness on $B$, include it in $X$. Each path from a source occurrence to its chosen representative gives a chronological raw $n$-cell. Apply the slot action of Response 114 occurrence by occurrence to the source writing: first regard its different occurrences as distinct top variables with the given parallel types, then use the supplied paths. This gives $u\to u_c$. For the target use paths from the representatives to the actual labels in their components, giving $v_B\to v$. Composing gives an inhabitant in the same language as the retained witness.

For the converse construct a finite context $Y$ over $X$, fixing the entire skeleton below $h$. Replace $a$ by copies $(a,c)$ for every representative $c$ reachable from $a$. Each declared arrow $z:a\to b$ has a copy $(a,c)\to(b,c)$ for every $c$ reachable from $b$; this supplies all the copies needed at its sources by transitivity. There are two maps. Folding to $X$ forgets $c$ and sends a copied arrow to $z$. Evaluation in $B$ sends $(a,c)$ to $c$ and every copied arrow to its identity. Both preserve all written faces. Lift the actual target $v$ by using $(b,[b])$ at its occurrences.

A witness downstairs lifts *backwards from this specified target*, with some lift of its source. Here backwards describes the order of assigning the tuple; the direction of every cell stays fixed. We give the argument because independently matching the two occurrence lists by their written order would be invalid. For a degree-$n$ boundary impose the relation that every lift of its target to $Y$ admits a witness from some lift of its source. Below rank $n$ use the actual raw or surface classes of $X$. Use a single cell at a boundary satisfying the relation and unique cells over compatible higher boundaries. For a degree-$n$ head use its ordinary positional tree and split the given lift of the positive face into labels for the positive section. This splitting uses the top-occurrence transport of Response 57: the lower skeleton maps identically, top variables have parallel copies, and a prescribed list of copies determines a unique lift of the surface class. In particular it applies to a converted operation on its bound tree, and the raw splitting is literal. At $h=1$ the same splitting just colours the edges of the ordinary path in order. Each top stack of the tree is now labelled at its last version. Traverse its changes from last to first. The relation on the assigned change furnishes its upper arrow at the current lifted target and gives the preceding label. The common lower sections were fixed at the start. Apply the original operation to this lifted tuple. Its positive section is the specified lifted target and its negative section provides the required source. This verifies closure of the relation under operations. The lower surface equations hold in the given classes and those at the tested rank hold by uniqueness at a boundary. Every declared top variable satisfies the relation by construction of its copies. This proves the lifting assertion, including for a composite witness. [Splitting at a lifted face and the model argument](#splitting-an-operation-at-the-actual-lifted-surface-cell)

The source lift has a representative folding literally to $u$, by top-occurrence transport; its lower faces are unchanged. Evaluate in $B$. We have obtained precisely a witness $u_c\to v_B$ with one of the proposed choices. Since $B$ has no $n$-generators its ordinary $n$-value is an identity. In particular the two multisets of top names agree, which justifies the discard test. This proves the individual equivalence. The construction allows a witness whose underlying $n$-cell exchanges top occurrences between its two written orders.

### Reflection as a property of the entire context

A failure on $X$ yields a surface-inhabited candidate on $B$, and none of its candidates has a raw inhabitant. For the reverse take a failure $p\to q$ on $B$, include it at the representative variables of $X$, and keep its surface witness. Since that witness already exists on $B$, $p$ and $q$ have identical multisets of $h$-generators. Choose a linear extension of the finite acyclic component graph and give its vertices strictly increasing integer weights along every proper directed edge. In any retained candidate for $p\to q$ each occurrence of $p$ can only increase in weight. Its new total equals the total of $q$, which was already the original total of $p$. Thus every occurrence keeps its own component. As the old names themselves were representatives, the only retained source is $p$ literally and the target is $q$. A raw witness in $X$ would consequently give a raw witness at the original failed type in $B$. This proves the fixed-context equivalence. In particular if the components are singletons, degree-$n$ reflection depends only on the original $(n-1)$-skeleton, regardless of how many one-way paths the top graph adds. The argument tests equality of sums only at this last step, after the actual direction-respecting lifts have been proved.

Its raw example uses five 3-variables on the composite 2-pole $k; k$, two nontrivial strongly connected components and edges between components. Two occurrences of the same old variable finish in different components. The code builds the three individual slot actions, places a native inner exchange between the source and target actions, and checks the composite at the prescribed old faces. [Crowley–Schick, Lemma 2.14 and its proof](https://msp.org/gt/2013/17-3/gt-v17-n3-p11-s.pdf) · [Adams, *On the groups J(X) IV*, Proposition 12.14](https://www.sas.rochester.edu/mth/sites/doug-ravenel/otherpapers/Adams-JX4.pdf)

**In arbitrarily high degrees, the number of essential probes gives a range in which a fibre failure forces failures in every higher degree.** Fix the surface and the finite ordinary 3-computad. ### Why the number of names controls stabilization

Work in the one occupied region supporting a nonzero projection. Forget the last moving point and use the section to read a last-point fibre class \(\alpha\in\pi_k W\), with \(W\) the wedge of 2-spheres in the punctured universal cover. Its letters include one meridian for each lift of each of the \(m-1\) fixed points and may also include spheres of the unpunctured cover. Deleting a fixed point pinches precisely its meridian letters. The resulting fibre injects into its configuration total, so minimality makes that pinch of \(\alpha\) zero. Take a Hilton basis with the inherited order on any subset of the letters. A basic product survives a pinch unchanged if all its letters survive, and vanishes otherwise; the surviving basic products form the basis on the retained alphabet. Hence **every nonzero coordinate** uses at least one letter from every fixed point. ### An effective restriction on counterexamples

For any finite collection of top rules, the largest removable block of expansions is computed as follows. Mark all rules whose source is not literally a variable. Repeatedly mark a remaining rule if its source variable occurs in the target of a marked rule. At termination the unmarked rules form an eligible block. Every eligible block avoids the initial marks, and by induction avoids each subsequent mark, proving maximality. Compute the contraction block in the opposite direction. Apply the two reductions repeatedly. Eligibility survives removal of other rules: restrict the proposed block to the rules still present; its complement can only shrink. Consequently overlapping eligible blocks can be eliminated in either order with the same union gone. Finiteness gives a unique terminal collection, even if nonmaximal blocks are chosen at each stage. The computation uses actual variable occurrences at the tested rank and tests *literal* variable faces; a unary compound face may contain a single occurrence without being a bare variable.

Fix an ordinary surface and output degree $k$. A failure on the original context implies a failure on its terminal collection in that degree. For $k\ge h+2$ the implication goes both ways, giving an equivalent fixed-context test. In a nonempty terminal collection every rule is marked from a nonvariable source by the forward procedure, and from a nonvariable target by the reverse procedure. If all top rules are eliminated, reflection reduces to the $h$-skeleton. This generalizes the all-degree one-sided result and the planar expansion/contraction condition to arbitrary generating rank and arbitrary retained top declarations. For example a family of compound-to-compound rules may remain, with whole recursive expansion systems attached on their input side, and recursive contractions on their output side. The bare input of an expansion may be reproduced by another rule in the same eliminated block. In Q3(b,c), taking $k=5,6$ gives these reductions at the actual old types in those degrees. Denote multiset firing reachability, allowing no steps, by \(\leadsto\).

This count is a strict grading. Collapse the degrees below \(j-1\) to singletons. In degree \(j-1\) take markings with addition at every cut; in degree \(j\) take a unique arrow \(p\to q\) when \(p\leadsto q\). Compose these arrows transitively at the top cut and by addition at the lower cuts. Adding a stationary marking preserves every firing. Commutativity below the top cut and uniqueness at fixed arrow endpoints give strict interchange. Above \(j\) take only identities. Each original generator has a grade, by induction over the declarations. In degree \(j-1\) it is one token. In degree \(j\) its transition is present. Above \(j\) its two parallel faces have identical grades by thinness in degree \(j\). Thus every language in the question maps to this target by its ordinary strict projection.

Let \(M,N\) be the counts at the two iterated \((j-1)\)-poles of the query. If \(M\not\leadsto N\), there is no inhabitant. Otherwise regard all grades below \(j-1\) as retained. Retain a marking \(p\) by testing its identity, and retain an arrow \(p\to q\) or a higher identity on it exactly when

\]

Duplicate the firing instructions in two control states, start in the first with \(M\), finish in the second with exactly \(N\), and allow one change of state consuming \(p\) and producing \(q\). Add a transition \(p\to q\) with its own name and ask if it belongs to the structurally cyclic transitions. If a return uses this new transition several times, replace all but one use by firings of the original net: the proposed grade itself supplies \(p\leadsto q\). This gives the required single use. The inner computation always has a single nested chain of pending calls with the current entry or exit at its tip. In particular its successive instructions share the state just produced; the outer birth and death share the respective states with their neighbors as well. Conversely every nonempty return closes at least one outer lens, whose private computation certifies a true output. Other outer lenses cannot change that computation. The construction is logspace and has only one root and at most a single child in each written port. Repeated calls to a shared circuit node do not duplicate its rules. With a true input and \(d\) successive AND nodes each calling the previous one twice, the shortest complete return has \(2^{d+2}-1\) uses, despite the polynomial decision. These hardness instances work for both questions; the questions themselves can differ. Creating a lens with two \(s\)'s and closing with two \(t\)'s, with only the inner rule \(s\to t\), permits an unrestricted return and forbids a dependent one. [Goldschlager, monotone circuit value](https://doi.org/10.1145/1008354.1008356)

### Two outer components suffice for the full lower bound

Given an exact Petri marking query \(u\leadsto v\), let the outer birth make a single \(x\)-lens containing \(u\) and one ready controller at \(y\), and require \(v\) and the same controller at its death. Serialize each transition into a private chain of controller states. First consume its required tokens, one per step beside the controller; then produce its output tokens, one per step beside the controller. The last step returns the ready state. A zero-change instruction with both vectors zero may be omitted. In every completed phase the next marking is exactly the original firing result. An incomplete phase cannot accept or enter another instruction. Each step uses and replaces the current controller, so an accepting simulation gives a dependent return. Conversely any closed outer lens gives an accepting marking path by reading only its own phases. Every inner rule has at most two outer components on each side; every outer port still has at most one. The encoding is linear in the explicitly repeated tokens (elementary with binary-encoded multiplicities). The general upper bound and the marking-reachability lower bound of Response 137 apply. [General closed-port complexity](#researcher-response-137)

## Researcher Response 147

**If every rule has at most one outer input component, recognizing either kind of positive empty return is NP-complete. At most two outer outputs already suffice for hardness. | Maximum outer inputs | Maximum outer outputs | Complexity |
|---|---|---|
| One | One | P-complete |
| One | Two or more, including unbounded | NP-complete |
| Two or more, including unbounded | One | NP-complete |
| Two or more | Two or more | Ackermann-complete |

### One certificate for the nested computation

At an object with one outer input, every marking move in Response 137 consumes at most one template. Internal summary transitions consume exactly one. This is communication-free Petri reachability. A birth can be represented by consuming and replacing a fresh permanent token in addition to emitting its list; its input then has size one. At a one-output object reverse the marking query and all marking moves for this local test. Time reversal at one object is only a device for checking the original directed face judgment. The initial and final forests of the summary keep their actual orientation.

In more detail, take one variable \(n_t\ge0\) for the integer count of each transition. Require that its total change gives the target minus the source. Each input place of a transition of positive count must be reachable from an initially marked place along the directed input-to-output graph of positive-count moves. A birth gives source access to its outputs. These two conditions are sufficient by the communication-free reachability theorem. They have polynomially sized existential certificates. For the access check use level one at initial places, and give an accessed noninitial place a producing transition of positive count whose input has smaller positive level, or a positive-count birth. The state equation alone would permit unsupported cycles. The solver tests this integer formula for the actual objects, face lists and marked rule variants. Although the computation iterates summary additions, **the entire accepting derivation has one NP certificate**. Guess a list of distinct directed template pairs, in the order of their justifications. Verify the common core and every corresponding face by a communication-free certificate using only original moves and pairs earlier in the list. Finally certify the chosen exterior marking test with the listed pairs; include the chosen first and last mark when required. There are only polynomially many pairs and face tests on the polynomially many marked templates. A least-fixed-point success supplies such a list by sorting its justifications by round. Conversely every verified entry is sound by induction on the list. This also explains why choosing opposite arity restrictions at different objects works. ### Exact cover inside a single occupied face

Given a universe and a list of subsets, the outer birth creates one lens holding the initial control state and the outer death requires that lens holding the final state and exactly one scalar for each universe element. As in Response 146 its interior object differs from the exterior one. At each subset the internal controller either skips it or emits a token for each of its elements, one per step along a private sequence of states. Each internal step consumes just the current state and produces the next state with at most one extra token. Element tokens are never consumed internally. Thus closing a lens witnesses pairwise disjoint chosen sets with precisely the required union. An exact cover gives a history whose successive steps share their actual controller, including the opening and closing incidences. Other lenses have independent private contents, so allowing arbitrary schedules cannot turn a no-instance into a return. This is a polynomial reduction for both return questions with output bound two; reversing the rules proves hardness for the opposite side restriction. |---|---|
| Absent | Every individual surface reflects in all degrees. |

### Counting through children over a whole lifetime

Read the rule ports and both query ends as typed forests as in Response 137. In each host the local incidence graph is a union of paths, including isolated uses and unchanged single strands. A trajectory joining the two lifetime ends gives one through child; a trajectory meeting neither end gives one free point after the branch contraction. Any such free trajectory yields an actual positive return at the object of the host: take its sequence of outer uses, with the full port diagrams and the private histories in the successive roots it creates and consumes. Other sibling trajectories can be forgotten. Conversely any positive return at that object placed beside the children supplies at least one free trajectory in the host. It can be inserted arbitrarily many times. Thus in computing \(H\) it suffices to maximize the number of through trajectories in each realizable host whose object admits a positive return. A host must be considered with its *actual* two lifetime ends: some children can be wholly temporary even if they occupy an intermediate template.

Use one state \(A_{\rm new}\) and one state \(A_{\rm ready}\) for each rooted template. A realizable persistent-core change gives an edge \(A_{\rm new}\to B_{\rm ready}\), including the identity case. A local unary rule consuming \(B\) and producing \(D\) gives an edge \(B_{\rm ready}\to D_{\rm new}\); keep these distinct even if the two unlabelled templates agree. Births may start at their output's new state, deaths may finish at their input's ready state, and a blank-to-blank event is recorded separately. Start each prescribed sibling in its new state and require each prescribed final sibling in its ready state. There is **exactly one internal edge per actual persistent core lifetime** along such a path.

First saturate the internal edges from the identity pairs. Add \(A_{\rm new}\to B_{\rm ready}\) for matching bare cores when the sibling lists in all corresponding bounded faces are reachable with the current edges. Use the vacancy-padded matching of Response 146, allowing a real through pair precisely for a path from new to ready with no intervening vacancy. A disposable source or a creatable target is matched to a vacancy. The lifetime decomposition and induction on finite nested computations give soundness and completeness as in Response 137. At saturation a positive return at an object is equivalent to either a blank event or a path from a birth state to a death state.

Then work **from the actual query inwards**. At a feasible pair of sibling lists \(U,V\), find each internal edge \(A_{\rm new}\to B_{\rm ready}\) usable in some such computation. Choose a source position of \(U\) or a birth, and a target position of \(V\) or a death. Require a path to the new state from the selected start, a path from the ready state to the selected finish, and feasibility of the remaining two lists with the selected real positions taken out. A birth start or death finish entails the corresponding actual birth or death rule. Iterate from the exterior query, processing each triple of object and sibling lists just once. Conversely tracing any actual lifetime through its ancestors visits that triple. In particular two internal edges may never be concatenated on the same core to manufacture a shorter observation interval.

Internal vertices of an augmenting path stay matched, so it still covers those compulsory endpoints. Complete the remaining endpoints by births and deaths. Take the maximum over the visited triples at returning objects only. All searches, matchings, pairs and rounds are polynomial in the explicit positioned input. Each order embeds on fundamental groups at the terminal configuration: the last expansion has a one-leaf left inverse, and the first expansion does too. In grouped terminal coordinates its exact membership test on a pure braid with trivial through restriction is as follows. Sufficiency follows from the pullback since the signed projections then specify agreeing loops at its common cut, and that cut has no second homotopy group.
