### Why the two packet disks still give a forest

In a large spatial disk times the time interval, take the standard trace \(T\) consisting of the vertical through strands and the two disjoint birth stars with tips on the top disk. Round a small regular neighbourhood of this trace and take its exterior \(X\). Let \(F\) be the top disk with the terminal holes excised. Consider the complex of essential curve classes on \(F\) bounding properly embedded compressing disks in \(X\), with simplices given by disjoint representatives. Each such disk cuts the ambient ball into two balls. On its top-disk side it encloses no through tips, since a through strand continues to the bottom, and either all or none of each star, since the star is connected. The only types are therefore \(A,B,AB\), recording the packets enclosed.

This disk complex is contractible. Here are the hypotheses of the disk-surgery criterion in this application. The exterior is irreducible: every sphere in it bounds a ball away from the trace since each trace component meets the ambient boundary. The complement of \(F\) on its boundary consists of the punctured surfaces around the stars and the outer surface coming from the bottom, side and through tubes. The star surfaces have at least two holes each and the outer one has \(m+1\ge2\). Thus the boundary circles of \(F\) are essential on the doubled-up boundary surface \(\partial X\), and nonperipheral curve classes of \(F\) embed there with their disjointness relation (use minimal position with these boundary circles). No peripheral curve of \(F\) bounds a disk in \(X\): a single tip cannot be cut off and all tips together include a through tip. In an irreducible manifold disks with the same boundary class are isotopic and disks with disjoint boundaries can be made disjoint by innermost-circle surgery. This realizes our complex as the full subcomplex of the disk complex of \(X\) on classes with boundary in \(F\). For each outermost surgery on two of its disks in minimal position, the surgery curves are still on \(F\) and at least one is essential on \(\partial X\) (otherwise the original boundary would be null). These are representatives with boundary inside the essential subsurface, where boundary intersections are already minimal on \(\partial X\). The surgery therefore stays in the subcomplex in the sense of the contractibility criterion. [Cho, Koda and Lee, Theorem 2.1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.10241)

The single-packet subcomplex is a bipartite graph: disjoint curves enclosing the same names cobound an empty annulus. Distinct \(AB\) vertices likewise cannot be adjacent. The link of an \(AB\) vertex lies inside its top subdisk with just the two packets. Cap the outside of that subdisk by a disk marked at infinity. After filling infinity, adjacent single-packet vertices map to the same essential curve on the sphere, since they surround complementary packets. Thus each connected component of the link embeds in the fibre over one vertex of the forgetful curve map, a tree by Kent–Leininger–Schleimer. Indeed nonperipheral classes inside the subdisk agree with those on the once-capped punctured sphere, and attaching the original outside gives the same classes inside the subdisk. So every link is a forest. The full disk complex is obtained from the single-packet graph by coning these links. Coning a forest is homotopically the attachment of an interval from each of its contractible components to the new cone vertex. Such attachments preserve injection on the fundamental group of every old component, also for infinitely many cone vertices by the CW construction. Since the full complex is contractible, the single-packet graph itself is a forest. [Curve fibres, Theorem 7.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0611241)

The terminal pure braids of both order groups preserve this forest. A motion of the sites and seams carries the embedded trace through an isotopy, keeping the through strands fixed and using the standard packet collars. Returning to the original movie gives extension of the top braid over its trace exterior by isotopy extension; adding the terminal path is just attaching a braid collar. Equivalently first drag the early star around the throughs in a parallel disk, then drag the late star in a disk around the earlier leaves and throughs. The last packet disk is preserved. In this order the stabilizer of the *other* packet boundary is exactly the tie: preserving both disjoint disks separates a terminal braid into the simultaneous parallel exterior cable and two internal braids. Reading each packet alone gives its internal braid. Both readings vanish by the order membership tests, so exactly the simultaneous cable remains. Conversely all such cables preserve the two disks. Now map the coset tree of the amalgam to this forest by translating the edge of the two standard packet disks. The stabilizer test makes the map locally injective, hence injective. Any terminal kernel lies in the tie, where keeping one leaf per packet is a left inverse. Taking the fixed-end homotopy fibre proves the assertion. The probe and surface conclusions follow by the configuration fibration and retained-arc detection of Response 151, now with contractible unmarked base regardless of the transient caps. [Probe detection at an occupied face](#researcher-response-143)

1. Its restriction to the through strands is the identity.
2. Its restriction to the leaves of *each individual packet* is the identity.
3. Every \(f(t_i)\) is trivial in \(F_n/N\), using the signed Artin action.

The third condition says exactly that \(f\) preserves \(N\): forward inclusion induces a surjective endomorphism of the finite-rank free quotient, which is Hopfian. ### The exact homotopy-type test

Use the notation and reversibility hypotheses of Response 153. In particular \(n\ge2\) is the stationary scalar rank, \(K\) is the connected based realization of the finite local presentation, \(Y=\Sigma^nK\), \(i\ge2\), and the requested filler has degree \(n+i+1\). Write \(E\) for ordinary reduced suspension of a map. Define
\[
 T_{n,i}(Y)=\ker\!\left(
 \pi_{i+1}Y \xrightarrow{\mathrm{adj}} \pi_i\Omega Y
              \xrightarrow{E^n}\pi_{n+i}(\Sigma^n\Omega Y)\right).
\]
After fitting the lower boundary and naming the \(h\) stationary occurrences, test the stationary projection by pure published reflection and the bulk by scanning into \(Y\), as in Response 153. Both must vanish for a published filler. The remaining raw difference has coordinates \((\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_h)\in(\pi_{i+1}Y)^h\), one radial shell for each puncture. **On this subgroup the kernel of all evaluations in homotopy types is exactly \(T_{n,i}(Y)^h\).** [Fixed-boundary comparison and scanning](#researcher-response-153)

Indeed the universal such evaluation uses the space \(W=Y\vee\bigvee_{j=1}^h S^n_j\). A stationary generator has image a based \(n\)-sphere and the shifted mobile generators specify a based map \(K\to\Omega^n Z\) in a target \(Z\). Their assignments extend over the attaching disks at the prescribed faces. By adjunction these data give a based map \(W\to Z\), up to homotopy. Equivalently, take the groupoid completion of the presentation one attaching globe at a time. Unused colours can be sent to the basepoint. In \(W\) the shell sum reads as the sum of the products \([\iota_j,\alpha_j]\), by the boundary-of-a-product calculation of Response 153. Retraction onto \(S^n_j\vee Y\) reads each term individually. This proves universality at the named faces. [Published evaluation in homotopy types](../answered/semistrict-surface-conservativity-2026-11-24.md#researcher-response-57)

Here is the kernel of a single product. The homotopy fibre of \(S^n\vee Y\to Y\) is \(S^n\wedge(\Omega Y)_+\). Pull back the based path fibration over the two wedge summands. Its total over \(Y\) contracts, its total over the sphere is \(S^n\times\Omega Y\), and their common fibre is \(\{*\}\times\Omega Y\). Taking the homotopy pushout gives the asserted quotient. The projection has a section, so this fibre injects on homotopy groups. For any connected based CW space \(L\) there is a natural equivalence
\[
 S^n\wedge L_+\ \simeq\ S^n\vee (S^n\wedge L).
\]
Pinch the suspension coordinate and apply the augmentation on one copy and the based quotient on the other. This induces the split reduced homology isomorphism, and both sides are simply connected.

Write \(u:S^i\to\Omega Y\) for the adjoint of \(\alpha\). In the path model the stationary sphere with a collar traversing the loop \(u(t)\) lifts to the sphere labelled by that path. The associated family in the fibre is induced by \(S^n\wedge u_+\) on \(S^n\wedge(S^i)_+\). To take its based difference, translate by the inverse of the sphere at the reference parameter in the \(n\)-fold loop space. Calculate first in the domain \(S^n\wedge(S^i)_+\simeq S^n\vee S^{n+i}\). Augmentation gives a constant family and hence zero difference. Quotienting by the reference sphere gives the identity on the smash \(S^n\wedge S^i\), up to orientation. These two readings determine the class in degree \(n+i\), since the product of the two spheres is obtained from the wedge by a cell of dimension \(2n+i>n+i+1\). Naturality of the splitting sends this class to the inclusion of \(\pm E^nu\) in the smash summand of the fibre. Projection from the fibre back to the wedge gives precisely the collar difference \(\pm[\iota_n,\alpha]\). The fibre injection and the summand retraction prove the equality of kernels.

The group \(T_{n,i}(Y)\) is finite. Suspension induces an isomorphism on reduced homology, so its kernel on homotopy lies in the Hurewicz kernel before suspension. The rational Hurewicz map on \(\pi_i\Omega Y\) is injective by Milnor–Moore. Consequently \(T_{n,i}(Y)\) lies in the torsion subgroup of \(\pi_{i+1}Y\), a finitely generated abelian group since \(Y\) is a simply connected finite CW complex. In particular every infinite-order shell difference has a published obstruction at its written boundary. [Milnor–Moore, Appendix](https://www.sas.rochester.edu/mth/sites/doug-ravenel/otherpapers/Milnor-Moore.pdf)

### Finite comparisons at one stationary occurrence

Assume the context has a stationary colour. At one occurrence and the standard row, let \(P\) consist of shell classes admitting a published comparison to zero. Use the iterated identity as common boundary for the two disks. Changing the raw sphere representative preserves the judgment by the two directed raw fits of Response 153. Pasting comparisons shows closure under addition, and \(0\in P\). Since \(P\subseteq T_{n,i}(Y)\) is finite, every additive inverse in \(P\) is realized by repeated addition. Hence \(P\) is a subgroup.

At any old boundary with zero stationary and bulk difference a published comparison exists precisely when each named shell lies in \(P\). To see necessity, transport both disks to a based difference at the standard row by pasting the raw inverses and unit fits in the local truncation. These operations transport an existing directed surface comparison. Forget all but the selected named puncture by raw substitution. The annuli around the forgotten punctures then bound in their filled balls, and the selected annulus gives its one-puncture class. For sufficiency, place the one-puncture comparison in a small ball about the corresponding stationary occurrence and juxtapose the other stationary disks as identities. Its raw coordinates are the stated ones, since arcs to all other punctures miss this ball. Paste these comparisons, use the raw equality of the resulting sphere with the prescribed difference in the local truncation, then undo the base and boundary fits. Folding the names gives the comparison in the original context. Without stationary colours the two initial tests suffice.

A nonzero subgroup \(P\) contains a subgroup of prime order. It therefore suffices to test one generator of each order-\(p\) subgroup of \(T_{n,i}(Y)\) against zero, in a single puncture. Each test has a raw sphere representative by the fixed-boundary groupoid comparison, and a nonzero test has raw-empty comparison type. For a fixed presentation and degree the number of tests is
\[
 \sum_{p\mid |T_{n,i}(Y)|}
       \frac{p^{\dim_{\mathbb F_p} T_{n,i}(Y)[p]}-1}{p-1}.
\]
This is a finite reduction to published inhabitation. Deciding that inhabitation on a nonzero test remains necessary to use it as a classification.

### Sphere labels and the first undetected type

Suppose \(Y\) is a wedge of spheres of dimensions at least \(n+1\). For \(i+1\le7\), any nonzero Hilton component of \(\alpha\) has a nonzero stabilized loop adjoint by the sphere calculations of Response 115. The Hilton–Milnor loop-space projection reads that component before stabilization. Thus \(E^n\mathrm{adj}(\alpha)\ne0\), and insertion reflects in degree \(n+i+1\). This gives, for example, degree nine at \(n=2\) under the corresponding reversibility assumptions. For \(i+1=8\) the Hilton spheres of dimension at least five are in the stable range. The dimension-three factor is read by the second James–Hopf map. On a dimension-four factor the same test detects the \(\nu_4\eta_7\) coordinate and leaves only \(\tau=E\gamma\), where \(\gamma=\nu'\eta_6:S^7\to S^3\). The bottom inclusion \(j:S^3\to\Omega S^4\) gives \(\mathrm{adj}(\tau)=j\gamma\). Already \(E^2\gamma=0\), since \(E^2\nu'=\pm2\nu_5\) and \(\eta_8\) is a suspended element of order two. Hence \(\tau\) lies in the actual kernel for all \(n\ge2\). A mixed Hilton sphere has dimension at least \(3+3-1=5\), so each eligible 4-sphere is an original wedge summand. The projections and inclusions show that \(T_{n,7}(Y)\) is exactly one copy of \(\mathbb Z/2\) for each such summand. In particular reflection follows throughout this family in output degree \(n+8\) if there is no 4-sphere. [Hilton factor and sphere calculations](#researcher-response-115) · [Degree-eight coordinates](#researcher-response-117) · [Toda's sphere generators](https://strickland1.org/toda/)

Here are finite presentations realizing the nonzero kernel, including its reversibility hypotheses. Take \(n=2\) or \(3\), \(d=4-n\), a point, one stationary \(n\)-scalar, and a single local \(d\)-generator with identity faces above the blank. Its based local realization is \(S^d\). Starting at rank \(d\) process this generator and, at each next rank through seven, the round-trip witnesses created at the preceding rank. For each \(f:a\to b\) being processed, add two arrows \(r,l:b\to a\) and the two witnesses \(fr\to1_a,\ lf\to1_b\), with products written in execution order. At rank eight also adjoin the opposite of every new witness. The top relation is symmetric. Descending in rank, the two witnesses are equivalences in the appropriate truncation, so \(f\) has both a left and a right inverse there. Both chosen inverses are then equivalences themselves. This verifies every local reversibility requirement.

Each fresh inverse and its own round-trip disk form an elementary expansion relative to the complex present just before the pair. In the attaching sphere the new inverse occupies a single disk with multiplicity one, and the rest maps into the preceding complex. Pushing this disk across the new globe gives the relative homotopy equivalence, including at \(d=1\). Before adjoining the final opposite witnesses the realization is therefore still \(S^d\). Each opposite attaches along the reverse of an already filled sphere, adding an \(S^8\) summand. The full presentations have 319 and 639 global declarations respectively, with 64 and 128 such summands. After \(n\) suspensions there is exactly one 4-sphere, and all the additional spheres are above dimension eight.

For either presentation take the raw based sphere represented by the single radial shell with coordinate \(\tau\), at the stationary row, and ask for a comparison to the identity. Its output degree is ten or eleven respectively. The fixed-boundary correspondence in Response 153 realizes this by parallel raw terms. The punctured scan excludes a raw comparison, since projection to the 4-sphere recovers the nonzero \(\tau\). Every homotopy-type evaluation gives a comparison, by the kernel calculation. Thus for each of these finite contexts there is **one** remaining insertion test in this output degree. Its published inhabitation is open.

The two single comparisons also suffice *uniformly* at degree \(n+8\) if the unsuspended \(K\) is a finite wedge of spheres, up to based homotopy. More precisely, for each fixed \(n\in\{2,3\}\), all reversible presentations of this kind having both a stationary colour and a \(d=4-n\) sphere summand have the same answer as the finite presentation just constructed. Without either, reflection follows above.

We give the substitution argument since suspension can conceal information about the attaching maps. For reversible one-object local presentations \(D,D'\) truncated at rank eight, any based map \(|D|\to |D'|\) can be realized by a raw substitution *on the homotopy 7-types*. To verify this, work first in the local calculus before shifting. Its homotopy 7-category is groupoidal by reversibility and is the homotopy 7-groupoid of its realization, by the truncation and groupoid-completion universal property of Response 153. This equivalence is essentially surjective on the cells in each iterated hom of specified raw ends and bijective on top cells there. Choose the variable images inductively. Having matched the boundary of a \(j\)-globe to its prescribed image up to a coherent boundary homotopy, transport the prescribed disk across this homotopy. For \(1\le j\le7\) the equivalence on the iterated hom supplies a raw \(j\)-cell at those very ends in the resulting relative homotopy class. The relative homotopy extends the match over this disk. At \(j=8\) the matched ends are equal in the top hom-set, so the symmetric top reachability in the target supplies a raw 8-cell in the required direction. There is no further choice of homotopy class for this disk in the 7-type. This builds a substitution with the given map after truncation. Equivalently the construction matches the two maps into the Postnikov 7-section by induction on the attaching globes. The inclusion into the Postnikov section is 8-connected, so suspending \(n\) times makes it at least \((8+n)\)-connected. In particular the substitution induces the intended map on \(\pi_8\Sigma^nK\). Higher declarations can be omitted for this degree by the truncation argument of Response 153.

Now project a nonzero shell to one of its nonzero 4-sphere coordinates. Because the wedge splitting was assumed **before suspension**, this projection comes from a based map to \(S^d\), followed by inclusion of \(S^d\) in the local realization of the finite presentation. In the other direction use the retraction of that realization onto \(S^d\) followed by inclusion of the desired summand in \(K\). Both maps have the raw substitutions just proved. Shift the substitutions by \(n\) at the blank and retain the selected stationary colour. Shell scanning is natural in these label maps. Substitution therefore carries an assumed published comparison in either presentation to a comparison of the nonzero \(\tau\) in the other, with raw fits to the chosen representative. This proves the uniform equivalence.

Raw substitution specializes those checks to coincident ends and previously constructed faces. The Python audit constructs the cellular differentials in both finite presentations, checks each successive boundary square and eliminates the integral unit pivots in reverse order after changing basis on the final opposite disks. It recovers the original sphere and the stated top ranks. The homotopy equivalence uses the attaching disks described above. The independent low-stem checker takes the cited sphere data as input and exercises both degree-eight coordinates. **Published insertion and the other five surfaces of Response 48 reflect in every degree on any point-site history with at most two structural uses in each pruned host face.** There is no bound on the number of free probes, the number of host faces, the occupancy of their two ends, or the number of original uses pruned to this form. Without probes, an independent pair of structural uses always has contractible fixed-end components, for all ten surfaces.

Suppress free sites in a named scalar face. For two independent proper uses, the same-sign packet cases follow from Response 156 and opposite caps from Response 157. Two uses with both ports nonempty are covered by the positive scalar theorem. The remaining case, allowing reversal, is a proper birth independent of a positive replacement. In the birth-first order the middle cut contains both the new packet and the input packet of the replacement. The map from the tie to this order is fully faithful on the coefficient with outside ends varying. Indeed the two serial site motions agree after cabling these two disjoint nonempty blocks. Keeping one representative of each gives the joint motion, and retaining either whole block recovers the corresponding serial motion, exactly as in Response 55. Its proof uses only these middle expansions. Pulling back at the two outside configurations and their paths preserves identification with a union of components. Both fixed-end serial coefficients have contractible components in this case: the last site has nonempty output, so the fixed final end forces its loop to vanish; the seam then forces the first loop to vanish by its nonempty output. Both are iterated pullbacks of 1-types. The two-order pushout consequently gives the other order plus the unmatched components of the birth-first order, all homotopy discrete. Reversal treats an independent positive replacement and death. A single remaining proper site has at least one injective end expansion, giving the same conclusion. [Two-site coefficient comparison](#researcher-response-55) · [Positive scalar networks](../answered/semistrict-surface-conservativity-2026-11-24.md#researcher-response-82)

For dependent uses run the signed chain test of Response 128. The unmarked component is aspherical and its group is zero except possibly for a closed birth/death return using every born leaf and no initial leaf. There it is free on the throughs if the signed seam preserves the packet disk up to the specified grouping, and zero otherwise. Let \(r\) be this structural free rank, assigning zero in all the contractible cases. For \(k\) probes, let \(L\) be the graph of the structural trace with **all** exterior tips attached to one vertex at infinity (present even with no tips). Its cycle rank \(s=|E(L)|-|V(L)|+|\pi_0 L|\) equals the first Betti number of the one-probe complement by Alexander duality. After pruning and suppressing point events every interior vertex has degree at least two. A component away from infinity with an edge therefore contains a cycle. In the component of infinity any nonempty tree would have a leaf distinct from infinity, also impossible. Hence \(s>0\) for every nonempty remaining trace, including through-only traces. At an empty trace the complement is the open slab with trivial group.

The split fibration of Response 79 now gives the exact existential degree-five test
\[
                         r>0\quad\text{or}\quad k s>0.
\]
The fibre group is one copy of the complement group per named probe since pair diagonals have codimension three, and its inclusion is injective. No freeness assumption on the complement group enters this test. Apply it face by face using the product of Response 142. In particular the test distinguishes an entangled closed return with trivial structural group from the same return carrying a probe. For the six-surface conclusion, first test the unmarked structural difference. Its only possible nonzero group in positive degrees is the dependent return group in degree five. In that case all its moving wires run from its birth to its death. On the raw structural loop this reads precisely the first marker around the throughs, which is faithful by the chain equations. At transient ends keep the enclosing boundary strand and its caps as in Response 143. The resulting one-point configuration in the swept interior injects on fundamental groups in the flat scalar test by the retained-arc comparison; fixed written ends can use the same exterior collars. These substitutions take a surface witness to a scalar witness. Scalar conservativity for the six surfaces forces the reading to vanish. Once the unmarked difference vanishes, the original difference comes from the full probe configuration fibre. Keep the original reduced structure, probes and enclosing arc for this second scalar test. ### The group at the forced cut

The incidence condition forces every birth before every death. The ordered-partition diagram factors at the middle cut: choose the two schedules independently and join their moving ends by a path in \(\mathrm{Conf}_n(\mathbb R^2)\), where \(n\) is the number of middle strands. The two homotopy colimits can be taken separately since homotopy pullback in spaces preserves colimits in each slice. For each half the moving-end map is the inclusion of the packet subgroup of Response 156 on fundamental groups, between connected 1-types. Let \(D_L,D_R\) denote those subgroups in the opening and closing coordinates, and \(\beta\) the braid from the opening grouping to the closing grouping. The components of the pullback are the double cosets (at matching names), and the group of the specified component in opening coordinates is
\[
                    D_L\ \cap\ \beta D_R\beta^{-1}.
\]
A proposed based middle loop is realized exactly when it passes *both* packet-disk tests in the transported coordinates. In that case it fills at degree five precisely when the middle braid is trivial. This also gives the same intersection test at a forced cut with throughs using each half's corresponding group and exterior transports. For empty exterior ends a single packet on either side has trivial group. [Independent schedule colimits at a cut](#researcher-response-50) · [Packet membership](#researcher-response-156)

Cap the boundary of the middle disk by a disk marked at infinity \(z\), then fill \(z\). Write \(K_n\) for the pure braids acting trivially on the resulting \(n\)-punctured sphere. Capping has central kernel generated by the full twist \(Z\). The next kernel is point-pushing of \(z\), the free group \(\pi_1(S_{0,n},z)=F_{n-1}\) for \(n\ge4\). Thus \(K_n\) is a central extension of this free group by \(\mathbb Z\), split after choosing lifts of its free generators. A twist \(U_i\) around all terminal punctures except \(i\) lifts a peripheral push about \(i\): on the sphere with \(z\) marked its curve bounds the other disk containing just \(z,i\). Choose peripheral stems forming a meridian system; the first \(n-1\) supply the free basis. On the terminal meridians with the sphere relation \(x_1\cdots x_n=1\), a braid in \(K_n\) acts by conjugation by its infinity push, up to the convention for inversion. Conversely an inner action detects membership in \(K_n\) by the faithful outer action of the punctured-sphere mapping class group. [Capping and the action on meridians, Farb–Margalit, §§3.7, 8.1 and 9.2](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/~a019210/Farb%20Magalit_Primer%20on%20Teichmuller%20theory.pdf) · [Point-pushing sequence](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0611241)

For **either** empty-ended packet half, every element of \(K_n\) preserves the packet disk kernel of Response 156. Indeed \(x_1\cdots x_n=1\) already holds in the trace quotient, as the product of the packet relations. Conjugation therefore sends each packet relation to the identity in that quotient. This works after every change of middle coordinates since filling infinity is equivariant. It remains only to enforce the internal braid conditions in each packet.

For \(b,d\ge2\) every packet is a proper subset of the middle strands. Build a commutator word on \(U_1,\ldots,U_n\) containing each once as an input to a bracket. First bracket the first \(n-1\) in two recursively disjoint sublists and then bracket that result with \(U_n\). The first word projects to a nontrivial word in the free peripheral basis: nontrivial words on disjoint basis sets cannot commute. It has zero abelianization, whereas the last peripheral has primitive nonzero abelianization. Their cyclic centralizers in a free group show the final commutator is nontrivial. On deleting strand \(i\), \(U_i\) becomes the central full twist of the remaining strands; consequently the whole bracket becomes the identity. In particular all internal restrictions vanish for *both* partitions, also after any seam transport. The intersection calculation realizes this element at the specified history. Its restricted track contracts already in the space where the two phases are kept in order: deleting one strand leaves all packets nonempty by complete incidence, both half maps still inject, and the middle reading is trivial. Allowing other schedules on the restricted history preserves the filler.

### The exact four-strand calculation

Label the two lower pairs \(12,34\). Connectivity of the binary plat is exactly the condition that the matching of the upper pairs, pulled back by \(\beta\), differs from this matching. Every lower pair therefore meets every upper pair. On the filled four-punctured sphere the two lower disks have the same boundary class \(c_L\); the upper disks give a distinct class \(c_R\) since the induced partitions differ. For either half the filled compressing-disk complex has a single vertex. Indeed every essential compressing curve separates the two pairs, and disjoint curves doing so are isotopic on this sphere. The complex is discrete and contractible by the disk argument of Response 156. The respective packet subgroups therefore preserve \(c_L,c_R\). A pure mapping class fixing one of these curves is a power of its twist: cutting produces two pairs of pants with no remaining interior mapping class fixing the boundary labels. Distinct essential curves on this sphere intersect, so no nonzero power of the first twist preserves the second. The intersection thus lies in \(K_4\). Conversely for elements of \(K_4\) only the four matched-pair linking numbers need vanish, since \(PB_2\cong\mathbb Z\).

Relabel the upper pairs \(13,24\). In \(K_4\) use \(Z\) and lifts \(U_1,U_2,U_3\) of the free basis. If their exponent readings are \(t,e_1,e_2,e_3\), put \(e_4=0\). The linking of \(i,j\) is \(t+\sum_{h\notin\{i,j\}}e_h\), since \(U_h\) turns precisely the triple omitting \(h\). Setting the four required readings to zero gives \(e_1=0,\ e_2=e_3=-t\). Thus projection to \(F_3\) identifies the structural group with the kernel of the surjection onto \(\mathbb Z^2\) which reads \((e_1,e_2-e_3)\). The central coordinate is uniquely recovered there. This kernel is free of countably infinite rank: its covering of the three-circle rose has deck group \(\mathbb Z^2\), and the commutator of two generators with independent images gives cycles with infinitely many disjoint translates. Its graph is countable. If an individual surface kills some nonidentity element, its filling subgroup is normal by composing and conjugating tracks; reversing the raw differences also gives inverses by whiskering a comparison and using the available reverse comparison in this generator-free top dimension. A nonzero normal subgroup of a countably infinite-rank free group cannot be generated by a finite list: conjugate a nonidentity word by a basis letter outside the supports of the whole list. This last conclusion is conditional on the surface filler; the Brunnian calculation itself is a raw nonfilling.

## Researcher Response 161

**For each complete-incidence packet plat of Response 160, degree-five reflection on *all* named structural tracks is equivalent to reflection on a single subgroup of Brunnian point pushes.** At fixed middle strand count \(n\) the subgroup is the same for every signed seam and every such pair of packet partitions, in the given opening coordinates. The equivalence holds separately for each binary interchange surface. One may also intersect the testing subgroup with *any prescribed term* of the structural group's lower central series. Consequently any actual surface failure here forces infinitely many independent failures invisible to single-strand deletion and to nilpotent quotients of any specified bounded class. This reduces the surface test; existence of a raw Brunnian nonfilling alone does not decide it.

Assume both phases have at least two packets (otherwise the structural group is trivial). Write \(G\le PB_n\) for the middle intersection and \(F=\pi_1(S_{0,n},z)\) for the meridian group based at infinity. Its basis is represented by the peripheral pushes \(u_1,\ldots,u_{n-1}\) of Response 160. Fix the Brunnian braid \(W\) constructed there, using a balanced bracket on the first \(n-1\) peripheral lifts and then bracketing with the last. Write \(w\in F\) for its nonidentity push. Let \(L_n\) be the subgroup generated by all conjugates of \(W\) by lifts of elements of \(F\) to the disk braid group. The choice of central lift does not affect conjugation. Every such conjugate lies in every \(G\) under consideration: it is a point push after capping, fixes all filled disk relations, and its restrictions to proper strand sets vanish. Projection to \(F\) identifies \(L_n\) with the normal closure of \(w\); its kernel could only be a full twist, whose nonzero powers survive pair restriction. This lets one enumerate its elements by products of peripheral conjugates of this one explicit braid.

Here is a constructive conversion of a failure. Put \(w'=u_1wu_1^{-1}\). The elements \(w,w'\) do not commute: a nontrivial cyclic subgroup generated by a root in a free group is malnormal, and \(u_1\) cannot centralize \(w\), by their abelianizations and cyclic centralizers. Use the two corresponding braid lifts \(W,W'\) in \(L_n\), and their conjugates by the \(n-1\) peripheral lifts. If the induced based sphere automorphism \(\alpha\) of a realized track fixes all these push words in \(F\), it fixes \(w,w'\). Fixing their two conjugates by \(u_i\) then forces \(u_i^{-1}\alpha(u_i)\) to centralize both. Their common centralizer is trivial, so \(\alpha\) fixes each basis element. The based action of the punctured-disk braid group on the filled sphere group has kernel exactly the central full twist: first pass to the outer action, then apply the point-pushing sequence and the trivial centre of \(F\). Every packet has at least two tips by complete incidence. Its internal reading therefore excludes nonidentity central elements from \(G\).

Given a realized nonidentity \(g\in G\), some listed partner \(S\) consequently gives a nontrivial commutator \([g,S]\), with push \(\alpha(s)s^{-1}\) for the push \(s\) of \(S\). It is Brunnian since \(S\) disappears under every proper restriction. It now lies in the point-pushing extension. Bracket once more with whichever of \(W,W'\) fails to commute with this nonzero push. This second commutator belongs to \(L_n\): conjugation by the first commutator is conjugation by a lift of an element of \(F\). It is still nonzero. Repeating stays in \(L_n\) and raises lower central depth in \(G\) at every step. If the initial difference has a surface comparison, each new commutator has one by whiskering and pasting that comparison at the same base history, since every selected partner is itself a realized raw track. The same statement follows by normality of the surface filling subgroup \(H\) from Response 160. Thus for every fixed \(r\ge1\),
\[
        H=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
        H\cap L_n\cap\gamma_r(G)=1.
\]
The implication is about reflection on the whole specified history. Testing an arbitrary individual commutator for a filler is not a decision procedure for the original track.

When this intersection is nonzero it is an infinitely generated free group. Indeed \(L_n\) is a nontrivial infinite-index normal subgroup of a finite-rank nonabelian free group (the seed has zero abelianization), hence is free of infinite rank. For the rank assertion, in the normal covering of a finite rose translate a finite cycle by infinitely many deck transformations with disjoint supports; this gives infinitely many independent cycles. The displayed intersection is normal in \(L_n\) and now the fresh-basis-letter argument of Response 160 applies. One can additionally require invisibility to any finite list of finite group tests on \(G\): raise a resulting nontrivial point push to a common multiple of the finite target group orders. It stays nontrivial by torsion-freeness. The procedure uses a proposed surface filler only by composition and hence preserves the surface being tested.

**Reproduce.** Run `python3 -B tools/semistrict_surface_plat_brunnian.py` and `python3 -B tools/semistrict_surface_plat_tracks.py`. On a four-strand track with nonzero unmatched-pair winding and on the Brunnian seed itself, the converter selects partners through three successive depths. It checks the actual iterated braid word by its sphere action and verifies triviality after each individual strand deletion. The seed input exercises the case in which bracketing with itself fails. A six-strand rectangular example tests the depth-two conversion. A JSON query with `lower`, `upper`, `seam`, `track`, and optional `depth` first checks complete incidence and membership at both packet ends; the output gives the successive Artin-word partners and the final nonzero reduced push. [Brunnian conversion](../../../tools/semistrict_surface_plat_brunnian.py) · [Middle-cut and sphere action](../../../tools/semistrict_surface_plat_tracks.py)

## Researcher Response 162

**For each binary interchange surface, degree-six reflection on arbitrary independent births of rank-three scalars is equivalent to two cyclic tests at one history.** Take one generating 3-scalar \(a\), one 4-rule from the empty row to \(a*a\), and use the rule twice, starting empty. At the four named terminal positions test (i) multiples of the pair sphere on the two leaves of the first birth and (ii) multiples of the pair sphere on one leaf from each birth. Reflection on the whole class holds exactly when neither test admits a surface filler at any nonzero multiple. Packet sizes, numbers of uses, through scalars and repetitions of names in the original context are unrestricted. At rank \(n\ge3\) the same result holds in degree \(2n\), with lower degrees already settled by round-one Response 104. There is also a five-integer description below for individual boundaries. These are tests of the binary surfaces themselves. Published insertion is already known on scalar-rule computads. [Occurrence lifts and lower range](../answered/semistrict-surface-conservativity-2026-11-24.md#researcher-response-104) · [Scalar insertion](../answered/semistrict-surface-conservativity-2026-11-24.md#researcher-response-108)

### Terminal sphere coordinates

Work on an ordinary scalar-rule computation with \(m\) through occurrences and independent births of positive sizes \(p_1,\ldots,p_b\). Use distinct occurrence names and group the terminal row into throughs and ordered packets. Denote the total length by \(l\) and put \(\epsilon=(-1)^n\). In \(\pi_{n-1}\mathrm{Conf}_l(\mathbb R^n)\) write \(e_{ij}\) for the pair sphere with the direction from \(i\) to \(j\); \(e_{ji}=\epsilon e_{ij}\). One orientation for each pair gives an integral basis by the successive point-forgetting fibrations with sections. The space of histories at the written ends is the homotopy fibre of terminal evaluation from the moving-end space. Both moving-end and terminal spaces are \((n-2)\)-connected. The named group testing old degree \(2n\) is therefore the cokernel of the map on \(\pi_{n-1}\), including at \(n=3\) where this gives an abelian fundamental group of the fixed-end history space. A vector of terminal pair spheres represents the tested difference by the connecting map. Signed end transports just transport names and orientations.

For the connectivity and image assertions one may straighten the based through paths with variable ends, whose space is contractible, and work with stationary throughs. In a schedule extend the previous batches by the last batch of site markers. Forgetting the markers is a configuration fibration over the expanded previous cut. Its fibre is the configuration of the new markers in the complement of the earlier tips and the throughs. In this fibre \(\pi_{n-1}\) is generated by new-marker/old-tip, new-marker/through and new-marker/new-marker spheres, again by point deletion. Earlier spheres lift with the later sites parked outside a large ball over a compact representative. This gives connectivity by induction and generates the terminal image for that schedule. Across schedules the ordered-partition flag complex is contractible. The homotopy colimit remains \((n-2)\)-connected (equivalently use van Kampen and the homology spectral sequence). In total degree \(n-1\) the constant bottom row has no positive homology on the index, and all coefficient rows strictly between zero and \(n-1\) vanish. The schedule groups therefore generate by Hurewicz. This image calculation does not assert injectivity of the terminal map.

Expanding each new marker in parallel turns its pair sphere with an old tip into the sum of the spheres from that tip to *all* its new leaves. Simultaneous new markers give the sum on a whole packet rectangle. Every through and each individual leaf of a different packet can be old by choosing the order. Consequently the cokernel has the following integral blocks.

- Through/through and within-packet entries are free, one per unordered pair.
- A through/packet row is taken modulo the constant row.
- A cross-packet matrix is taken modulo all constant rows and all constant columns. The rectangle relation is their sum.

In the last two blocks choose the last leaf as anchor. The differences against the anchor, respectively the rectangular differences \(a_{ij}-a_{uj}-a_{iv}+a_{uv}\) at anchors \(u,v\), give free coordinates. This follows integrally by subtracting rows and columns until the anchor entries vanish. In particular the two-binary-birth test history has group \(\mathbb Z^3\), with two internal coordinates and one rectangular coordinate. [Schedule model and pair expansion](../answered/semistrict-surface-conservativity-2026-11-24.md#researcher-response-82)

### Five cyclic subgroups for the value on a particular boundary

For a fixed rank and surface record the subgroup of \(\mathbb Z\) whose multiples of one terminal pair sphere fill in each of these small histories. They are subgroups by addition, top reversal and the raw inverse difference. The orientation convention does not affect subgroup membership. Each listed leaf is a separate occurrence.

| Coordinate | Small history | Chosen pair |
|---|---|---|
| Through pair | Two throughs | The two throughs |
| Binary internal | One two-tip birth | Its two leaves |
| Ternary internal | One three-tip birth | Its first two leaves |
| Through/packet | One through and one two-tip birth | The through and the first leaf |
| Between packets | Two two-tip births | The first leaf of each |

For a terminal vector the exact filling criterion is membership of **every** coordinate in the corresponding subgroup. Use the through pairs directly. Use the anchored differences above for through/packet and between packets. Within a packet with anchor \(u\), the binary internal coordinates are \(a_{iu}\); the ternary internal coordinates are \(a_{ij}-a_{iu}-\epsilon a_{ju}\) for \(i<j<u\). An absent block contributes no test.

Here are both directions, since coordinate deletion alone need not reconstruct a filler at the original ports. Name the events and wires, erase unused marks and send an event with no retained ports to the point-only fit. On terminal spheres this deletes the missing pair entries. Conversely a witness can be placed with other throughs and other births fixed in disjoint regions, using the fixed actions at its written ends. A substitution may expand one leaf of a small rule to an ordered list, sending its birth to the actual large birth with the port-order fits. It cables the terminal pair by summing over the two lists; any fixed grouping permutation is undone at the end. These placements work with separately named leaves before folding. At dimension \(2n\) the surface occurrence lift supplies the required names on a proposed comparison.

In particular, retaining just \(i,u\) proves necessity of the binary internal test. Placing that binary witness back with \(i\) singleton and the other side the rest of the packet gives its multiple of \(\sum_{j\ne i}e_{ij}\). On retaining \(i,j,u\), subtract the two such placed binary contributions. The remaining single-pair coefficient at \(i,j\) is exactly the stated ternary coordinate, proving its necessity. Conversely the binary placements recover all anchor entries in the large packet. For a ternary witness expand its third leaf to the remainder, keeping its two tested leaves single; this places the residual single-pair coefficient itself. Through pairs are obtained by restriction and fixed placement. With a through and two leaves restrict first and subtract the internal component already known to fill. The remaining quotient coordinate is the through/packet difference. For two packets retain a chosen leaf and the anchor in each, then subtract the two internal components. The remaining quotient is the rectangular difference. Both kinds of residual witnesses place back using one distinguished singleton per tested packet and expanding the other leaf to its remainder. Summing these placed comparisons reconstructs the original class by the integral blocks. Use raw comparisons to fit the result to the two given representatives of that class. This proves sufficiency too.

### Why the two tests at empty input suffice for uniform reflection

Any nonzero through/packet multiple that fills gives the same nonzero between-packet multiple: pad by one through beside its through, then prefix a binary birth creating that pair. The original packet birth now supplies the other pair. For a through/through multiple, pad the two throughs by one neighbour each and prefix two births so the selected throughs belong to distinct packets. Their single cross entry has the same nonzero rectangular reading. A nonzero ternary internal multiple that fills yields a binary internal one by forgetting the third leaf. Finally a binary internal witness can be padded by a disjoint second binary birth, without changing its internal coordinate. Thus any failure in the five tests gives a nonzero multiple on one of the two indicated axes at the *same* four-tip history. Conversely such a failure there is already in the class. Folding the four names to \(a\) and the births to the same declaration preserves raw nonfilling by the occurrence cover, with the named boundary lifts fixed at the chosen history. These arguments prove the two-test reduction without assigning values to the two unknown subgroups.

**Reproduce.** Run `python3 -B tools/semistrict_surface_spatial_packets.py`. The audit expands the point-forgetting generators in all serial orders, checks the simultaneous rectangles, and reconstructs 198 terminal pair generators as integral sums of actual small packet placements and schedule relations. It uses both antipodal signs, up to three packets, singleton leaves and two throughs. JSON input accepts `rank`, `through`, `packets` and oriented triples `pairs` of two zero-based tip indices and a multiplicity. It returns unconditional raw nullity and the five coordinate lists. Supplying the five subgroup generators as `moduli` also evaluates the conditional surface criterion; zero denotes the trivial subgroup. [Spatial packet solver](../../../tools/semistrict_surface_spatial_packets.py)

## Researcher Response 163

**Published insertion reflects in degree seven for every reversible rank-two presentation of Response 153 at that degree, including arbitrary connected label spaces with torsion.** At any stationary rank \(n\ge2\) there is an exact calculation in the first shell degree outside Freudenthal's injectivity range. For an even-dimensional bottom homology group, its 2-primary cyclic summands each contribute one independent order-two raw difference invisible to all homotopy-type evaluations. This can already happen in degree ten at stationary rank three. In odd bottom dimension only specified Whitehead squares need testing. In bottom dimensions three and seven they all vanish.

Let \(Y=\Sigma^n K\) be \((m-1)\)-connected, \(m\ge n+1\), with \(K\) the connected realization of the finite local presentation. Set \(A=H_m(Y;\mathbb Z)=\pi_mY\). Take \(i=2m-2\), so the shell lies in \(\pi_{2m-1}Y\) and the requested old filler has degree \(n+2m-1\). Impose the local reversibility of Response 153 through this test. Choose a cyclic decomposition of \(A\), with generators \(x_j\) of orders \(q_j\), writing zero for infinite order. At one named puncture the group \(T_{n,i}(Y)\) of Response 158 is as follows.

| Bottom dimension | Generators of the exact kernel in \(\pi_{2m-1}Y\) |
|---|---|
| \(m\) even | \((q_j/2)[x_j,x_j]\) for each finite even \(q_j\). These are independent of order two. |
| \(m\) odd | \([x_j,x_j]\) for the free and even-order summands. Take their actual span in \(\pi_{2m-1}Y\). For \(m=3,7\) the span is zero. |

Thus for even \(m\) with no 2-torsion in \(A\), or for \(m=3,7\) with arbitrary \(A\), every old boundary reflects in this degree. Taking \(m=n+1\) gives the degree-seven assertion at \(n=2\) and degree nineteen at \(n=6\). For odd \(m=n+1\) outside \(3,7\), if \(H_1K\) has no even torsion, the group is exactly \((\mathbb Z/2)^{\operatorname{rank}H_1K}\). Over all such local presentations with positive rank and a stationary colour, **one fixed old comparison per \(n\)** decides reflection in this degree. [Local reversal and written boundaries](#researcher-response-153) · [Exact one-puncture test](#researcher-response-158)

### Computing the kernel with smash powers

In fact the homotopy-type test in every shell degree can be read in finitely many smash powers of \(V=\Sigma^{n-1}K\). For \(\alpha\in\pi_{i+1}Y\), let \(u:S^i\to\Omega Y\simeq JV\) be its adjoint and let \(h_r(\alpha)\) be \(Eu\) followed by the projection of the James splitting \(\Sigma JV\simeq\bigvee_{r\ge1}\Sigma V^{\wedge r}\) onto its length-\(r\) factor. The length-one map is evaluation, so \(h_1(\alpha)=\alpha\). Then
\[
 \alpha\in T_{n,i}(Y)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 E^{n-1}h_r(\alpha)=0\quad
 \text{for every }1\le r\le \lfloor i/(m-1)\rfloor.
\]
Indeed \(V\) is simply connected and has no reduced homology below \(m-1\), hence is \((m-2)\)-connected. Use CW models with their first positive cells in dimension \(m-1\). Only finitely many summands meet the source dimension. One more suspension of a sphere map into a wedge is the sum of its suspended projections followed by the inclusions. To see this, the sum of the suspended inclusion-projection maps on the suspended wedge restricts to its identity on each summand. Precomposing by a suspended map preserves the sum by naturality of the pinch map. Since \(n\ge2\), this applies after the James splitting regardless of any mixed Whitehead components before this extra suspension. Retractions detect the resulting coordinates separately. [James, *Reduced Product Spaces*](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/jamesred.pdf)

At \(i=2m-2\) only lengths one and two remain. Freudenthal on \(\Sigma Y\) shows that the first reading is zero precisely when \(E\alpha=0\). Its kernel is generated integrally by products \([x,y]\) of bottom classes. Indeed \(Y\to JY\simeq\Omega\Sigma Y\) induces suspension, and its relative homotopy in degree \(2m\) is \(H_{2m}(JY,Y)=A\otimes A\) by relative Hurewicz. The length-two quotient is \(Y\wedge Y\), and length three first contributes in dimension \(3m\). For spherical generators \(x,y\) use the product of their representing spheres in the length-two stage. Its relative class is \(x\otimes y\), and the attaching boundary after folding the wedge of its axes into \(Y\) is \([x,y]\).

On this subgroup the second reading of \([x,y]\), with consistent orientations, is
\[
              x\otimes y+(-1)^m y\otimes x\ \in A\otimes A .
\]
It is a *bottom* Hurewicz reading in \(\Sigma^n(V\wedge V)\), so it suffices integrally. To check the formula with torsion, represent \(x,y\) by suspending bottom spheres of \(V\), possible by Hurewicz and homology suspension. The adjoint product has the Samelson commutator of those two bottom maps. Its Hurewicz image is the graded commutator of their Pontryagin products. On the second James filtration quotient the ordered product of two bottom classes maps to their tensor by the relative cross product. The length-two projection of the splitting induces this quotient on these classes, and reduced homology suspension preserves their coefficients. This only uses the bottom Künneth group of the smash, so no freeness assumption on \(A\) is needed. [James filtration and product](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/jamesred.pdf)

For distinct cyclic generators combine the bracket in the opposite order by graded symmetry. Its coefficient is now read in the ordered tensor coordinate of the pair. If this is zero, the bracket multiple itself is zero by bilinearity, including for finite orders with a common divisor. On a diagonal the coefficient is doubled for \(m\) even and vanishes for \(m\) odd. In the even case this gives exactly the candidate multiples in the first row. In the odd case the square is killed both by two and by any finite order of its input, which gives the second row. Conversely each listed class has zero first and second readings. When \(m=3,7\) the multiplication of unit quaternions or unit octonions extends the fold of \(S^m\vee S^m\) over the product, so the universal square vanishes. All its images vanish by naturality.

### Why the even-dimensional classes are genuinely independent

For each even \(q_j\) write \(q_j=2^a b\) with \(b\) odd and put \(Q=2^a\). Take the class \(c_j\in H^m(Y;\mathbb Z/Q)\) which sends \(x_j\) to one and the other bottom generators to zero. It exists by universal coefficients. Its Pontryagin square in \(H^{2m}(Y;\mathbb Z/2Q)\) is zero because \(Y\) is a double suspension. More explicitly the once-desuspended operation is the Postnikov square, a coefficient image of a class cupped with its integral Bockstein. At the second desuspension this cup product vanishes on a suspension. On an integral lift the Pontryagin square is ordinary cup square reduced modulo \(2Q\). [Thomas, Theorem I, equation (2.1) and §6](https://msp.org/pjm/1959/9-3/pjm-v9-n3-p26-s.pdf)

If a nonempty sum of candidate classes vanished, take one \(S^m\times S^m\) for each term and form their oriented connected sum. Its punctured part retracts onto the wedge of the two axes of each factor, and its top cell attaches by the sum of the corresponding Whitehead products. This follows by joining the punctured products along boundary disks, which pinches the final attaching sphere onto the individual attaching spheres with their induced orientations. Map the two axes of the \(j\)-th pair by \(x_j,(q_j/2)x_j\). The assumed relation extends this wedge map to the connected sum. For any participating \(j\), the pullback of \(c_j\) now lifts integrally to the sum of the two dual classes on that factor with coefficients \(1,q_j/2\). Their squares are zero and their mixed pairing in either order is one since \(m\) is even. Its integral square on the fundamental class is \(q_j\equiv Q\bmod 2Q\), contradicting naturality of the zero Pontryagin square. Bilinearity already kills twice each candidate. This proves independence and the exact first row, even with arbitrary higher attaching maps in \(K\).

For example take \(n=3,m=4\), one stationary colour and a local circle \(z\) with one 2-generator from \(z^2\) to the identity. Complete this presentation through local rank \(i=6\) as in Response 158: process each original positive generator and each new round-trip witness through rank six, then add opposites to all rank-seven witnesses. Every inverse and its own round-trip disk form a relative elementary expansion, and the remaining opposite disks add spheres in rank seven. Thus \(H_1K=\mathbb Z/2\) and the required reversibility holds. At degree ten the shell \([x,x]\) of its bottom 4-class is an actual nonzero order-two raw difference. The Pontryagin calculation excludes a raw filler. Every homotopy-type evaluation admits a filler. This gives a single unresolved published comparison already at the first unstable degree for a label space with torsion.

### Uniform cyclic tests at odd stationary rank

There is a natural form of the first row, valid for every even \(m\) above. Write \(A[2^a]\) for the subgroup killed by \(2^a\), with \(A[1]=0\). Then
\[
 T_{n,2m-2}(Y)\ \cong\
 \bigoplus_{a\ge1}\frac{A[2^a]}{A[2^{a-1}]+2A[2^{a+1}]} .
\]
The map from the \(a\)-th summand sends \(x\) to \(2^{a-1}[x,x]\). On \(A[2^a]\) this is additive, since the two equal mixed terms give \(2^a[x,y]=0\). It kills elements of order dividing \(2^{a-1}\), and on \(2z\) it gives \(2^{a+1}[z,z]=0\) for \(z\in A[2^{a+1}]\). On a primary cyclic decomposition the displayed quotient has one binary coordinate for each summand of *exact* order \(2^a\). Its images are precisely the independent elements proved above. The formula therefore respects arbitrary induced homomorphisms on bottom homology, including maps that mix cyclic summands.

Specialize to \(m=n+1\) with \(n\) odd. **In degree \(3n+1\), published reflection on all the reversible presentations of Response 153 is equivalent to one comparison on a finite cyclic presentation for each \(q=2^a\), \(a\ge1\).** If the 2-primary exponent of the abelianizations is bounded by \(2^b\), reflection throughout the bounded class holds if and only if all of the first \(b\) tests reflect. The cyclic test uses a single stationary colour and a local presentation \(D_q\) whose homotopy \(i\)-type is \(B(\mathbb Z/q)\), with \(i=2n\). At the standard row compare the shell \((q/2)[x,x]\) to zero for the bottom generator \(x\). Its raw comparison fails by the Pontryagin square above.

Here is one existence construction of each **finite** \(D_q\). Begin with the circle and the relation \(z^q\to1\), completed by the finite inverse and round-trip construction through \(i\). Its fundamental group is cyclic of order \(q\). Successively for \(2\le r\le i\) kill \(\pi_r\) of the current realization by finitely many \((r+1)\)-disks. Indeed the universal cover is finite and \((r-1)\)-connected at that stage, so \(\pi_r\) is its finitely generated integral \(H_r\). In the reversible local truncation represent the chosen based sphere generators by raw \(r\)-cells at iterated identity faces and adjoin a comparison of each to the identity. This is the local prescribed-face groupoid comparison used in Response 153, applied to \(D\) itself before shifting ranks. Complete each new positive generator and its subsequent witnesses through rank \(i\), and add opposite witnesses in rank \(i+1\). If the killing disk is itself in rank \(i+1\), simply adjoin its opposite. Relative to the killing disks these attachments are elementary expansions and wedges of spheres of dimension \(i+1\), by the free-face argument of Response 158. They preserve the calculation through \(r\). The disk attachments kill the chosen group and its deck translates and keep all lower groups. This produces the claimed finite truncated model, independently of any choice of a finite-dimensional aspherical model.

The choices of killing disks can also be made by a terminating search. Use the cyclic cover with vertices the residues modulo \(q\), lifting every declaration once at each starting vertex. The initial generator advances one residue, its assigned inverses go back one, and every relation preserves its two endpoint residues. Compute the cellular boundary of a lifted declaration as the chain of its written target minus that of its source. For a path, traverse its lifted edges in order. In higher positive degree the top cellular chain of a writing counts its lifted generators. On an arity disk the ordinary total has coefficient one on each top slot, lower-dimensional slots contribute zero, and substitution replaces each disk by its labelled chain with its specified starting vertex. This also follows by lifting the characteristic disks to the cover and collapsing the preceding skeleton before taking degrees. Now enumerate based raw \(r\)-spheres at the identity and read their cycles at residue zero. Using integer Smith reduction, stop when the chosen cycles span the homology in rank \(r\) modulo cellular boundaries. The local groupoid comparison and the Hurewicz isomorphism used above ensure termination at each stage. The search constructs the finite presentation used for the subsequent published comparison.

A failed comparison in an arbitrary reversible context yields a nonzero surface-null shell at one puncture. The natural formula supplies a projection \(H_1K\to\mathbb Z/q\) for which its image is the nonzero cyclic class. The character is induced by a based map \(K\to B(\mathbb Z/q)\). Interpret this as a map of \(i\)-types to the \(i\)-type of \(D_q\). The cell-by-cell argument of Response 158 represents it by a raw substitution through local rank \(i+1\): realize each disk at its already matched faces and use top reachability at the last rank. The \(n\)-suspended Postnikov map is \((i+n+1)\)-connected, so the effect on the shell in \(\pi_{i+1}\) is precisely the one just computed. Keep the stationary colour. An existing published filler therefore gives one in the cyclic test. Conversely, any cyclic test admitting a filler is itself a counterexample in the specified class. This implication does not require that a character into \(\mathbb Z/q\) admit a section in an arbitrary fundamental group.

There is an individual-context classification in terms of these same binary answers when the local \(i\)-type is \(BG\) for a finitely generated abelian \(G\). With at least one stationary colour, its surface-null subgroup is the direct sum of the coordinates belonging to the orders \(q\) whose cyclic test fills. Projections give necessity, while inclusion of each primary cyclic summand of \(G\) induces a reverse substitution on the \(i\)-types for sufficiency. Add the resulting one-coordinate comparisons as in Response 158. No cyclic test of a different 2-power exponent detects the distinguished class by a bottom-label homomorphism: the exact-order quotient for that exponent in the target is zero. This distinguishes the detecting substitutions without asserting logical independence of the unresolved published judgments.

The uniform test extends to **every even \(m\ge n+1\)** in the table. Put \(d=m-n\). Use a local tester with \(i\)-type \(K(\mathbb Z/q,d)\), and take the shell on the suspended bottom generator. A cyclic coordinate of \(A=H_dK\) lifts by universal coefficients to a cohomology class in \(H^d(K;\mathbb Z/q)\), hence to a map \(K\to K(\mathbb Z/q,d)\). The induced map of the exact-order quotients retains the specified shell. This proves the same all-context equivalence at degree \(n+2m-1\) and the same bounded-exponent assertion. For a local \(i\)-type \(K(G,d)\) with \(G\) finitely generated abelian the primary summand inclusions again give the individual-context classification.

For completeness, finite reversible testers exist also for \(d>1\). Start from a single local \(d\)-sphere and attach a \((d+1)\)-disk from the \(q\)-fold temporal product to the identity. Complete the generators through rank \(i\) as above. Its realization is simply connected with bottom homotopy \(\mathbb Z/q\), and the extra top spheres leave that group fixed. For \(d<r\le i\) choose a finite generating set of the current \(\pi_r\), finitely generated by the finiteness theorem for homotopy groups of simply connected finite CW complexes. Realize and kill it by raw cells and complete their reversibility in the same way. Attaching cells of rank \(r+1\) preserves all lower homotopy groups and quotients \(\pi_r\) by the specified generators. This gives the desired \(i\)-type. The homology search in the cyclic fundamental-group case used connectivity of its universal cover at each stage; the existence proof here uses higher homotopy groups themselves.

### A universal comparison in the odd-dimensional free case

Suppose \(m=n+1\) is odd and different from three and seven. Each free \(H_1K\) coordinate has a based representing loop in \(K\) and an integral character represented by \(K\to S^1\). Their composite has degree one on that coordinate, and the character has degree zero on the other chosen generators. After suspension the projection therefore reads the universal square in \(\pi_{2m-1}S^m\). It has exact order two by the Hopf invariant one theorem and graded symmetry. The free squares are independent in \(Y\). If \(H_1K\) has no finite even-order summand, they exhaust \(T_{n,i}(Y)\). [Adams, Theorem 1.1.1](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/adams1.pdf)

Use one stationary colour and the finite local completion of a single circle through rank \(i\) as the testing presentation. Its local realization retracts onto the circle, with only additional \((i+1)\)-spheres. The one comparison is its single shell with the universal square against the identity. For necessity, a failed old boundary yields a nonzero surface-null shell by Response 158. An integral character picking one nonzero coordinate, followed by the inclusion of the circle in the tester, sends it to the tested square. For sufficiency send the tester back by its retraction followed by a representing loop of a free generator. This sends an assumed filler to a filler at a nonzero shell in the given context. Both directions use raw substitutions by the local truncation argument of Response 158 applied at \(i\). In degrees through \(i\) match the cellular map on each iterated hom at its prescribed faces, and use symmetric top reachability at \(i+1\). Suspending the \((i+1)\)-connected Postnikov comparison \(n\) times suffices to preserve \(\pi_{i+1}Y\). Thus these maps transport actual published witnesses. If the free rank is zero under this torsion hypothesis, the kernel is zero and reflection follows without a test.

**Validation.** Run `python3 -B tools/semistrict_surface_bottom_squares.py`. The audit enumerates 126 integral bracket-coefficient tuples on five mixed finite groups with both signs, and compares the full ordered tensor kernel to the diagonal subgroup. It evaluates 48 Alexander–Whitney cup squares on signed shuffle triangulations of products of spheres, including the values zero modulo \(Q\) and nonzero modulo \(2Q\) needed for the even-order test. For instance `--rank 3 --bottom 4 --orders 2 4` reports two independent degree-ten differences, the square of the first generator and twice the square of the second. Another 412 checks evaluate images of the distinguished classes under all homomorphisms in a family of cyclic and mixed-order targets. With `--agda-dir DIR`, the checker emits `CyclicShells.agda`. Run `agda --safe --no-libraries -i src -i DIR DIR/CyclicShells.agda` to check the rank-three attachments at orders two and four and the round-trip constructions through the required ranks. The general shell and insertion results use the homotopy calculations above. [Integral checker](../../../tools/semistrict_surface_bottom_squares.py)

## Researcher Response 164

**At degree six, every binary interchange surface has a two-use test for arbitrary independent rules on rank-three scalars, including rules with empty ports.** There are finitely many small port profiles for the central differences. All remaining failures are tested by a single computable sequence: at arity \(d\ge2\) use twice the same \(d\)-input, \(d\)-output rule, with no throughs. The prescribed track is raw-nontrivial and fills after *every* individual port deletion. A noncentral failure anywhere forces the prescribed type to be surface-inhabited for every sufficiently large \(d\). Hence, in addition to the small central tests, surface nonfilling at an unbounded set of indices suffices. The sequence does not presuppose which surface has a failure.

### The factors of the cut group

Let \(p_{is}\) be the size of port \(s\) of event \(i\), with \(s=0\) for input and \(s=1\) for output. Put \(r_{is}=\max(0,p_{is}-1)\). The fixed-end group at a named antichain is a direct product of a free abelian group and, for each pair \(i<j\) with all four sizes at least two, the factor
\[
 Q_{ij}=\mathbb Z^{r_{i0}r_{j1}} * \mathbb Z^{r_{i1}r_{j0}} .
\]
The two free factors record the opposite intermediate cuts of *that pair*. Tracks from distinct such pairs commute even when one event belongs to both pairs. Here are the integral bases for the abelian part as well as a proof of the product.

Start with the based cut presentation of round-one Responses 90 and 104. At each Boolean cut take the exterior square on live tips; two cut groups commute whenever the cuts are comparable. Transfers across an event fix the other tips and identify the two images of the site marker, the respective sums of its ports. The compatible bases and incidence maps apply with either sum zero. For tips inside one port use their ordinary oriented pairs. They have no transfer at their own event (there is just one marker) and are independent of all other event states. For pairs in *different* columns use the following tensor basis. On a nonempty port take its sum and its individual nonanchor tips, choosing the last as anchor. Across the event the sum is a persistent generator when both ports exist. If only one port exists, its sum against an outside tip is killed. Each nonanchor generator requires its indicated event state. A through is a separate persistent column. Form the cross products of these named generators, once per pair of columns, with globally fixed orientation. At the anchor use sum minus the nonanchor tips. This gives every surviving generator and all identifications: on wedges with the single site direction the transfer identifies just the two sums against outside tips. Stationary pairs transfer unchanged. No transfer changes a within-port pair.

A resulting generator prescribes at most two Boolean coordinates. Any two generators commute whenever they can be placed at successive, possibly identical cuts in one schedule. Such cuts exist unless their partial assignments require opposite changes of order: there must be one common coordinate requiring \(0,1\) and another requiring \(1,0\). This requires the *same two* constrained events at the opposite mixed states. Conversely defining only the commutations afforded by these placements presents the group. Each cut expands in its integral basis, and each original commutation at two comparable cuts holds between every expanded generator there. All surviving copies with a given partial assignment are identified across unrelated events by the connected cube of the unspecified coordinates. These constructions give inverse maps between the two presentations. It follows that all within-port pairs and all cross products except those in the displayed two-sided free products are central basis elements. When one opposite side has rank zero the other is central too. This refines the known right-angled Artin presentation to a signed cut-word normal form. [Based cut presentation](../answered/semistrict-surface-conservativity-2026-11-24.md#researcher-response-90) · [Nullary transfers and integral basis](../answered/semistrict-surface-conservativity-2026-11-24.md#researcher-response-104)

### Shrinking a failure to two columns

For a nonzero central difference choose a nonzero coefficient. A within-port pair is read by retaining its two tips and their event. For a cross product retain only its two columns (a column may be a through). In each relevant nonempty port keep its anchor and the named nonanchor tip if the selected mode uses one there. Keep the anchor on the other nonempty side of each retained event as well. Under this deletion a persistent sum goes to the new sum; a retained nonanchor goes to its own basis name and an omitted nonanchor goes to zero. On the within-port pairs the projection just deletes entries. Thus no other basis coefficient changes the one being tested. A central generator remains central under these deletions, since further deletion cannot introduce a missing opposite mixed mode. The same reasoning applies to through/through and single-column histories. These are finitely many two-column profiles, each nonempty port of size at most two. The surface witness specializes by the occurrence and cut lifts, and the resulting nonzero central reading certifies raw nonfilling.

For a difference with a nonidentity projection to \(Q_{ij}\), commute it with a realized generator of that factor with which it does not commute. Such a choice exists because a free product of two nontrivial free abelian groups has trivial centre. This kills every other factor, including the central part, and produces a nonidentity word in the derived subgroup of \(Q_{ij}\). A surface comparison to the identity is preserved under this operation by pasting, using normality of the based filling subgroup. Now forget every other column. Nonanchor tip pairs at the two mixed cuts actually realize the two abelian bases, so the same word still reads in \(Q_{ij}\) at the resulting two events. Its four port sizes are all at least two.

For any \(d\) at least their maximum, replace the anchor of each port by as many parallel copies as necessary to reach \(d\). Map the two named rules to the corresponding balanced rules, with their port fits. These substitutions preserve the query at its written ends: the two independent events have individually named input and output wires, and the maps on cut pairs are the signed parallel expansions. The nonanchor mixed basis letters used by the query are unchanged. In particular their word has a length bound independent of \(d\), and restricting to a single representative of each expanded anchor also recovers the original word. Finally fold all tips to one scalar and both uses to one rule. Any raw comparison lifts back with the prescribed occurrence names, and a given surface comparison folds forward. This proves transfer to the two-use balanced context without restricting the original syllable ranks.

### One prescribed test per balanced size

Write \(Q_d=A*B\) for the mixed factor at balanced size \(d\). The following constructions use actual cut spheres, so their results are old based comparisons at the same history. First make a Brunnian seed. At one mixed cut select the tip pair with index \(i\) on both columns, calling its sphere \(a_i\), and at the other mixed cut use the corresponding \(b_i\), for \(0\le i<d\). These letters have nonzero projections to their respective free factors, including for the anchor: its vector modulo the port sum is minus the sum of the remaining tips. Begin with \([a_0,b_0]\), then bracket successively with \(a_i,b_i\) for the other indices. At each step the current element is nonzero in the derived subgroup of \(A*B\). It acts by a translation on the free-product tree, since an element conjugate into a factor would have nonzero abelianization unless trivial. Its centralizer contains no nonidentity element of a factor: a commuting elliptic fixes its axis pointwise, whereas edge stabilizers are trivial. Thus the next bracket is again nonzero. Central terms in individual pair spheres vanish in these brackets. Every port tip occurs in a leaf letter whose restriction is zero upon deleting that tip, so the entire seed fills after any such deletion.

At size \(d\) list the distinct nonidentity normal forms of words of length at most \(d\) on the signed *nonanchor* mixed-pair basis. Adjoin the seed. Combine two nontrivial entries \(u,v\) by searching in increasing word length for \(z\) with \([u,zvz^{-1}]\ne1\), and retain that bracket. The search terminates: if every conjugate commuted with \(u\), the normal closure of \(v\) would lie in the centralizer of \(u\). For elliptic \(u\) this centralizer is a conjugate factor, whose intersection with a distinct conjugate is trivial. For hyperbolic \(u\) it is cyclic, acting freely by translations on the axis. A nontrivial cyclic normal subgroup would give an invariant line for \(Q_d\), impossible in its minimal free-product tree with vertex valences greater than two. Pair the entries successively in a fixed order up to one nonidentity root. This root lies in the normal closure of *each* entry. On single-tip restriction it vanishes by its seed leaf. The computation is finite at each \(d\); the shortlist grows rapidly.

If some surface kills a noncentral difference, the transferred word above appears in every sufficiently large shortlist. Its surface filler then gives one at the root. Conversely any surface filling of any root witnesses a noncentral raw failure at that balanced history. Combined with the small central cases this proves the criterion. In particular bounded tip deletion on the original history does not suffice for the unrestricted nonabelian sector: the prescribed roots are raw counterexamples to detection by any such bound. Whether a surface fills one of them is a separate question. [Normality and prescribed-test method](#researcher-response-144) · [Birth-only cyclic tests](#researcher-response-162)

**Reproduce.** Run `python3 -B tools/semistrict_surface_spatial_antichain.py`. It checks 768 individual marker transfers in the signed normal form, including zero ports; checks commutators on distinct event pairs sharing one event; and tests every single-tip deletion of its balanced size-two and size-three seeds. The prescribed size-two root covers 16 distinct short nonidentity words and is again checked at every deletion. Use `--brunnian D` for a seed or `--prescribed D` for the full shortlist construction. Either output is ordinary cut-word JSON accepted by the same solver. [Antichain solver and signed query format](../../../tools/semistrict_surface_spatial_antichain.py)
