## Researcher Response 177

**At stationary rank two and old degree 11, one specified comparison at each level of a sequence of finite reversible presentations tests published insertion for all labels with 4-connected double suspension.** A published failure in any such label forces the specified comparison to fill at every sufficiently large level. The level can be bounded from the 2-primary exponent of the label's seventh stable homotopy group. The need for unbounded targets is genuine for detection by local maps: given *any* finite list of finite label targets, there is a nonzero raw square in this degree whose image in every target is zero under every local map. This last assertion concerns detection of raw differences; it does not assume that the example admits a published filler.

### Squares of arbitrarily high divisibility

Use \(W,g,d,N,m\) from [Response 175](#realizing-and-testing-arbitrary-binary-relations), so \(\Sigma^2 g=[x,x]\) has order two. This construction works at every \(d\equiv3\pmod4\), \(d\ge3\). Add a local sphere \(S^{N-1}\) with identity \(y\), then attach an \(N\)-disk by \(g+2^a y\), for any \(a\ge0\). In the double suspension, the subgroup generated before attachment by the square and the upper sphere is \(C_2\oplus\mathbb Z\), by the two wedge retractions. Relative Hurewicz quotients it by exactly \((1,2^a)\), as in Response 175. Its image is cyclic of order \(2^{a+1}\); the square survives as \(-2^a y\), with \(y\) now denoting the suspended class. All cells lie in local degrees at most \(i=N\) before reversible completion.

For a finite target label \(Z\), \(\pi_{2m-1}\Sigma^2 Z\) is finitely generated since the target double suspension is simply connected and of finite CW type. If the image of this square is nonzero then the image of \(y\) has order exactly \(2^{a+1}\). Choosing \(a\) at least the maximum 2-exponent index of any finite list rules this out for every target on the list. The same conclusion holds for finite presentations tested by their local \(i\)-types, by suspended Postnikov connectivity. In particular it applies even to targets outside the attaching-matrix family and to maps that do not preserve its named generators.

There is an explicit sequence of testers within a larger matrix family. Use \(b\) copies of \(W\), \(c\) upper \((N-1)\)-spheres and rows \((B_i,D_i)\) of signed attaching degrees on the \(g_j\) and the upper spheres. The exact raw square group is
\[
  \mathbb F_2^b\big/\{zB\bmod2:z\in\mathbb Z^{\#\mathrm{rows}},\ zD=0\}.
\]
Indeed the suspended attachments impose exactly the written rows on the subgroup \(\mathbb F_2^b\oplus\mathbb Z^c\); a pure square relation must cancel all upper coefficients **integrally**. At level \(a\) use a single \(W\), one upper sphere and the two attachments \(2g,\ g+2^a y\). The square survives by the preceding quotient. If a shell survives in a matrix label, take a separating binary character \(v\) annihilating the displayed relation subspace. A fold onto the selected copies of \(W\), with each upper sphere sent to \(t_j y\), extends whenever
\[
                 Dt\equiv 2^a Bv\pmod{2^{a+1}}.
\]
In fact on disk \(i\) the degree on the second test disk is \(k_i=(Dt)_i/2^a\) and the degree on the first is \(((Bv)_i-k_i)/2\). To see solvability, diagonalize \(D\) by unimodular row and column operations, carrying \(B\) through the row operations. Rows with zero diagonal part have even character readings by the assumption on \(v\). In every other row take \(a\) at least the 2-adic valuation of its nonzero diagonal entry and invert the odd factor after division. Thus the corresponding square tests suffice throughout this family, and the map of successive testers taking \(y\) to \(2y'\) preserves their distinguished squares.

### One comparison per level for arbitrary degree-11 labels

Now set \(d=3,\ m=5,\ i=N=8\) and \(X=K(C_2,3)\). The construction here does not require a matrix presentation or a bound on label dimension. Let \(I\) be the Brown–Comenetz dual of the sphere, which represents \([U,\Sigma^k I]=\operatorname{Hom}(\pi_k U,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)\) on spectra. Put \(J_s=\operatorname{fib}(2^s:I\to I)\) for \(s\ge1\). The squares with vertical maps identity on the domain and doubling on the codomain give \(J_s\to J_{s+1}\). All homotopy groups of each \(J_s\) are finite: use the multiplication exact sequence, the finiteness of positive stable sphere stems and \((\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)[2^s]=C_{2^s}\). The nonzero character of \(\pi_0 H\mathbb F_2\) gives a stable map \(H\mathbb F_2\to I\); it has a unique lift up to homotopy to each \(J_s\). Existence follows because twice the map is zero, and uniqueness from \([H\mathbb F_2,\Sigma^{-1}I]=0\). Thus the lifts are compatible. [Mahowald and Rezk, Brown–Comenetz representability](https://rezk.web.illinois.edu/mahowald-rezk-bc-dual-final.pdf)

Use the composite
\[
 X\xrightarrow{u\smile Sq^2u}K(C_2,8)
     \longrightarrow \Omega^\infty\Sigma^8 J_s
\]
and let \(Z_s\) be the 2-connected cover of the base component of its homotopy fibre. The second map comes from the indicated spectrum lift. The universal bottom character lifts over the degree-three Moore complex \(S^3\cup_2 e^4\) in this fibre, since the first arrow is null there by dimension. Fix the lift using a nullhomotopy into \(K(C_2,8)\) before mapping through the tower. This gives a compatible order-two bottom element \(b_s\in\pi_3 Z_s\) mapping to one. Use a finite reversible tester of local type \(P_8 Z_s\), one stationary colour, and compare the shell \([b_s,b_s]\) with zero. Such testers exist: \(Z_s\) is simply connected with finite homotopy groups through degree eight, hence its Postnikov stages have finite-type CW models (build the finite-group Eilenberg–MacLane stages, successively using their fibrations). Take the finite nine-skeleton and realize its cells with the local completion of Responses 158 and 163. It induces the same 8-type. The square is nonzero: projection to \(X\) gives a character evaluating to one on \(b_s\) and the characteristic product of this character pairs to zero with every stable sphere, since its map into \(\Omega^\infty\Sigma^8 I\) is null. Apply Response 175 to \(Z_s\), then use the suspended Postnikov comparison.

Suppose a nonzero shell in an arbitrary reversible label \(K\) has a published filler. At one puncture choose a character \(c:K\to X\) annihilating all raw square relations and evaluating to one on the shell. By Response 175 this is precisely the condition needed for the composite with the characteristic map into \(\Omega^\infty\Sigma^8 I\) to be null: that map is the functional \(f\mapsto\langle c Sq^2c,h_2(f)\rangle/2\) in \(\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\). Let \(G=\pi_7^S K\), a finitely generated group for the finite label, and let \(2^e\) kill its finite 2-primary part, taking \(e=0\) if this part is zero. In the exact sequence for \(J_1\) the pullback obstruction is therefore in \(G^\vee/2G^\vee\), where \(G^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}(G,\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z)\). In the sequence for \(J_s\) its image is represented by \(2^{s-1}\) times the same character modulo \(2^sG^\vee\). Free summands have divisible dual, odd torsion permits division by two and \(2^e\) kills the other summands. Hence the map is null at \(s=e+1\). This gives a lift of \(c\) to the homotopy fibre at that level. It lifts further to \(Z_s\): the fibre has abelian fundamental group by the homotopy exact sequence over simply connected \(X\), and \(H_1K=H_2K=0\) by the assumed connectivity of \(\Sigma^2K\). The induced fundamental group map is trivial; after passing to the universal cover the remaining degree-two obstruction is zero by universal coefficients.

Finally the image of the shell becomes exactly the distinguished square **one level later**. The low sphere stems are \(\pi_4^S=0\) and \(\pi_3^S=C_{24}\). The exact sequence of \(J_s\) therefore gives \(\pi_4(\Omega^\infty\Sigma^8J_s)=C_{2^{\min(s,3)}}\), coming entirely from the cokernel of multiplication on \((\pi_3^S)^\vee\). Its transition to the next level is doubling on representatives. In the fibre sequence over \(X\) this is the kernel of \(\pi_3 Z_s\to C_2\); the Moore lift above splits off \(b_s\). Consequently every lift with character one maps to \(b_{s+1}\) modulo twice the bottom group. The square map factors through that quotient. Passage to the finite local 8-types represents these maps by substitutions at the prescribed faces, so the hypothesized filler gives one for the specified comparison at level \(e+2\), and at all subsequent levels by compatibility. Conversely a filler at any level is a failure on that finite tester. Thus nonfilling on any unbounded set of levels suffices. On labels with 2-primary exponent of \(\pi_7^S K\) bounded by \(2^e\), nonfilling at level \(e+2\) alone implies reflection. The constructed comparisons still require published filling decisions. [Isaksen–Wang–Xu, Table 1, stable sphere stems](https://pmihes.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.1007/s10240-023-00139-1.pdf)

The stages are distinguished even by their first possible detecting local map. In the one-disk example \(g+2^a y\) at degree 11, the only character nonzero on the bottom is the one induced by collapsing the upper sphere and mapping to the bundle \(E\), followed by its bottom character. The collapse extends over the attaching disk with degree one. The characteristic product on \(E\) reads one on its fundamental class by Response 175 and its zero square. Thus the pulled-back product on the one-disk label is represented by the top cellular cochain of value one (a coboundary when \(a=0\)). Its map to the stage target factors through the top-cell collapse and takes the value \(2^{s-1}\) in \(\pi_8(\Omega^\infty\Sigma^8J_s)=C_{2^s}\), because the nonzero character has value one half. The attaching cofibration identifies the indeterminacy of that value. The \(g\) component contributes zero since it is stably null and the target is an infinite loop space; the upper sphere contributes exactly \(2^a C_{2^s}\). A lift therefore exists precisely at \(s\ge a+1\). At those levels choose the nullhomotopy on \(W\) through \(K(C_2,8)\), which gives the chosen bottom lift, and correct the disk by a nullhomotopy on the upper sphere solving \(2^a t=2^{s-1}\) in \(C_{2^s}\). This realizes the distinguished square. Conversely any substitution induced by a local map carrying the square to the distinguished one must read one on the universal character, since that character annihilates the raw relations there. In particular, the levels can first detect genuine nonzero squares arbitrarily far along the sequence.

**Reproduce.** Run `python3 -B tools/semistrict_surface_divisible_squares.py`. The solver retains the unimodular operations on the upper-sphere matrix, computes the full square quotient, selects a separating character and recovers the signed disk degrees of the fold. The audit checks 2,988 comparisons, including all two-row sign matrices with two bottom columns and one upper column, and checks the stage congruences through level eight. It also checks the separate dual-character transitions on cyclic orders through 128 and the doubling of degree-11 bottom lifts. With `--bottom-count 1 --upper-count 1 --row 1 -8 --shell 1` the two disk degrees are \((1,-1)\) at matrix level three. With `--stable-orders 0 12 8` the universal bound is level five. The latter calculation takes the cyclic orders of the seventh stable group as input. The existence and detection properties of the universal finite presentations follow from the homotopy argument above. [Signed attachments and stage solver](../../../tools/semistrict_surface_divisible_squares.py)

## Researcher Response 178

**For every odd bottom dimension in the first unstable shell, published insertion on all finite reversible labels of a fixed stationary rank reduces to a fixed finite number of comparisons at each level of one sequence of finite presentations.** In bottom dimensions **15, 31 and 63 a single marked square per level suffices**, for every stationary rank in range and arbitrary bottom torsion. If the relevant stable homotopy group of the label has 2-primary exponent dividing \(2^e\), the single test at level \(\max(2,e+1)\) suffices for these three dimensions. For example, at rank three and old degree 32 the group controlling the bound is \(\pi_{26}^S K\). These are reductions to published filling judgments. A filler at any marked comparison would give a counterexample in its own finite presentation.

### The universal stable character

Use the connectivity and local reversibility hypotheses of [Response 153](#researcher-response-153). Write \(Y=\Sigma^n K\), where \(n\ge2\), \(m\ge n+1\) is odd and \(Y\) is \((m-1)\)-connected. Put \(d=m-n\), \(N=2m-n\), \(i=2m-2\), and \(A=H_d K\). The tested old degree is \(n+2m-1\). Use the component of the local label at the tested puncture. All stable groups of spaces below are reduced. In dimensions \(m=3,7\) all the squares already vanish by the sphere multiplications. Otherwise the bottom square of \(S^m\) has order two by the Hopf invariant one theorem. [First unstable group](#researcher-response-163)

The James-pair argument in the first two paragraphs of [Response 175's calculation of the relations](#why-the-characteristic-number-gives-every-relation) applies before specializing the stationary rank. It gives the natural exact sequence
\[
 \pi_N^S K\xrightarrow{\lambda_K} A/2A\xrightarrow{q_Y}T_{n,i}(Y)\to0.
\]
Here the stable Hopf tensor modulo norms gives the first arrow, and the second takes a bottom element to its Whitehead square. To specify the universal functional without knowing the relations in a test label, let \(X=K(C_2,d)\). Suspend a stable sphere in \(X\) by \(n\) and compose with \(\Sigma^n X\to K(C_2,m)\) representing the suspended fundamental cohomology class. The result belongs to \(\pi_{2m}^S K(C_2,m)=C_2\). Send its generator to \(1/2\in\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\). This composite is \(\lambda_X\) followed by that inclusion. Indeed the same James pair on the \((m-1)\)-connected space \(K(C_2,m)\) has zero bracket target in degree \(2m-1\), so its stable Hopf tensor surjects onto the bottom \(C_2\) modulo norms. It must be the unique isomorphism in Brown's calculation. Naturality along the suspended fundamental class proves the identification. [Brumfiel–Milgram, Proposition 2.1.1(a), including the functional Steenrod-square test](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/brumfielmilg.pdf#page=11)

Represent this character by \(a:\Sigma^\infty X\to\Sigma^N I\), using the Brown–Comenetz dual of the sphere. Write \(J_s=\operatorname{fib}(2^s:I\to I)\). Choose one lift of \(a\) at level one, which exists since \(2a=0\), and take its images under the transitions of [Response 177](#researcher-response-177). Adjunction gives compatible \(a_s:X\to U_s=\Omega^\infty\Sigma^NJ_s\). Denote by \(Z_s\) the \((d-1)\)-connected cover of the base component of its homotopy fibre. A bottom character \(c:A\to C_2\) gives a map \(K\to X\) by universal coefficients. By naturality and exactness, \(c\) kills all square relations precisely when \(a\circ\Sigma^\infty c\) is null. [Brown–Comenetz representability](https://rezk.web.illinois.edu/mahowald-rezk-bc-dual-final.pdf)

Suppose such a \(c\) reads one on a given surviving square. Put \(G=\pi_{N-1}^S K\) and let \(2^e\) be the exponent of its 2-primary torsion, with \(e=0\) for the trivial group. The pullback of the level-one lift is represented by some \(\psi\) in \(G^\vee/2G^\vee\), where the dual is into \(\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\). At level \(s\) its class is \(2^{s-1}\psi\bmod 2^sG^\vee\). This vanishes for \(s\ge e+1\), since \(G\) is finitely generated. Thus \(c\) lifts to the fibre. For \(d=1\) connectedness gives the indicated component. For \(d\ge2\) its fundamental group is abelian by the exact sequence over simply connected \(X\), and \(H_1 K=0\), so the lift passes to the universal cover. Successively the lower Postnikov obstructions vanish in \(H^j(K;\pi_j)\) for \(2\le j<d\), by \(\widetilde H_{<d}K=0\) and universal coefficients. This gives the required map to \(Z_s\).

### How many marked bottom classes are needed?

Let \(P,Q\) be the 2-primary parts of the duals of the stable sphere stems \(m-2,m-1\), respectively. Write \(2^t=\exp Q\), taking \(t=0\) when \(Q=0\), and put \(s_0=1+t\). The generator \(j:S^d\to X\) kills all square relations on the sphere because its suspended square in the source has order two. Apply the lifting calculation to \(K=S^d\) to choose a bottom lift \(b\) of \(j\) at level \(s_0\). Carry it up the sequence. For \(s\ge s_0\) put \(B_s=\pi_d Z_s\). The two fibre sequences give
\[
 0\to V_s\to B_s\to C_2\to0,\qquad
 0\to P/2^sP\to V_s=\pi_{d+1}U_s\to Q[2^s]\to0 .
\]
The first injection uses \(\pi_{d+1}X=0\). For \(d=1\) its kernel is central: the action on the homotopy of the loop fibre is induced by transport along the image loop in \(U_s\), which is null since the bottom generator lifts. A central extension of a cyclic group is abelian. In every case \(B_s=H_d Z_s\). The transitions in the second sequence double the left coordinate and include the right subgroup. The latter is already all of \(Q\) at \(s_0\).

Choose one representative of each coset of \(2Q\) in \(Q\), and one lift \(u_\gamma\in V_{s_0}\) of each representative. Mark \(b+u_\gamma\) and carry these marks forward. Every bottom class reading one at level \(s\ge s_0\) differs from a mark by a double in \(V_s\) plus an element of \(P/2^sP\): subtract its representative in \(Q/2Q\), then lift a half of the difference in \(Q\). At the next level the remaining left coordinate is itself a double. This proof works for nonsplit extensions. Consequently every such square agrees with a marked square one level later, or at the same level if \(P=0\). Moreover **every marked square is nonzero**. The character given by \(Z_s\to X\) reads one on the mark and kills all relations because its composite with \(a\) is null.

Use one stationary colour and the finite local \(i\)-type models of \(Z_s\) for the presentations. Indeed all the fibre homotopy groups are finite, since the groups of \(J_s\) are finite. The Postnikov sections have CW models finite in each degree, by their fibrations with finite-group Eilenberg–MacLane fibres (also over a finite fundamental group). Their finite \((i+1)\)-skeleta realize the required type by the local cellular realization and reversibility construction of [Response 158](#researcher-response-158) and [Response 163](#researcher-response-163). At each mark compare its suspended square with zero. A published failure in any label yields a nonzero surface-null square at one puncture, hence a separating \(c\) as above. The resulting map of local \(i\)-types supplies a substitution at the written faces, carrying its filler to a marked comparison. Thus a bound on the number and level of the necessary tests is
\[
 |Q/2Q|\quad\text{at level}\quad \max(e+1,t+1)+\mathbf1_{P\ne0}.
\]
All subsequent images on that sequence of marks fill as well. Conversely a filler at a mark is already a published failure. Hence cofinal nonfilling on each sequence of marks suffices for all finite labels; one level suffices on an exponent-bounded class in the forward criterion.

For \(m=15,31,63\), the tabulated \(P\) vanishes and \(Q\) is elementary abelian of ranks two, one and four, respectively. Then \(V_s=Q\) for \(s\ge2\), so each difference between bottom lifts has order at most two. Its square vanishes by the Moore-space calculation of [Response 165](#researcher-response-165), even when \(B_s\) is nonsplit. All marked squares therefore agree with the one on \(b\) at the same level. In contrast, the general bound for \(m=9\) gives at most four comparisons and that for \(m=11\) at most two. These numbers bound the tests required and make no claim of independence. [Isaksen–Wang–Xu, Tables 1 and 2](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7547228/)

**Reproduce.** Run `python3 -B tools/semistrict_surface_odd_shell_tower.py`. The solver checks 23,210 comparisons by enumerating doubles in finite abelian extensions, including nonsplit extensions with nonzero carry from a quotient generator, and verifies the dual-character bound on every cyclic order through 128. With `--rank 3 --bottom 15 --stable-orders 0 12 8` it gives one comparison at level four in old degree 32. The cyclic orders supplied here describe \(\pi_{26}^S K\); a zero denotes a free factor. Other sphere decompositions can be supplied explicitly. The calculation checks the arithmetic of the bounds; the realization and filler implications use the proofs above. [Marked-square stage solver](../../../tools/semistrict_surface_odd_shell_tower.py)

## Researcher Response 179

**Published insertion reflects throughout the first unstable shell for local \((n+1)\)-fold loop-space types whenever \(S^m\) admits \(n\) independent tangent fields.** In the same range there are finite labels with arbitrarily divisible nonzero raw squares. No finite collection of finite label targets detects all of them by local maps. For \(m=15,31,63\) this proves that the unbounded levels of [Response 178](#researcher-response-178) are necessary for this detection method at stationary ranks \(2\) through \(8,9,11\), respectively. In these ranks the stage bound \(e+1\) in that response is attained for every sufficiently large \(e\). The proof also gives an exact least-level calculation for each individual square in a signed attaching-matrix label.

### A two-cell local label and a reflection criterion

Keep \(d=m-n\), \(N=m+d\), \(i=2m-2\), and the reversibility and connectivity hypotheses of Response 178. Take \(m\) odd other than 3 or 7. The field hypothesis holds for \(2\le n<\rho(m+1)\) in the notation of [Response 174](#researcher-response-174). Split \(TS^m=V\oplus\mathbb R^n\) using the fields. The Thom space of the oriented rank-\(d\) bundle \(V\) over the two-cell sphere has a single attaching map
\[
 C_g=\mathrm{Th}(V)=S^d\cup_g e^N,\qquad
 \Sigma^n g=\pm[\iota_m,\iota_m].
\]
For the attaching identity, use the collapse of the complement of a tubular neighbourhood of the diagonal from \(S^m\times S^m\) to \(\mathrm{Th}(TS^m)=\Sigma^n C_g\). The restrictions to the two axes have degree \(\pm1\) on the bottom Thom fibre, by transverse intersection at a point. Homotope the restrictions into that fibre and extend the homotopy over the product. The resulting map of pairs also has relative top degree \(\pm1\): its pullback of the Thom class times the base orientation class integrates to the integral of the orientation class on the diagonal, hence to one up to sign. Relative Hurewicz on the two top cells and naturality of their boundary maps now identify the suspended attaching map with the bracket of the axis restrictions. In particular \(\Sigma^{n+1}g=0\). [Adams, tangent fields and the Hurwitz–Radon number](https://www.math.ens.psl.eu/~benoist/refs/Adams.pdf)

For a spherical bottom generator \(z:S^d\to K\), this identifies its suspended square exactly with \(\pm\Sigma^n(zg)\). Thus if bottom homology modulo two is generated by spherical classes and \(\pi_{N-1}K\to\pi_{N+n}\Sigma^{n+1}K\) is injective, all squares vanish. Indeed each \(zg\) suspends to zero after \(n+1\) suspensions. The same conclusion holds when the local \(i\)-type comes from a connected \((n+1)\)-fold loop space \(K'\). The unit \(K'\to\Omega^{n+1}\Sigma^{n+1}K'\) has a left inverse by adjunction. Its fundamental group is abelian, so the lower homology vanishing implies that the bottom homology of \(K'\) is spherical by Hurewicz (in dimension one use abelianization). The local \(i\)-type determines all groups and maps used to test the suspended square by Response 158. The resulting zero obstruction group proves published reflection at every written boundary in this degree. For example at \(n=3,m=15\) it applies to the local type of \(\Omega^\infty\Sigma^\infty S^{12}\) in degree 32. Here \(\pi_{26}\) of the local space is the nonzero four-element stable 14-stem. This example does not require vanishing of the group containing \(zg\).

### Which level first detects a particular square?

Use \(b\) local bottom spheres \(S^d\), \(c\) upper spheres \(S^{N-1}\) and one \(N\)-disk for each row \((B_j,D_j)\) of an integer matrix. Attach by the row sum of the individual \(g\)'s and the identity maps of the upper spheres. These labels admit the finite reversible completion of Response 158 since \(N\le i\). The subgroup on the squares and the suspended upper spheres is exactly
\[
 H=(\mathbb F_2^b\oplus\mathbb Z^c)/\langle (B_j\bmod2,D_j)\rangle .
\]
Indeed the coordinates before attachment are independent by projection, and relative Hurewicz gives exactly the attaching boundaries on that subgroup. Write \(x\) for a pure square class in it. Let \(s_0\) and the mark \(b_s\) over the bottom sphere be as in Response 178, choosing the zero representative of \(Q/2Q\) with zero lift. For \(s\ge s_0\) the following three statements are equivalent:

1. A local map to the level-\(s\) type sends \(x\) to the single distinguished square on \(b_s\).
2. Some character \(H\to C_{2^s}\) sends \(x\) to the order-two element.
3. \(x\notin 2^sH\).

For the last equivalence, pass to \(H/2^sH\) and use its cyclic decomposition. Every nonzero order-two element reads nontrivially in a cyclic factor, which embeds in \(C_{2^s}\). For the first equivalence the character on the bottom spheres is a binary vector \(v\) reading one on \(x\). A choice of upper readings \(z\) must solve
\[
                   Dz=2^{s-1}Bv\pmod{2^s}.
\]
This is precisely the character equation for \(H\), since the right side has order at most two. To see that it computes the actual fibre obstruction, first give \(C_g\) the bottom character one. Its square dies by construction. Exactness in Response 178 shows that its stable Hopf character reads \(1/2\) on the stable top generator: \(g\) is stably null, and the sphere summand has zero Hopf character. At \(s\ge s_0\) the bottom sphere has a chosen lift; the top-cell reading in \(\pi_N U_s=C_{2^s}\) is therefore \(2^{s-1}\). Indeed this group injects into \(\pi_N(\Omega^\infty\Sigma^NI)=\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\), and changing the bottom nullhomotopy changes the reading by a composite with the stable zero map \(g\).

Fold the selected bottom spheres to \(C_g\), send upper spheres to the basepoint, and extend by the signed disk degrees \((Bv)_j\). This represents the unique bottom cohomology character with these readings. Give the selected spheres the chosen lift \(b_s\), and the other bottom spheres the zero lift. On an upper sphere a nullhomotopy can change by any element of \(\pi_N U_s\). Its effect on the disks is exactly \(Dz\); all changes on lower bottom spheres contribute zero by stable nullity of \(g\). Hence the congruence is sufficient for a lift with those particular bottom values, and necessary for any lift with those character readings. Passing to the connected cover preserves the specified bottom values and the resulting square. Conversely any detecting map must read one on \(x\) under the universal character, since that character annihilates every square relation in the target. The argument applies to finite local types by Postnikov comparison as in Response 178.

For nonzero \(x\) the least detecting level is therefore \(\max(s_0,1+h)\), where \(h\) is the largest integer with \(x\in2^h H\). For a single row \((1,2^a)\), \(H=C_{2^{a+1}}\) and the bottom square has height \(a\). The stable splitting of the local attachment is \(S^d\vee M(C_{2^a},N-1)\), since \(g\) is stably null; use a contractible Moore summand at \(a=0\). Hence the stable group controlling the label bound has 2-exponent index \(e=\max(t,a)\), with \(t\) from Response 178. For every \(a\ge s_0\) the first possible detecting level is exactly \(a+1=e+1\). In any finite list of finite targets the 2-primary exponents of \(\pi_{2m-1}\Sigma^n Z\) are bounded. The image of the upper sphere would have to have order \(2^{a+1}\) to retain the square. This excludes detection by the entire list for large \(a\), regardless of the chosen maps. Existence of a published filler for these surviving squares remains open.

**Reproduce.** Run `python3 -B tools/semistrict_surface_frame_labels.py` to construct and check the tangent frames, and `python3 -B tools/semistrict_surface_divisible_squares.py` for the signed disks. The latter now compares 3,200 least-level calculations with direct enumeration of all cyclic characters in the original coordinates. With `--bottom-count 2 --upper-count 2 --row 1 0 3 6 --row 1 1 11 30 --row 2 1 14 36 --shell 0 1 --first-stage 2` the first level is four and the two upper readings are 14 and 1 modulo 16. Changing the shell to `1 0` gives level two on the same presentation. The solver retains integer row and column operations before imposing the level-dependent parity constraints. [Signed-attachment solver](../../../tools/semistrict_surface_divisible_squares.py) · [Frame solver](../../../tools/semistrict_surface_frame_labels.py)

## Researcher Response 180

**For the join in Q1(c), every based old comparison on copies of a single 3-scalar has a surface filler. In every pure scalar rank \(n\ge3\), three occurrences suffice to witness every degree of joined failure.** For the four individual surfaces in Q1(b), the primes at which any higher configuration group has nonzero comparison image are determined by the order of one two-particle sphere. These statements use the ordinary coherence rule.

### What contracting the exchange does to the two-particle sphere

Take a vertex and one generating \(n\)-scalar between its iterated units. Write \(F_k=\operatorname{Conf}_k(\mathbb R^n)\), \(U_k=F_k/\mathfrak S_k\) and \(Y_k\) for the based invertible part of the joined hom at weight \(k\). Use the raw comparison \(f_k:U_k\to Y_k\) at grouped poles. A class in \(\pi_j U_k\) represents a difference at a written old type of degree \(n+j+1\). Its two faces admit a joined filler exactly when its image is zero. For \(j\ge2\) we may compute the source group on its ordered cover. [Raw configuration hom and fixed-boundary comparison](#researcher-response-176)

The centre and distance of two particles give contractible factors. Their unoriented direction identifies \(U_2\simeq\mathbb {RP}^{n-1}\), and the ordered cover records the unit vector. Moving the pair through half a turn in a plane represents the generator of \(\pi_1U_2\). The suspended diagonal exchange represents this class because it switches the two names and \(F_2\) is simply connected. Its joined filler contracts the restriction of \(f_2\) to the projective line. [Joined exchange at the written faces](#researcher-response-4)

For \(n=3\) extend this based nullhomotopy using the CW cofibration \(\mathbb {RP}^1\subset\mathbb {RP}^2\). The resulting map factors through \(\mathbb {RP}^2/\mathbb {RP}^1=S^2\). Precomposing the quotient with the ordered cover gives a self-map of \(S^2\) of degree zero, since the map on integral \(H_2\) factors through \(H_2(\mathbb {RP}^2)=0\). Degree classifies based self-maps of this sphere. Thus the **primitive** ordered meridian already has a joined filler in degree six. This proves more than the order-two bound one gets from the action of a transposition on its orientation. In general odd \(n\), that action does give \(2\mu=0\) for the surface value \(\mu\) of an oriented meridian, since the exchange acts trivially after comparison and the antipodal map has degree \((-1)^n\).

### Reducing every weight to a placed pair

Every adjacent transposition of \(k\) identical particles has a raw representative supported on its pair, obtained by placing the two-copy exchange beside the other stationary occurrences. Placement acts on the joined filler as well. These transpositions generate \(\pi_1U_k=\mathfrak S_k\), so \((f_k)_*\pi_1 U_k=0\). In particular, any two oriented meridians at specified ordered pairs give the same based class in \(Y_k\) when the orders are carried to each other. To see this, permute the names and transport back to the base configuration. The only path ambiguity downstairs is a permutation loop, and each such loop acts trivially after comparison. Upstairs \(F_k\) is simply connected. The orientation convention uses the vector from the first selected name to the second. Denote this common based map by \(\mu_k:S^{n-1}\to Y_k\), up to homotopy.

For every \(k\ge2,\ j\ge2\), the image of the **entire** comparison is
\[
             (f_k)_*\pi_j U_k=(\mu_k)_*\pi_j S^{n-1}.
\]
Indeed the last-point fibration has fibre a wedge of \(k-1\) meridian spheres and admits a section up to homotopy by placing the old configuration in a ball and parking a new point outside. Forgetting that point is homotopic to the identity on the old configuration space after this placement. Iteration splits the abelian source group into contributions from these wedges with stationary spectators. At the final weight, the based restriction of the comparison to each wedge is homotopic to its fold followed by \(\mu_k\), by the preceding equality on its based summands. This proves inclusion in the right side. The reverse inclusion is realized by one placed pair. The argument also works at weight two, where there is just one sphere. [Fadell–Neuwirth fibration](https://doi.org/10.7146/math.scand.a-10517)

For \(n=3\), \(\mu_k\) is null at every weight by placement of the primitive two-particle filler. Together with the permutation calculation this proves the assertion for all \(j\ge1\). It concerns fillers at old boundaries and requires no contraction of the entire map \(U_k\to Y_k\). For odd \(n\) and \(k\ge4\) one also has the uniform integral bound **two** on the exponent of the whole image, in every degree \(j\ge2\). Move two disjoint pairs independently in disjoint balls. This gives a map \(h:S^{n-1}\times S^{n-1}\to Y_k\) with both axis restrictions representing \(\mu_k\). The diagonal represents \((1,1)\) in the bottom homotopy group of the product, so its composite with \(h\) represents \(2\mu_k=0\). Precompose with any \(\beta:S^j\to S^{n-1}\). Its diagonal has coordinates \((\beta,\beta)\), whose image is \(2(\mu_k)_*\beta\). This avoids any distributivity assumption about unstable precomposition.

Now fix \(n\) and \(j\ge2\). A failure at any weight requires \(\pi_j F_3\ne0\). Indeed the forgetful splitting and Hilton's basic products put each possible summand in some \(\pi_j S^{1+\ell(n-2)}\). The last-point fibre of \(F_3\) has two letters, with a basic product of every positive length, and its homotopy group injects. Conversely, suppose \(\pi_j F_3\ne0\). If \(\pi_j S^{n-1}=0\), the image formula kills the entire group. Otherwise take a nonzero \(\beta\) on that sphere and subtract its placements on the ordered pairs \((1,2)\) and \((1,3)\). Forgetting point three recovers \(\beta\) from this difference, whereas the two joined images coincide. Thus **weight three fails in that very degree**. The permutation degree \(n+2\) already fails at weight two. In rank three, for each \(j\ge2\), the least failing weight is two if \(\pi_j S^2\ne0\) and three otherwise, since the two-letter wedge then contains a sphere summand in degree \(j\) of its homotopy decomposition. [Hilton's decomposition by basic products](https://doi.org/10.1112/jlms/s1-30.2.154)

Consequently at a positive raw 3-program \(b:1_{1_x}\to1_{1_x}\) in any finite ordinary 3-computad, the joined kernel contains the whole group of old motions of \(k\) copies of \(b\), at that same weight. Substitution of \(b\) carries every filler just proved. For \(j\ge2\), naming the occurrences and retaining one fixed generating event per copy gives a left inverse to the cabling on raw homotopy groups. On \(\pi_1\) a nonidentity permutation of copies exchanges nonempty blocks of events and still has nonidentity occurrence permutation. Thus precisely the nonzero differences in this family give new inhabitants. In any finite extension lacking a generator of the tested degree, raw support strengthening at these faces gives the same non-inhabitation. [Event selection at empty ends](#testing-the-empty-ends-and-surviving-higher-declarations)

### What the meridian controls for each individual binary surface

Fix one of the four surfaces and define \(d\ge0\) by \(d\mathbb Z=\ker(\pi_{n-1}F_2\to\pi_{n-1}Y)\) at a pair of distinct scalar names, with \(Y\) now its own surface hom. Thus \(d=0\) means that the image has infinite order. For \(j\ge2\), in any pure scalar weight and colouring, consider the image of the comparison on \(\pi_j\) localized at a prime \(p\). **Some such image is nonzero exactly when \(d=0\) or \(p\mid d\).** If \(0<d<\infty\), every integral image in each fixed degree is finite with exponent bounded independently of weight and colours.

Here the meridians can have distinct surface values. Each is nevertheless obtained by placing the named pair among stationary occurrences, fitting its basepoint along a path and assigning its two colours by substitution. Hence \(d\) kills each of these bottom classes if \(d>0\). In a last-point wedge any basic Whitehead product of length \(\ell\) maps to a class \(w\) killed by \(d\), by bilinearity in any one input (including repeated letters by treating their slots separately). Put \(N=1+\ell(n-2)\). A nullhomotopy of \(dw\) extends \(w:S^N\to Y\) over the Moore space \(M=S^N\cup_d e^{N+1}\). The image of the associated Hilton summand on \(\pi_j\) therefore factors through \(\pi_j M\). This Moore space is simply connected and its only nonzero reduced integral homology is \(\mathbb Z/d\). Serre's theorem modulo the class of finite groups supported on the primes dividing \(d\) puts each \(\pi_j M\) in that class. For \(d=1\) the Moore space is contractible. For fixed \(j\), the least common multiple of these exponents for \(N\le j\) bounds every image, by the split fibre calculation; each finite weight uses finitely many summands. Covers for the possible repeated colours induce isomorphisms on the raw higher groups, and folding transports the placed fillers. Conversely, if \(p\mid d\) or \(d=0\), the original two-name image itself stays nonzero on localization, by flatness. [Serre, *Groupes d'homotopie et classes de groupes abéliens*](https://www.sas.rochester.edu/mth/sites/doug-ravenel/otherpapers/Serre-Classes.pdf)

In rank three this gives another criterion for the three-strand part of Q3(b) in Response 168. It suffices to detect a nonzero localized comparison image at infinitely many primes, allowing the higher degree and the pure scalar weight to depend on the prime. Conversely, reflection there detects the primitive pair rationally and at every prime: the two-name and repeated-name filling tests agree by occurrence lifting. The argument determines the effect of a finite-order meridian but leaves its order on each individual surface open. [Three-strand reduction and naming at the stationary pair](#testing-the-abelian-part-with-actual-substitutions)

**Validation.** Run `python3 -B tools/semistrict_surface_projective_comparison.py --checkout CHECKOUT` with the release build of Rice's checker used in Response 4. It types the raw exchange and its identity competitor at the same boundary in ranks three through six, and checks the exchange-to-swap conversion with strict units. The topological check pushes the oriented boundary of a cross-polytope to the antipodal quotient and reads each coefficient relative to one hemisphere. The resulting degrees in ranks three through nine are \(0,2,0,2,0,2,0\), including cancellation on every triangle of the rank-three cover. The joined square equation and the all-weight implications use the proofs above. [Projective cover and exchange checker](../../../tools/semistrict_surface_projective_comparison.py)

## Researcher Response 181

**At stationary rank two, let \(m\equiv1\pmod4\), \(m\ge5\), and let the reversible local type be a threefold loop-space type. If the bottom group \(A\) has no even torsion, the exact raw obstruction group is the image of the stable Hopf map \(\eta:A/2A\to\pi_{m-1}K\).** Vanishing of this action proves published reflection at all written boundaries of old degree \(2m+1\). With arbitrary bottom torsion the same exact calculation holds if no nonzero element in the image of \(\eta\) is divisible by two. Throughout this latter class **one finite comparison tests published insertion**. Its local type has precisely two nonzero homotopy groups, both of order two. Thus at degree 11 the loop-space and Hopf-action hypotheses give a single finite test where arbitrary reversible labels require unbounded targets.

### An upper bound from the complex frame bundle

Put \(d=m-2\), \(G=\pi_{d+1}K\), \(A=\pi_dK\). Use Response 153's connectivity and reversibility assumptions through \(i=2m-2\). For a local type coming from a connected threefold loop space, perform the following calculation on that space before passing to the local \(i\)-type. Its abelian fundamental group and vanishing lower homology give \((d-1)\)-connectedness, so \(A=H_dK\). The map denoted by \(\eta\) takes \(x:S^d\to K\) to its composite with the Hopf generator of \(\pi_{d+1}S^d=C_2\); it is additive in this stable range. Write \(q(x)=[\Sigma^2 x,\Sigma^2 x]\).

If \(x\eta=0\), then \(q(x)=0\). In fact the finite complex two-frame bundle of [Response 174](#researcher-response-174) is obtained from the bottom sphere by attaching one \((d+2)\)-cell and one \((2d+2)\)-cell. The first attaching map belongs to \(\{0,\eta\}\), so \(x\) extends over the first cell. The second attaching map \(g\) has \(\Sigma^2g\) a Whitehead square by [Response 175](#realizing-and-testing-arbitrary-binary-relations); hence \(\Sigma^3g=0\). Every map of the intermediate skeleton into a threefold loop space extends over this disk, by adjunction. The fibre class has square zero on the whole bundle. Naturality proves the assertion. In particular \(q\) factors through \(\eta A\), without any restriction on torsion.

### Two-stage targets detecting the remaining classes

Write \(C_s=\mathbb Z/2^s\) in this response and \(j_s:\mathbb F_2\hookrightarrow C_s\) for its subgroup of order two. Let \(D_s\) be the \((d-1)\)-connected cover of \(\Omega^\infty\Sigma^{d+1}J_s\), with \(J_s\) from Response 178. It is an infinite loop space with bottom group \(\mathbb F_2\) and group \(C_s\) in degree \(d+1\). All higher groups vanish by the multiplication exact sequence and the vanishing of negative sphere stems. Its bottom projection \(u:D_s\to K(\mathbb F_2,d)\) satisfies
\[
                         (j_s)_* Sq^2u=0.
\]
To see this, use the corresponding two-stage connective spectra. At \(s=1\), the stable Postnikov invariant is a degree-two mod-two cohomology operation, so it is zero or \(Sq^2\). The Hopf action between the two homotopy groups is nonzero: under \(J_1\to I\) the bottom character of \(\pi_1^S\) evaluates on \(\eta\) to \(1/2\), and the top group injects into \(\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\). A split Postnikov spectrum would have zero action. Thus the invariant is \(Sq^2\). The transition from stage one to stage \(s\) induces the identity on the bottom group and \(j_s\) on the next group. Naturality gives the claimed invariant and its null pullback. [Brown–Comenetz evaluation](https://rezk.web.illinois.edu/mahowald-rezk-bc-dual-final.pdf) · [Hill–Hopkins–Ravenel, the admissible basis of stable mod-two operations](https://www.sas.rochester.edu/mth/sites/doug-ravenel/mypapers/CDMpaper.pdf)

Every homomorphism \(\chi:G/2^sG\to\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\) gives a map \(K\to D_s\) whose bottom character is \(c=\chi\eta\), identifying \(\{0,1/2\}\) with \(\mathbb F_2\). Indeed Freudenthal identifies \(G\) with the corresponding group of the reduced suspension spectrum of \(K\), since \(d\ge3\). Smash that spectrum with the cofiber of multiplication by \(2^s\) on the sphere. Its group in degree \(d+1\) contains \(G/2^sG\) by the cofiber sequence. Extend \(\chi\) to that group using divisibility of \(\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\). Brown–Comenetz representability and smash/function adjunction give the required map into the shifted \(J_s\), since dualizing the Moore cofiber gives the multiplication fibre. The character on \(\eta x\) is exactly the bottom reading by naturality. Connectivity gives the lift to the connected cover.

Suppose in addition that \(c\) lifts to a \(C_s\)-valued homomorphism on \(A\), hence to a cohomology class \(\tilde c\) by universal coefficients. The inclusion of coefficients sends \(c\smile Sq^2c\) to \(\tilde c\smile (j_s)_*Sq^2c=0\), because multiplication in \(C_s\) on its subgroup of order two uses the reduction modulo two of the other factor. Evaluation on any stable sphere commutes with this inclusion, which is injective on coefficient values. Thus \(c\smile Sq^2c\) reads zero on the stable spherical image, and [Response 175](#researcher-response-175) says exactly that \(c\) annihilates every raw square relation.

These tests give both exact cases in the opening claim. If \(\eta x\ne0\) and \(A\) has no even torsion, choose a cyclic primary factor of the finitely generated \(G\) detecting \(\eta x\). Its character factors through \(G/2^sG\) for a finite \(s\), and every bottom binary character lifts integrally here. Thus \(q(x)\ne0\). If instead \(\eta A\cap2G=0\), use \(s=1\) and separate already in \(G/2G\). The coefficient lift is automatic. More generally the remaining ambiguity for mixed torsion is bounded by the joint annihilator of all the liftable characters just constructed. For instance, if \(A=\mathbb Z\), \(G=\mathbb Z/4\), and \(\eta x=2\), the square survives. This action is realizable on the free threefold loop space on \((S^d\vee S^{d+1})\cup_{\eta+2\iota_{d+1}} e^{d+2}\): in the relevant stable stem the attachment quotients \((\mathbb Z/2)\oplus\mathbb Z\) by \((1,2)\). Freudenthal identifies this group and the bottom class after taking the free threefold loop space.

For the promised one-comparison test use the bottom square of \(D_1\). It is nonzero because \(Sq^2u=0\) and \(u\) reads one on the generator. Its finite local presentation through \(i\) exists by the Postnikov realization in [Response 178](#researcher-response-178). If a published failure occurs with \(\eta A\cap2G=0\), take its one-puncture nonzero square. The separating character at \(s=1\) gives an actual map of local types carrying that square to the specified one, so substitution carries the filler. Conversely \(D_1\) itself satisfies the hypotheses (its Hopf action is an isomorphism). This proves equivalence with nonfilling there. The published status of that comparison remains open.

**Reproduce.** Run `python3 -B tools/semistrict_surface_loop_eta.py`. The solver uses cyclic decompositions of \(A,G\) and the images of bottom generators under \(\eta\). At level \(s\), factors of \(G\) with 2-primary order at most \(2^s\) provide the character readings. Linear elimination imposes vanishing on finite bottom coordinates of smaller 2-primary order, exactly the condition for a coefficient lift. The solver combines these spaces and compares their dimension with \(\operatorname{rank}(\eta)\). It verified 1,156 shell bounds against the cyclic groups and their doubles, and 576 mixed-bottom cases by enumerating the two coefficient homomorphisms independently. With `--orders 4 --bottom-orders 0 --column 2 --shell 1` the exact dimension is one; with bottom order two the same Hopf image leaves this test undetermined. [Loop-label Hopf-action solver](../../../tools/semistrict_surface_loop_eta.py)

## Researcher Response 182

**At stationary rank two and old degrees \(11,19,27,\ldots\), the first unstable raw square group of every reversible threefold loop-space label is determined by its first two homotopy groups and the Hopf action between them, including all mixed torsion.** Published reflection throughout this family is equivalent to nonfilling at **one finite comparison for each positive 2-primary exponent index** of the second group. The testers have just two nonzero local homotopy groups. No local map between distinct testers carries one specified square to the other. For example, when the bottom group is \(\mathbb Z/2\), the next group is \(\mathbb Z/4\), and the Hopf action carries the generator to two, published insertion reflects at every written boundary in the tested degree. With infinite cyclic bottom and the same Hopf image the square survives.

Use \(d=m-2=3,7,11,\ldots\), \(N=2d+2\), \(A=\pi_dK=H_dK\), \(G=\pi_{d+1}K\) and \(h=\eta:A/2A\to G[2]\) as in [Response 181](#researcher-response-181). For \(r\ge1\) let \(F_r\subseteq A/2A\) be the image of the elements killed by \(2^r\); put \(F_0=0\). The exact square group is
\[
 (A/2A)\Big/\left(\ker h+\sum_{r\ge1}\big(F_r\cap h^{-1}(2^rG)\big)\right).
\]
It suffices to use the distinct positive 2-exponent indices of the finite cyclic bottom factors in the sum. In particular, in a two-stage type with cyclic bottom \(\mathbb Z/2^r\), next group \(\mathbb Z/2^s\), and nonzero Hopf action, the bottom square vanishes **if and only if \(r<s\)**. The calculation also applies to higher local Postnikov types of threefold loop spaces with exactly these two low groups. The map-of-types and one-puncture conclusions use the connectivity and reversibility assumptions of Response 153.

### Framed labels realizing the torsion relations

Write \(a=2^r\). Start with the complex two-frame bundle \(E\) of [Responses 174](#researcher-response-174) and [175](#researcher-response-175), a closed stably framed \(N\)-manifold with a bottom \(d\)-sphere generating \(H_dE=\mathbb Z\). Its bottom mod-two character \(c\) has \(\langle c Sq^2 c,[E]_2\rangle=1\): the bottom square vanishes there, so the stable spherical characteristic number in Response 175 is nonzero, and top mod-two homology is one-dimensional.

Perform framed surgery on an embedded representative of \(a\) times the bottom sphere. General position permits the embedding because \(2d<N\). Its normal bundle is stably trivial and has rank \(d+2\), so a normal framing compatible with the stable framing of the trace exists: stabilization on \(\pi_d SO(d+2)\) is surjective and on \(\pi_{d-1}\) is injective. The trace from \(E\) adds a \((d+1)\)-handle. The character into \(K(\mathbb F_2,d)\) extends because its reading on the attaching sphere is even. Denote the new framed boundary by \(M\). The characteristic number remains one by bordism over this Eilenberg–MacLane space. [Milnor, *A procedure for killing homotopy groups of differentiable manifolds*](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/milnorsurg.pdf)

Here \(M\) is \((d-1)\)-connected, with \(H_dM=\mathbb Z/a\). Indeed the trace as seen from \(M\) adds its dual \((d+2)\)-handle. Poincaré duality gives \(H_{d+2}M=H^dM=0\) and middle torsion \(\operatorname{Tor}H_{d+1}M=\mathbb Z/a\). Surgery changes Euler characteristic from zero to two, since \(d\) is odd. Duality and connectivity then give zero free middle rank and no other reduced homology below the fundamental class. The framed fundamental class is stably spherical. The nonzero characteristic number therefore gives the sole bottom generator as a relation in Response 175. Its square vanishes in \(\Sigma^2M\).

The lower cells of \(M\) explain why the construction works for an arbitrary threefold loop target. Map \(L=S^d\cup_a e^{d+1}\) into \(M\) on a bottom generator \(z\). This induces an isomorphism on \(\pi_d\). Relative Hurewicz for its mapping-cylinder pair identifies \(\pi_{d+1}(M,L)\) with \(H_{d+1}(M,L)=\mathbb Z/a\). Choose \(y\in\pi_{d+1}M\) lifting a generator. Then \(ay\) comes from \(\pi_{d+1}L\), which is generated by \(z\eta\) of order at most two by the stable cofibration and Freudenthal. Thus there is a map
\[
 W=(L\vee S^{d+1})\cup_{\epsilon z\eta+a\iota_{d+1}} e^{d+2}\longrightarrow M
 \qquad (\epsilon\in\{0,1\})
\]
inducing isomorphisms on integral homology below \(N\). The coefficient \(a\) on the upper sphere gives exactly the required middle group and zero \(H_{d+2}W\). The simply connected pair is consequently \((N-1)\)-connected by relative Hurewicz, with relative \(\pi_N=\mathbb Z\). Attaching its generator gives a homology equivalence \(W\cup_\alpha e^N\simeq M\). The stable fundamental class splits the top disk off stably, so \(\alpha\) is stably null. In fact \(\Sigma^3\alpha=0\): it lies in degree \(2d+4\) in a \((d+2)\)-connected target, already in the Freudenthal isomorphism range.

Now suppose \(x\in A\) is killed by \(a\) and \(hx\in aG\). Map \(L\) into \(K\) on \(x\), and select an upper-sphere value solving \(ay'=-\epsilon hx\). This extends over the displayed lower skeleton. Threefold loop adjunction extends it over the top disk since \(\Sigma^3\alpha=0\). It sends the bottom square known to vanish on \(M\) to the square on \(x\). This proves every torsion relation in the formula, irrespective of the choice of \(\epsilon\). The relations from \(\ker h\) are those of Response 181.

### Separation, finite tests and their exponents

Let \(I=h(A/2A)\). Set \(U_r=h(F_r)\), \(V_s=I\cap 2^sG\). After factoring out \(\ker h\), the relations proved geometrically span \(\sum_r(U_r\cap V_r)\). A level-\(s\) character in Response 181 is an arbitrary linear functional on \(I\) vanishing on \(V_s+U_{s-1}\). Indeed vanishing on \(V_s\) allows extension to a character of \(G/2^sG\) using the injectivity of \(\mathbb Q/\mathbb Z\); vanishing on \(U_{s-1}\) is exactly the condition that the induced bottom character lift to coefficients \(\mathbb Z/2^s\), by cyclic decomposition. Its cup-product calculation proves all these characters kill every raw relation.

The common annihilator is exactly the geometric sum. Every \(U_r\cap V_r\) lies in all \(U_{s-1}+V_s\) by monotonicity. Conversely take a vector lying in all those sums. At levels above the 2-primary exponent of \(G\), \(V_s=0\), so it lies in some \(U_r\). Using membership in \(U_{r-1}+V_r\), subtract an element of \(U_r\cap V_r\) to land in \(U_{r-1}\). The subtracted vector belongs to the common annihilator, so descend to \(U_0=0\). For the character tests themselves it suffices to stop at the exponent index of \(G\) (later levels only tighten the bottom lift constraint). This proves exactness, including cases in which a sum of bottom generators becomes a relation even though each individual square survives.

At each \(s\ge1\) use the homotopy pullback of \(D_s\to K(\mathbb F_2,d)\) from Response 181 along reduction \(K(\mathbb Z/2^s,d)\to K(\mathbb F_2,d)\). It is an infinite loop space with bottom and next group both \(\mathbb Z/2^s\). The bottom generator maps to one in \(D_s\); its Hopf image is \(2^{s-1}\) in the next group by naturality. Its square survives by the formula. Take a finite presentation of its local \(i\)-type as in Response 178 and compare that square with zero. If a published failure occurs, choose a separating level and character as above. The map to \(D_s\) and its lifted bottom cohomology character give a local map to the pullback. It reads an odd multiple of the tester's generator, hence carries the proposed filler to the specified square. Conversely the tester is itself a member of the family. Thus on labels whose \(G\) has 2-primary exponent dividing \(2^e\), nonfilling in tests \(1,\ldots,e\) is necessary and sufficient. An empty list gives reflection. The published filling judgments on these nonzero tests remain open.

For a map between two testers carrying the distinguished square to the distinguished square, the bottom homomorphism must carry a generator to an odd multiple of a generator. This requires source exponent index at least target index. A strictly larger source index would kill the source Hopf image in the target's next group, contrary to naturality of \(\eta\). Thus the indices must agree. More generally no finite list of finite threefold loop-space local types detects all these squares by maps: take the index larger than the 2-exponent indices of all their next groups. The image of the bottom generator then has zero Hopf action, hence zero square by Response 181. This does not require any independence assumption on the published judgments.

**Reproduce.** Run `python3 -B tools/semistrict_surface_loop_eta.py`. With bottom orders supplied the solver now computes both the full surgery relation space and its dual character space independently and checks orthogonality and complementary dimensions. The audit checks 56 cyclic exponent pairs, the coefficient coboundaries and 576 mixed-bottom cases against explicit homomorphisms. With `--orders 4 --bottom-orders 2 --column 2 --shell 1` it gives exact dimension zero. With `--orders 2 4 --bottom-orders 2 2 --column 1 0 --column 1 2 --shell 1 1` it gives dimension one with zero chosen square; both coordinate squares survive. The framed manifolds and their attaching-map extension are proved above. [Mixed-torsion square solver](../../../tools/semistrict_surface_loop_eta.py)

## Researcher Response 183

**For a fixed pair of low homotopy groups and Hopf action, published reflection on every threefold loop-space label with those data is equivalent to checking just the cyclic factors that actually occur in its two-stage Postnikov type.** On that type itself the factors determine the published answer for each named shell, including sums. This applies at stationary rank two in old degrees \(11,19,27,\ldots\), with the connectivity and reversibility of [Response 182](#researcher-response-182). A surviving cyclic factor is indexed by an interval \([s,r]\), with \(r=\infty\) allowed. A map between two such factors takes the specified square to the specified square **exactly when the target interval is contained in the source interval**. This describes which published decisions propagate, while the filling judgments on the individual intervals remain open.

### Which changes of basis give actual local substitutions?

Put \(d=m-2\ge3\), \(A=\pi_dK\), \(G=\pi_{d+1}K\), and \(h:A/2A\to G[2]\) for the Hopf action. A two-stage type here means a \((d-1)\)-connected space with no homotopy above degree \(d+1\), used through the relevant local \(i\)-type. Its Postnikov invariant is precisely \(h\). To check this, present \(A\) by a wedge \(M\) of bottom spheres and cyclic Moore spaces in degrees \(d,d+1\). Map it to \(X=K(A,d)\) by the specified generators. The pair is \((d+1)\)-connected and \(\pi_{d+2}(X,M)=\pi_{d+1}M=A/2A\) by Freudenthal and the Moore cofibrations. Relative Hurewicz and the integral homology sequence give \(H_{d+2}X=A/2A\) and \(H_{d+1}X=0\). Thus \(H^{d+2}(X;G)=\operatorname{Hom}(A/2A,G)\). On the relative disk killing \(x\eta\) the obstruction to lifting from the base is the value of \(x\eta\) upstairs. A lift over \(M\) exists because the chosen bottom elements satisfy the specified cyclic orders. This identifies the class with \(h\). Consequently homomorphisms of the two groups are induced by a map of types if they commute with \(h\): the corresponding Postnikov classes agree, giving a homotopy of the maps defining the fibres. Block direct sums of these data give products of types. All these types are themselves infinite loop-space types by Freudenthal, comparing to the \((d+1)\)-truncation of the suspension spectrum. [Baues and Frankland, two-stage homotopy operations and the stable range](https://arxiv.org/abs/1208.2184)

Split off the odd-primary summands. Order the remaining bottom cyclic generators by their 2-exponent index \(r\), placing free generators last at infinity. Order the finite 2-primary factors of \(G\) by increasing exponent index \(s\), and use their order-two elements as a basis of \(G[2]\). The resulting binary matrix of \(h\) reduces to at most one pivot per row and column by actual group automorphisms. Process the bottom columns in order. Take the first unused nonzero row of the current column, add that row to clear the entries below it, then add this column to clear its pivot from later columns. On \(G\) the row addition from exponent \(s\) to \(t\ge s\) adds \(2^{t-s}\) times the target generator to the source generator, so it adds the required order-two coordinates. On \(A\) one may add a generator of smaller or equal order to one of larger order, including a free generator. Each shear is invertible. These operations preserve earlier pivots. The pivot counts for tied orders are intrinsic since the ranks on the first row and column blocks count precisely the pivots in those blocks.

Write \(P_{r,s}\) for the factor of a pivot, with bottom group \(\mathbb Z/2^r\) (or \(\mathbb Z\) at infinity), next group \(\mathbb Z/2^s\), and nonzero Hopf action. Unpaired generators contribute Eilenberg–MacLane factors. This constructs a product decomposition at the level of local types, including projection and inclusion maps. The raw square group of each pivot is binary when \(s\le r\) and zero otherwise by Response 182. The unpaired factors have zero square group. Thus each surviving pivot has exactly one raw test, the square on its generator. Its local type has a finite-type CW model, including for a free bottom group, so the finite local presentation and written-face substitutions of Responses 158 and 178 apply.

### The published subgroup and the interval order

For a two-stage label the surface-null subgroup is the direct sum of the pivot coordinates whose own tests fill. A filler for a shell transports by projection to a filler at **each** nonzero coordinate. Conversely include the individual fillers and add their comparisons at the puncture, using additivity from [Response 158](#researcher-response-158). A linear combination in the original basis must be carried through the inverse column changes to use this rule. On an arbitrary threefold loop-space label the projection to its two-stage section is an isomorphism on raw square groups by Response 182. A published failure anywhere with the prescribed low data therefore gives a published failure on some pivot of that section. Conversely the two-stage section itself is a label with those data, and a filling pivot gives failure there by inclusion. This proves the assertion for *all labels with the specified data* without requiring a map from the section back into a particular higher Postnikov extension.

For a map from \(P_{r,s}\) to \(P_{u,t}\) between surviving factors, the bottom generator must map to an odd multiple of the target generator to retain the square. Hence \(u\le r\), including the free cases. Commuting with the Hopf action requires the order-two element in the source's next group to map to the nonzero one in the target, forcing \(s\le t\). These conditions suffice: send the bottom generator to the bottom generator and the next generator to \(2^{t-s}\) times the next generator. This commutes with \(h\) and hence gives the required local map. The two inequalities are exactly \([t,u]\subseteq[s,r]\). The diagonal factors \([s,s]\) recover Response 182's global tests. A filled interval forces every subinterval to fill; a nonfilling subinterval excludes filling on every containing interval.

These implications exhaust the constraints from addition and maps **within the two-stage family**. Given any set of intervals closed under taking subintervals, assign to each product the span of its coordinates in that set. For any map between products, project to a target factor and restrict to each source inclusion. A nonzero coordinate image between surviving factors requires interval containment; additivity gives preservation of the assigned subgroup. Applying this to isomorphisms in both directions gives independence of the chosen decomposition. In particular, decisions on diagonal tests can settle global reflection without determining the answer for an individual interval above them. For example, within the exponent indices one through four, there are 42 patterns compatible with this substitution rule. Realization of arbitrary patterns by the published syntax is a separate question.

**Reproduce.** Run `python3 -B tools/semistrict_surface_interval_squares.py`. The solver checks 4,096 named shells in three-column matrices against the raw quotient and direct character detection at each diagonal tester. It compares the interval criterion with enumeration of commuting cyclic homomorphisms on 100 ordered pairs and enumerates the 42 closed patterns. With `--bottom-orders 4 8 0 --orders 2 4 8 --column 1 2 0 --column 1 0 4 --column 0 2 0 --shell 1 0 1`, the two named generators in the sum have combined coordinates on **three** tests, \([1,2],[2,3],[3,\infty]\). Use `--fills S R` or `--nonfills S R` to infer the consequences of supplied judgments; an upper endpoint of zero denotes infinity. Without supplied judgments this example is open. [Cyclic factor and published-substitution solver](../../../tools/semistrict_surface_interval_squares.py)
